etymology_story.zh: 英语 toucan 经法语 toucan、葡萄牙语 tucano，最终借自南美洲图皮语的鸟名。它进入英语后保留了原有的鸟类指称，并不是由英语 two 与 can 拼成的词。[来源：Dictionary.com](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/toucan)
etymology_story.en: English toucan came through French toucan and Portuguese tucano from a Tupi bird name in South America. It retained its reference to the bird and is not an English compound of two and can. [Source: Dictionary.com](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/toucan)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中把 toucan 作为完整借词记忆。词族：toucan + -s → toucans（巨嘴鸟的复数）；toucan + 指小后缀 -et → toucanet（小型巨嘴鸟类）；toucanet + -s → toucanets（其复数）。toucanet 是若干小型巨嘴鸟的名称，不专指幼鸟。[派生形式来源：Dictionary.com](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/toucanet) 分级说明：CEFR-C2 为建议学习等级，并非官方逐词认证。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat toucan as a complete loanword in modern English. Word family: toucan + -s → toucans; toucan + diminutive -et → toucanet, a name for certain smaller toucans; toucanet + -s → toucanets. A toucanet is not simply a baby toucan. [Derivative source: Dictionary.com](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/toucanet) Classification note: CEFR-C2 is a suggested learning level, not an official word-level certification.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有常用的严格同义词。toucanet（小巨嘴鸟）和 aracari（簇舌巨嘴鸟）指巨嘴鸟科中的特定类群，范围更窄；hornbill（犀鸟）虽也有大喙，却属于另一类鸟，不能作为 toucan 的同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym. Toucanet and aracari name particular groups within the toucan family and are narrower terms; hornbill describes a different group of large-billed birds and is not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Attach the whole borrowed name to one striking image: a huge colorful bill on a tropical branch.

senses.meaning_zh: 乡巴佬；被轻蔑地认为土气、缺乏见识的乡下人
senses.meaning_en: A country person regarded as unsophisticated, used insultingly.
senses.english_definition: If someone calls a person a yokel, they are insulting them by suggesting that they come from the countryside and lack knowledge or social experience.
senses.collocation_en: a local yokel; a country yokel
senses.collocation_zh: 当地的乡巴佬；乡下土包子
senses.sentence_en: The visitors dismissed him as a local yokel, although he knew far more about the area than they did.
senses.sentence_zh: 游客们轻蔑地把他当作当地的乡巴佬，尽管他对这一带的了解远远超过他们。

etymology_story.zh: yokel 在19世纪初已见于英语，用作对乡下人的轻蔑称呼，其更早来源尚不确定。这个词把乡村出身与缺乏见识联系起来，因此带有明显的贬义。
etymology_story.en: Yokel is recorded in English from the early nineteenth century as a contemptuous name for a country person, but its earlier origin is uncertain. Its meaning associates rural origins with a supposed lack of sophistication.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中整体分析为 yokel，不宜强拆词根词缀。复数：yokels；派生词包括 yokelish（乡巴佬似的）、yokelism（乡巴佬的言行或习气）和 yokeldom（乡巴佬群体或乡土社会），这些派生词均较少见。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, yokel is an unanalysed base rather than a transparent combination of root and affixes. Its plural is yokels; uncommon derivatives include yokelish, meaning characteristic of a yokel, yokelism, meaning a yokel's behaviour or mannerism, and yokeldom, meaning yokels collectively or their social world.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bumpkin（乡巴佬）同样突出土气和缺乏世故；hick（土包子）尤常见于美式口语，贬义明显；rustic（乡下人）较有文学色彩，可只强调乡村生活背景，侮辱性通常较弱。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bumpkin similarly emphasizes rural unsophistication; hick is especially associated with informal American English and is clearly derogatory; rustic is more literary and can simply identify someone with country life, making it less insulting.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住一个带偏见的称呼：“把乡下人说成没见识的人”。这是语义锚点，不是词源拆解。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the prejudiced label: a country person dismissed as unsophisticated. This is a meaning-based hook, not an etymological breakdown.

senses.meaning_zh: 闭经；月经不来
senses.meaning_en: The absence of menstrual periods.
senses.english_definition: Amenorrhoea is a condition in which a person who would normally be expected to menstruate does not have menstrual periods.
senses.collocation_en: primary amenorrhoea; secondary amenorrhoea
senses.collocation_zh: 原发性闭经；继发性闭经
senses.sentence_en: The study examined possible causes of secondary amenorrhoea in athletes.
senses.sentence_zh: 这项研究考察了运动员发生继发性闭经的可能原因。

etymology_story.zh: 这个医学名称由希腊语来源的 a-（无）、mēn（月）及表示流动的成分构成，经医学拉丁语形式进入英语。字面上的“没有每月的流出”对应月经缺如这一含义。
etymology_story.en: This medical term was formed from Greek-derived elements meaning absence, month, and flow, and entered English through medical Latin terminology. Its literal idea of no monthly flow corresponds to the absence of menstruation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 医学构词：a-（无）+ men/o（月经；源义为月）+ -rrhoea（流出）→ amenorrhoea。美式拼写为 amenorrhea；相关形容词包括 amenorrhoeic、amenorrheic（闭经的），以及较少见的 amenorrhoeal、amenorrheal；同一构词系统还有 menorrhoea（月经流出）和 dysmenorrhoea／dysmenorrhea（痛经）。
morphology_enriched.en: Medical formation: a- (absence) + men/o (menstruation, originally month) + -rrhoea (flow) → amenorrhoea. The American spelling is amenorrhea; related adjectives include amenorrhoeic and amenorrheic, with the less common alternatives amenorrhoeal and amenorrheal. Related medical formations include menorrhoea, meaning menstrual flow, and dysmenorrhoea/dysmenorrhea, meaning painful menstruation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: amenorrhea 是同一术语的美式拼写，意义完全相同；absence of menstruation（月经缺如）是直白的释义表达；a missed period（一次月经未来）指单次现象，不能在所有语境中等同于闭经这一医学术语。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Amenorrhea is the American spelling of exactly the same term; absence of menstruation is a plain descriptive equivalent; a missed period describes an individual occurrence and is not interchangeable with the medical term in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: a- 无 + men/o 月经 + -rrhoea 流出：没有月经流出。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Absence + menstruation + flow: menstrual flow is absent.

etymology_story.zh: balsa 借自西班牙语 balsa，意为“木筏”，后来用于指制作木筏的轻质木材及其树种。西班牙语这个词的更早来源尚不确定。
etymology_story.en: Balsa was borrowed from Spanish balsa, meaning a raft, and came to name the lightweight timber used for rafts and the tree producing it. The earlier origin of the Spanish word is uncertain.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 balsa 是整体借词，没有可透明拆分的英语词缀。表示木材时通常不可数，表示树木时可数，复数为 balsas；常见复合表达为 balsa wood，也写作 balsawood；另有 balsa tree 和 balsa-wood model 等组合。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, balsa is a borrowed base with no transparent English affixes. It is normally uncountable when referring to timber and countable when referring to trees, with the plural balsas. Common compounds and combinations include balsa wood, also written balsawood, balsa tree, and balsa-wood model.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: balsa wood 和 balsawood 都明确指轻木木材，是木材义的对应表达；lightweight timber（轻质木材）是上位概念，还包括其他木材，不能精确替换树种名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Balsa wood and balsawood explicitly name the timber and are equivalents of the material sense; lightweight timber is a broader category that includes other woods and cannot precisely replace the tree's name.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the Spanish meaning raft to wood light enough to float easily, then to the tree that supplies it.

senses.collocation_en: beryllium oxide; copper–beryllium alloy
senses.collocation_zh: 氧化铍；铜铍合金
senses.sentence_en: The springs are made from a copper–beryllium alloy.
senses.sentence_zh: 这些弹簧由铜铍合金制成。

etymology_story.zh: beryllium 以矿物 beryl（绿柱石）的名称为基础，加上元素名称中常见的 -ium 构成，因为铍最初是在这种矿物中被识别出来的。beryl 经拉丁语上溯至希腊语 bēryllos，指绿柱石一类宝石。
etymology_story.en: Beryllium was named from beryl, the mineral in which the element was first identified, with the element-name ending -ium. Beryl ultimately comes through Latin from Greek bēryllos, a name for beryl or a related gemstone.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：beryll-（与 beryl“绿柱石”相关的词干）+ -ium（元素名称后缀）→ beryllium。相关词包括 beryl（绿柱石）、beryllia（氧化铍的名称）、berylliosis（铍病）和 beryllium-containing（含铍的）；beryllium oxide、beryllium copper 等是常见化学或材料组合，并非独立词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: beryll- (the stem associated with beryl) + -ium (an element-name suffix) → beryllium. Related words include beryl, the mineral; beryllia, a name for beryllium oxide; berylliosis, a disease caused by beryllium exposure; and beryllium-containing. Combinations such as beryllium oxide and beryllium copper are chemical or material names, not separate parts of speech.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Be 是铍的化学符号，不是普通词汇中的近义词；glucinium 是铍的历史旧称，现代通常使用 beryllium。beryl 指含铍矿物绿柱石，与元素铍本身不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Be is the chemical symbol rather than an ordinary lexical synonym; glucinium is a historical alternative name, whereas beryllium is the usual modern term. Beryl names a beryllium-bearing mineral, not the element itself.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: beryl 绿柱石 + -ium 元素名：从矿石名称记住其中发现的元素“铍”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Beryl + the element ending -ium: remember the element through the mineral in which it was identified.

usage_note: 常见于触屏、传感器和电路；不是表示一般容量大的形容词。

etymology_story.zh: capacitive 由 capacity 的词干 capacit- 加 -ive 构成，发展出与电荷储存能力有关的技术含义。capacity 经法语上溯拉丁语 capacitas，表示容纳能力，最终与 capere（容纳、拿取）相关。
etymology_story.en: Capacitive was formed from the stem capacit- of capacity with -ive and developed a technical meaning concerning the ability to store electric charge. Capacity comes through French from Latin capacitas, meaning holding ability, ultimately related to capere, to hold or take.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：capacity 去掉词尾 -y，取词干 capacit- + -ive → capacitive；capacitive + -ly → capacitively（以电容方式）。核心相关词族包括 capacity（容量、能力）、capacitance（电容）和 capacitor（电容器）；更广的同源词族包括 capacious（宽敞的）、capaciously（宽敞地）、capaciousness（宽敞）、incapacity（无能力）、incapacitate（使失去能力）和 incapacitation（失能）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: remove final -y from capacity and add -ive to the stem capacit- → capacitive; add -ly → capacitively. The central related family includes capacity, capacitance, and capacitor. The broader etymological family includes capacious, capaciously, capaciousness, incapacity, incapacitate, and incapacitation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: capacitance-based（基于电容的）可释义某些设备中的 capacitive；electrostatic（静电的）涉及静止电荷及其作用，范围更广；dielectric（电介质的）强调绝缘材料及其在电场中的性质，不能与 capacitive 普遍互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Capacitance-based can paraphrase capacitive for certain devices; electrostatic concerns stationary electric charges and their effects more broadly; dielectric concerns insulating materials and their behaviour in electric fields, so it is not generally interchangeable with capacitive.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: capacity 是容纳能力；capacitive 把这种能力限定到电荷：能储存电荷，或利用电容工作。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Capacity means holding ability; capacitive applies that idea to electric charge: storing it or using capacitance to operate.

senses.meaning_zh: 用热、化学药剂等烧灼组织，以止血或去除异常组织
senses.meaning_en: to destroy or seal tissue using heat, chemicals, or a similar method
senses.english_definition: If a doctor cauterises tissue, they destroy or seal it using heat or a chemical, often to stop bleeding.

senses.sentence_zh: 外科医生烧灼封闭了那根小血管，以止住出血。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语和晚期拉丁语的相关形式传入英语，最终源于希腊语 kautēriazein，意为“用烙铁烧灼”，与表示“燃烧”的 kaiein 同源。最初的烙铁烧灼概念后来扩展到化学药剂等造成的组织烧灼。
etymology_story.en: The word reached English through French and Late Latin forms, ultimately from Greek kautēriazein, meaning to burn with a hot iron, related to kaiein, meaning to burn. The original hot-iron procedure later extended to tissue destruction by chemicals and other methods.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 cauter-（与烧灼有关的黏着词干）+ -ise（构成动词）；美式拼写为 cauterize。屈折形式有 cauterises、cauterised、cauterising；主要派生词有 cauterisation/cauterization（烧灼术）、cauteriser/cauterizer（烧灼器械或施术者）；相关同源词 cautery 指烧灼术或烧灼器。
morphology_enriched.en: A modern analysis is cauter- (a bound stem associated with cautery) + -ise (a verb-forming suffix); the American spelling is cauterize. Inflections include cauterises, cauterised, and cauterising; principal derivatives include cauterisation/cauterization and cauteriser/cauterizer. The related word cautery denotes the procedure or an instrument used for it.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: burn（烧伤、烧毁）范围最广，不一定有治疗目的；sear（灼烧表面）强调高温迅速作用于表面；cauterise 专指有目的地破坏或封闭组织，通常用于医疗。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Burn is broad and need not describe treatment; sear emphasizes intense heat acting on a surface. Cauterise specifically describes deliberately destroying or sealing tissue, usually as a medical procedure.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the original hot iron: burn the tissue to seal the bleeding point.

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语的相关形式来自盎格鲁法语，通常追溯到拉丁语植物名 conferva，并与 confervere（一起沸腾；长合、愈合）联系起来。这个名称反映了古人认为此类植物有助于伤处长合的观念，并不构成现代疗效证据。
etymology_story.en: Middle English forms came through Anglo-French and are generally traced to the Latin plant name conferva, associated with confervere, meaning to boil together or grow together. The name reflects an old belief that such plants helped injuries knit together, rather than establishing a modern medical benefit.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 comfrey 是不可再作常用构词分析的单纯词，不宜拆成 com- 和 frey。作植物总称或材料名时通常不可数，表示不同种类或植株时可用复数 comfreys；没有常用的形容词或动词派生形式，常见组合有 comfrey leaf（聚合草叶）、comfrey root（聚合草根）和 comfrey tea（聚合草浸液，具体用途取决于语境）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, comfrey is a simple lexical base and should not be split into com- and frey. It is usually uncountable as a plant or material name, but comfreys can refer to kinds or individual plants. It has no common adjectival or verbal derivatives; combinations include comfrey leaf, comfrey root, and comfrey tea, whose intended use depends on context.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: common comfrey（普通聚合草）和 true comfrey（真聚合草）通常专指 Symphytum officinale；knitbone 是强调传统“接骨”用途的民间名称。comfrey 本身还可以泛指聚合草属的其他植物，因此这些名称并非在所有语境下完全等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Common comfrey and true comfrey usually denote Symphytum officinale specifically; knitbone is a folk name reflecting traditional use for injuries. Comfrey can also refer more broadly to other Symphytum plants, so these names are not interchangeable in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “聚合草”对应古老的“长合”联想：把名称与组织重新长在一起的历史观念相连。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect comfrey with its old grow-together association: the historical image is injured tissue knitting together.

etymology.text: 英语用拉丁语来源的 con- 与 specific 组成生物学词；specific 在这里关联 species（物种），把共同属于一个物种作为记忆线索。

usage_note: 同种并不表示同一只，也不表示完全一样；本课用形容词义，名词义指同种个体。

etymology_story.zh: 这是英语生物学术语，由拉丁语来源的 con-（共同）与 specific 构成。specific 在这里保留“物种的”这一生物学含义，因此全词表示共同属于一个物种，并进一步用作名词指同种个体。
etymology_story.en: This biological term was formed in English from the Latin-derived prefix con-, meaning together, and specific. Here specific carries its biological meaning of relating to a species, producing an adjective meaning of the same species and a noun for an organism of that species.

morphology_enriched.zh: con-（共同、相同）+ specific（物种的）→ conspecific（同种的）；形容词经零派生成为名词 conspecific（同种个体），复数 conspecifics。主要派生形式有 conspecificity（同种性；同属一个物种的状态）和 conspecifically（就同种关系而言）；相关基础词包括 species（物种）和 specific（物种的；特定的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Con- (together or the same) + specific (relating to a species) forms conspecific. Conversion produces the noun conspecific, plural conspecifics. Principal derivatives are conspecificity, the state of belonging to the same species, and conspecifically, with respect to that relationship. Related base vocabulary includes species and specific.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: same-species（同种的）是直接、易懂的形容词释义；member of the same species（同一物种的成员）是名词用法的自然释义。相关词 intraspecific（种内的）描述一个物种内部发生的关系或过程，不能在所有位置替换 conspecific。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Same-species is a plain adjectival equivalent; member of the same species naturally paraphrases the noun. The related adjective intraspecific describes relationships or processes within a species and cannot replace conspecific in every construction.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: con- 表示“共同”，specific 在此关联 species：共同属于一个物种。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Con- means together; connect specific with species: together in the same species.

etymology_story.zh: corm 来自新拉丁语 cormus，最终源于希腊语 kormos，意为“树干”或“去掉枝条的树干”。这一“茎干”的历史含义与现代植物学用法相呼应：球茎是膨大的茎，而不是根。
etymology_story.en: Corm comes from New Latin cormus, ultimately from Greek kormos, meaning a trunk or a trunk stripped of its branches. That stem-based origin fits the modern botanical meaning: a corm is a swollen stem rather than a root.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 corm 是单纯词，复数为 corms。主要派生词有 corm + -let → cormlet（小球茎）、corm + -el → cormel（子球茎）以及 corm + -ous → cormous（具球茎的）；cormlet 和 cormel 都可指形成于母球茎旁的小球茎。
morphology_enriched.en: Corm is a simple modern English base, with the plural corms. Principal derivatives include corm + -let → cormlet, corm + -el → cormel, and corm + -ous → cormous, meaning having corms. Cormlet and cormel can both denote small corms produced beside a parent corm.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全对应的常用英语近义词；易混的相关词有 bulb（鳞茎）、tuber（块茎）和 rhizome（根状茎）。corm 主要由实心、膨大的茎组织构成，bulb 主要靠肉质鳞叶储存养分，tuber 是膨大的茎或茎段，rhizome 则是通常横向生长的地下茎。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday synonym; related terms are bulb, tuber, and rhizome. A corm consists chiefly of solid swollen stem tissue, a bulb stores food mainly in fleshy leaf bases, a tuber is a swollen stem or stem portion, and a rhizome is a usually horizontal underground stem.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从词源“树干”记住“茎”：球茎是缩短、膨大并储粮的地下茎。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the original trunk image to remember stem: a corm is a shortened, swollen underground food store.

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自拉丁语 emollire（使柔软）的现在分词词干 emollient-，其中 mollis 表示“柔软的”。英语先用它形容具有软化作用的物质，后来也用作润肤制剂的名称，并将“软化”引申为缓和人的情绪或分歧。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from emollient-, the present-participle stem of Latin emollire, meaning to soften, based on mollis, meaning soft. English first used it adjectivally for softening substances, then as a name for skin preparations, while figurative use extended softening to feelings and disagreements.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是借入的拉丁语分词形式；历史上可分析为 e-/ex-（此处有加强作用）+ moll-（柔软）+ 分词词尾，英语表面形式以 -ent 结尾。现代英语中通常整体识记；名词是由形容词转类而来，复数为 emollients；相关派生词有 emollience（柔化作用；安抚性）和 emolliently（以安抚的方式，较少见），mollify（使平静；缓和）是同源词。
morphology_enriched.en: This is a borrowed Latin participial formation, historically analyzable as e-/ex- (with an intensive force here) + moll- (soft) + a participial ending, appearing in English as -ent. It is generally learned as a whole modern base. The noun is converted from the adjective, with plural emollients; related derivatives include emollience and the less common emolliently, while mollify is an etymological relative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: moisturizer（保湿产品）强调改善皮肤干燥，与名词 emollient 有较大重叠，但 emollient 更突出柔润作用；soothing（舒缓的、安抚的）可用于身体不适或情绪；conciliatory（有意和解的）专门强调减少冲突，接近 emollient 的比喻义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Moisturizer emphasizes relieving skin dryness and overlaps substantially with the noun emollient, which highlights softening. Soothing can describe relief of physical discomfort or emotional distress; conciliatory specifically emphasizes reducing conflict and is close to the figurative adjective.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 moll- 的“柔软”：使皮肤柔软，也使强硬的情绪软下来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor moll- to soft: soften the skin, or soften a tense emotional atmosphere.

etymology_story.zh: hidebound 由 hide（兽皮）和 bound（束紧的）组成，最初形容牲畜因病弱等原因皮肤紧贴身体的状态。后来，这种身体受紧皮束缚的形象被用于比喻思想僵化、受传统束缚。
etymology_story.en: Hidebound combines hide, meaning animal skin, with bound, meaning tightly constrained, and originally described livestock whose skin clung tightly to the body. This physical image later developed into a description of people whose thinking is constrained by tradition.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：hide（兽皮，名词）+ bound（bind 的过去分词，表示被束住的）→ hidebound（顽固守旧的，形容词）。相关派生：hideboundness（顽固守旧；思想僵化，较少见）；比较级和最高级通常用 more hidebound、most hidebound。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: hide, a noun meaning animal skin, + bound, the past participle of bind used adjectivally, → hidebound. The related derivative hideboundness means rigid traditionalism and is uncommon; comparison normally uses more hidebound and most hidebound.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 近义词：conservative（保守的）、inflexible（不灵活的）、dogmatic（教条的）。hidebound 贬义较强，突出传统观念造成的束缚；conservative 不一定含贬义，inflexible 强调不肯调整，dogmatic 强调把自己的信念当作不可质疑的真理。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Near-synonyms: conservative, inflexible, and dogmatic. Hidebound strongly criticizes restriction by tradition; conservative can be neutral, inflexible emphasizes unwillingness to adapt, and dogmatic emphasizes treating one's beliefs as unquestionable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hide（皮）把思想 bound（束住）：外壳太紧，观念转不过弯。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Imagine the mind bound inside a tight hide: its ideas have no room to change.

etymology_story.zh: impasto 借自意大利语，原有“面团、糊状混合物”之意，与 impastare（揉成面团；拌成糊）有关。英语绘画术语保留了这种糊状物的形象，用来表示厚厚施加颜料的技法及其形成的颜料层。
etymology_story.en: Impasto comes from Italian impasto, meaning dough or a paste-like mixture, and is related to impastare, meaning to knead or mix into a paste. In English painting terminology, the image of a thick paste became the name for both the technique and its raised paint.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 impasto 作为完整借词，不拆成具有现代英语构词功能的前后缀。词族及相关词形：impasto（名词；亦有较少见的绘画专业动词用法，意为厚涂）、impastos（复数）、impastoed（厚涂的；动词过去式及过去分词）、impastoing（动词现在分词及动名词）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, impasto is normally treated as a complete loanword rather than a combination of productive English affixes. Its family and related forms include impasto as a noun and an uncommon technical verb meaning to apply paint thickly, impastos as the plural, impastoed as an adjective or past form, and impastoing as a participle or gerund.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 近义表达：thick application of paint（厚施颜料）、paint buildup（颜料堆积）、textured painting（肌理绘画）。第一项直接描述施色方式，第二项强调堆积出的颜料，第三项范围更广；impasto 特指厚颜料本身形成凸起肌理的技法或颜料层。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Near-equivalents: thick application of paint, paint buildup, and textured painting. The first describes the method, the second emphasizes accumulated paint, and the third covers a broader range of textures; impasto specifically involves raised texture created by thick paint.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of paint spread like thick dough: the thicker the paint, the more visible its texture.

etymology_story.zh: imprecate 源自拉丁语 imprecari，意为“祈求降临；诅咒”，由 in-（向、对，在 p 前变为 im-）和 precari（祈求）组成。英语承接了其中祈求灾祸降临的含义，即把祈求转向伤害或惩罚。
etymology_story.en: Imprecate derives from Latin imprecari, meaning to invoke or curse, formed from in-, meaning upon or toward, and precari, meaning to pray. English preserves the hostile application of prayer: calling down harm or punishment.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中它是较正式的拉丁来源动词，可借词源结构 im-（向、对）+ prec-（祈求）+ -ate（动词词尾）理解，而非现代自由拼接的构词。词形：imprecates、imprecated、imprecating；派生词：imprecation（诅咒；咒语）、imprecatory（诅咒的）、imprecative（表示诅咒的，较少见）、imprecator（诅咒者，罕见）。
morphology_enriched.en: This is a formal Latinate verb whose historical structure can be understood as im-, meaning upon or toward, + prec-, associated with prayer, + the verbal ending -ate; it is not a freely assembled modern formation. Inflections are imprecates, imprecated, and imprecating; derivatives include imprecation, imprecatory, the less common imprecative, and the rare agent noun imprecator.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 近义词：curse（诅咒；咒骂）、damn（咒骂；宣判受罚）、execrate（痛斥；憎恶）。imprecate 最强调祈求灾祸降临，且语体庄重或古雅；curse 最通用，damn 常带愤怒或宗教惩罚意味，execrate 更强调强烈憎恶和谴责。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Near-synonyms: curse, damn, and execrate. Imprecate particularly emphasizes invoking harm and has a formal or literary tone; curse is the broadest term, damn often suggests anger or religious condemnation, and execrate emphasizes intense hatred and denunciation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: prec- 是“祈求”：把祈求对准灾祸，就是诅咒。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The prec- element suggests prayer: praying for harm to fall upon someone becomes cursing.

etymology_story.zh: medulla 借自拉丁语 medulla，原意是“骨髓”，也可表示内部的核心。解剖学沿用这一内部组织的形象，将它用于某些器官的髓质；单独使用时，它也常指 medulla oblongata，即延髓。
etymology_story.en: Medulla comes from Latin medulla, meaning marrow and, by extension, an inner core. Anatomical usage applies this image to the inner regions of certain organs, while medulla alone also commonly abbreviates medulla oblongata.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 medulla 是完整的拉丁借词，其专业词干为 medull-，不宜把词尾 -a 当作有独立意义的英语后缀。复数为 medullae 或 medullas；主要派生词为 medullary（髓质的；延髓的）及较少见的 medullar（髓质的）；相关专业词有 medullated（有髓鞘的）和 medullation（髓鞘形成）。
morphology_enriched.en: Medulla is a complete Latin loanword with the technical stem medull-; its final -a is not an independently meaningful English suffix. Plurals are medullae and medullas; principal derivatives include medullary and the less common medullar, while related technical terms include medullated, meaning myelinated, and medullation, meaning myelin formation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 近义或解释性用词：marrow（骨髓）、pith（植物的髓）、core（核心；内部）。这些词都涉及内部物质，但 marrow 主要指骨内组织，pith 主要指植物茎的中央组织，core 是一般用语；medulla 是具体解剖结构的术语，不能在所有场合与它们互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Related or explanatory terms: marrow, pith, and core. Marrow usually refers to tissue inside bones, pith to central tissue in plant stems, and core is a general word; medulla names particular anatomical regions and is not interchangeable with all three.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“骨髓”抓住“内部”：medulla 常是器官里面的髓质，也可专指延髓。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with marrow, the tissue inside a bone: medulla points inward, and in the brainstem it names the medulla oblongata.

senses.pos: adj. 形容词（地理学、生态学）
senses.meaning_zh: 山地的；生长或分布于山地带的

senses.english_definition: Montane plants, animals, and habitats occur in mountain regions, especially in ecological belts below the subalpine and alpine zones.

etymology_story.zh: montane 源自拉丁语 montanus（山地的），其基础是 mons，词干为 mont-，意为“山”。英语保留了它与山地相关的意义，并常将其用于山地植被、动物和生态带的描述。
etymology_story.en: Montane comes from Latin montanus, meaning mountainous or belonging to mountains, based on mons, with the stem mont-, meaning mountain. English retains this geographical meaning and often uses it to describe mountain vegetation, wildlife, and ecological zones.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 montane 作为完整的借入形容词；词源上可识别 mont-（山）与形容词词尾 -ane，但 -ane 在这里不是可自由套用的现代英语后缀。相关词族包括 submontane（山麓带或山地较低处的）、intermontane（山间的）、intramontane（山地内部的）和 transmontane（越过山脉的；山那边的）；这些词共享 mont- 词干，并非全由 montane 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats montane as a complete borrowed adjective; historically, mont- means mountain and -ane is an adjectival ending, rather than a freely productive English suffix here. Related formations include submontane, referring to foothills or lower mountain belts; intermontane, between mountains; intramontane, within a mountain region; and transmontane, across or beyond mountains. These share mont- and are not all direct derivatives of montane.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 近义词：mountainous（多山的；山地的）、alpine（高山的）、upland（高地的）。montane 常用于山地生态带；mountainous 强调地形多山，alpine 在生态学中通常指林线以上的高山带，upland 只强调地势较高，不一定属于山地。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Near-synonyms: mountainous, alpine, and upland. Montane often identifies a mountain ecological belt; mountainous emphasizes mountainous terrain, alpine in ecology usually concerns the zone above the tree line, and upland means relatively high ground that need not be mountainous.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 认准 mont-＝山：montane 把生物和环境放进山地带。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Recognize mont- as mountain: montane places a habitat or species in a mountain region.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经斯堪的纳维亚语言进入英语，可追溯至古北欧语 nár（尸体）和 hvalr（鲸）的组合。这个名称通常被解释为源于独角鲸斑驳的灰白体色；它的“角”实际上是一颗伸长的牙齿。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through Scandinavian languages and goes back to Old Norse nár, meaning 'corpse', and hvalr, meaning 'whale'. The name is usually explained as a reference to its mottled, pale coloration; its 'horn' is actually an elongated tooth.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为不可再作能产性拆分的借入词整体记忆，不把 nar- 和 -whal 当作英语词缀。复数为 narwhals，也可使用不变复数 narwhal；另有拼写变体 narwhale，复数 narwhales。没有常用的派生形容词或动词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, narwhal is an unanalyzed borrowing rather than a productive combination of English morphemes. Its plural is narwhals or unchanged narwhal; the spelling variant narwhale has the plural narwhales. There are no common derived adjectives or verbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有常用的严格同义词。whale（鲸）是范围更广的上位词；toothed whale（齿鲸）指其所属的大类；beluga（白鲸）是近缘但不同的鲸类，不能与 narwhal 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym. Whale is a broader term; toothed whale names the larger group to which narwhals belong; beluga refers to a closely related but different whale and is not interchangeable with narwhal.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史命名看“灰白斑驳”，辨认外形看“长牙似角”：独角鲸。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Its pale, mottled body explains the historical name; its hornlike tooth identifies the narwhal.

etymology_story.zh: noggin 在十六世纪已有“小杯、小容器”的用法，但更早的词源不确定。后来它发展出诙谐口语中的“脑袋”义，可能与杯子和头部的外形联想有关，但这种联系并无定论。
etymology_story.en: Noggin was used for a small cup or vessel in the sixteenth century, although its earlier origin is uncertain. It later acquired the humorous meaning 'head', possibly through an association between the shapes of a cup and a head, though that connection is not established.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 noggin 作为独立词基记忆，不宜机械拆成 nog + -gin。复数为 noggins；罕见的历史派生词 nogginful = noggin（小杯）+ -ful（满杯的量），表示“一小杯的量”，不属于“脑袋”义的常用词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat noggin as an independent base in modern English rather than mechanically dividing it into nog + -gin. Its plural is noggins. The rare historical derivative nogginful combines the 'small cup' sense with -ful to mean the amount held by such a cup; it is not a common derivative of the 'head' sense.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: head（头）最中性，可用于正式或日常表达；brain（脑、头脑）强调思考能力；nut（脑袋）也可作俚语，但语气往往更粗随意。noggin 通常显得轻松、诙谐。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Head is the neutral term for the body part; brain emphasizes thought or intelligence; nut is another slang term for the head but can sound rougher. Noggin usually has a playful, humorous tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把圆圆的小杯联想成圆圆的脑袋；use your noggin 就是“动动脑子”。此联想用于记忆，并非确定词源。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a little round cup as a little round head: use your noggin means 'think'. This is a memory aid, not a proven etymology.

senses.meaning_en: unnecessary trouble, fuss, or complicated arrangements, especially in British informal usage
senses.english_definition: If you call an activity a palaver, you mean that it involves more trouble or effort than you think is necessary.

senses.meaning_en: to talk at length, often unnecessarily or idly

senses.sentence_zh: 他们围绕各项安排聊了一个小时，才终于有人开始干活。

etymology_story.zh: palaver 来自葡萄牙语 palavra（话语），最终可追溯至晚期拉丁语 parabola（比喻、言说）。它早期用于贸易接触中的交谈和交涉，后来发展出“冗长空谈”，并进一步引申为“麻烦、折腾”。
etymology_story.en: Palaver comes from Portuguese palavra, meaning 'word' or 'speech', ultimately from Late Latin parabola, meaning 'parable' or 'discourse'. It was used for discussions and negotiations in trading encounters before developing the meanings 'unnecessary talk' and, later, 'fuss or trouble'.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 palaver 作为完整借入词基；名词可通过零派生用作动词，不宜拆成虚构的英语词根。名词复数及动词第三人称单数为 palavers，过去式和过去分词为 palavered，现在分词为 palavering；palaverer = palaver + -er，表示“喋喋不休者”，较少见。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats palaver as a complete borrowed base, with the noun also used as a verb through conversion; it should not be divided into invented English roots. Inflected forms are palavers, palavered, and palavering. The uncommon derivative palaverer adds -er to mean someone who talks at length.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 说话义中，chatter（闲聊、叽叽喳喳）强调轻松或连续说话，未必惹人厌烦；prattle（絮叨）强调内容浅薄；麻烦义中，fuss（忙乱、小题大做）强调不必要的操心或折腾。palaver 常暗含“费了很多口舌或工夫却不值得”。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For talk, chatter suggests light or continuous conversation without necessarily expressing annoyance, while prattle emphasizes trivial content. For trouble, fuss emphasizes unnecessary activity or concern. Palaver often suggests that the talk or effort is excessive and unproductive.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“话语”出发：话说太多成空谈，事情太繁成折腾。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with 'speech': too many words become empty talk; too much procedure becomes a palaver.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经拉丁语 panegyricus 追溯至希腊语 panēgyrikos，原指适合公众盛会的演说，其基础词 panēgyris 表示“全体集会”。在盛会上发表的演说常用于赞颂人物或功绩，因此逐渐形成“颂词、颂扬的”之义。
etymology_story.en: The word comes through Latin panegyricus from Greek panēgyrikos, referring to an address delivered at a public festival; its underlying noun panēgyris means a general assembly. Such public addresses often praised people or achievements, giving rise to the senses 'formal tribute' and 'praising'.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜把 panegyric 作为完整的学术借入词记忆；历史上的 pan- 表示“全体”，其余部分与希腊语“集会”有关，不是能产的英语构词单位。相关词族包括 panegyrical（颂扬的）、panegyrically（颂扬地）、panegyrist（颂词作者、赞颂者）以及 panegyrize／panegyrise（赞颂）；这些派生形式多用于正式或文学语境。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, panegyric is best treated as a complete learned borrowing. Historically, pan- means 'all', while the remaining material relates to a Greek word for an assembly rather than a productive English base. Its related family includes panegyrical, panegyrically, panegyrist, and panegyrize or panegyrise, mainly in formal or literary usage.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: eulogy（悼词、颂词）现代常用于赞颂逝者；encomium（赞词）强调热烈赞美，语体同样正式；tribute（致敬、赞颂）范围更广，也可指行动或礼物。panegyric 尤指篇幅较完整、措辞隆重的赞颂，有时暗含赞美过度。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Eulogy now commonly refers to praise of someone who has died; encomium similarly denotes enthusiastic praise in a formal register; tribute is broader and can include an action or gift. Panegyric particularly suggests an elaborate formal expression of praise and can imply excess.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pan- 是“全体”：想象全体齐聚盛会，台上发表隆重颂词。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pan- means 'all': picture everyone assembled at a festival to hear a grand speech of praise.

etymology_story.zh: pugilist 由拉丁语 pugil（拳击手）一系的词干加上表示从事者的 -ist 构成，拉丁语词族与 pugnus（拳头）有关。它进入英语后用于称呼拳击运动的参与者，如今通常比 boxer 更显正式或带有历史色彩。
etymology_story.en: Pugilist was formed from the stem of Latin pugil, meaning 'boxer', with the agent suffix -ist; the Latin word family is related to pugnus, meaning 'fist'. In English it names someone who boxes and now generally sounds more formal or historical than boxer.

morphology_enriched.zh: pugil-（与拳击有关的黏着词干）+ -ist（从事者）→ pugilist（拳击手）；复数为 pugilists。相关词族包括 pugilism（拳击运动）、pugilistic（拳击的；好斗的）和 pugilistically（以拳击方式；好斗地）。
morphology_enriched.en: Pugil- is a bound stem associated with boxing, and -ist denotes a participant or practitioner: pugil- + -ist → pugilist. The plural is pugilists. Related words include pugilism, meaning boxing; pugilistic, meaning relating to boxing or combative; and pugilistically.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: boxer（拳击手）是最常用、中性的称呼；prizefighter（职业拳击手）强调以奖金或报酬为目的参赛；fighter（格斗选手）范围更广，也可指其他格斗项目的选手。pugilist 带有正式、文学或旧时拳坛的色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Boxer is the usual neutral term; prizefighter emphasizes fighting for payment or prize money; fighter is broader and can refer to participants in other combat sports. Pugilist has a formal, literary, or historical flavor.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pugil- 联结“拳头、拳击”，-ist 表示“从事者”：靠拳头比赛的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect pugil- with fists and boxing, then add -ist for the practitioner: someone who competes with their fists.

etymology_story.zh: 由 re-（重新）与 master（制作母版）构成；在录音和影视制作中，master 指用于制作发行副本的母版。该词后来扩展到电子游戏，表示在原作基础上提升画面、声音等技术质量。
etymology_story.en: The word combines re-, meaning 'again', with master, the verb associated with preparing the master used to produce distribution copies of recordings or films. Its use later extended to video games whose graphics, sound, or other technical features are upgraded.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：re-（重新）+ master（制作母版）→ remaster；动词可直接转用为名词。常用词族：remasters（第三人称单数或名词复数）、remastered（过去式、过去分词，也作修饰语）、remastering（现在分词，也指重新制作母版这一过程）；相关基础词有 master（母版；制作母版）和 mastering（母版制作）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: re- ('again') + master ('prepare a master') → remaster; the verb also functions as a noun through conversion. Common family forms are remasters, remastered, and remastering, with remastered also used as a modifier and remastering as a process noun; relevant base forms are master and mastering.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: restore（修复）着重消除损坏或恢复原貌；remix（重新混音）着重重新调整或组合各条音轨；remake（重新制作）通常涉及重新拍摄、录制或开发。remaster 主要改善原有作品的技术呈现，通常保留其基本内容。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Restore emphasizes repairing damage or recovering an earlier condition; remix means changing how recorded tracks are combined; remake usually involves creating the work again. Remaster primarily improves the technical presentation of an existing work while generally preserving its basic content.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: master 是复制用的“母版”；re-master 就是“重新做好母版，让旧作品更清晰”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A master is the source for copies: re-master it to make the existing work look or sound better.

etymology_story.zh: right 与 wing 组合而成，wing 在这里指政治阵营。政治上的“右”源于法国大革命时期议会的座次：支持君主制和传统制度的成员坐在右侧，此后 right wing 逐渐成为右翼阵营的名称。
etymology_story.en: The word combines right with wing in the sense of a political faction. Political 'right' comes from seating arrangements during the French Revolution, when supporters of monarchy and traditional institutions sat on the right, giving rise to right wing as a political label.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：right（右）+ wing（派别）→ rightwing（右翼的），形容词也常写作 right-wing。相关词族：right wing（分写的名词短语，右翼阵营）、rightwinger／right-winger（右翼人士）、rightist（右翼人士；右翼的）、rightism（右翼思想或立场）；leftwing／left-wing（左翼的）是对应构词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: right + wing ('faction') → rightwing, also commonly written right-wing as an adjective. Related forms include right wing, the separately written noun phrase for the political faction; rightwinger/right-winger, a person on the political right; rightist, a noun or adjective; and rightism, right-wing views. Leftwing/left-wing is the corresponding formation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: conservative（保守的）强调维护传统和渐进变革，具体政治定位随语境而异；rightist（右翼的）直接标示政治阵营，通常较正式；reactionary（反动的、主张复旧的）强调恢复过去的制度，含义更强且常带贬义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Conservative emphasizes preserving traditions and preferring gradual change, with its political position depending on context; rightist directly identifies alignment with the political right and is often more formal; reactionary implies seeking a return to an earlier social or political order and is stronger and often disapproving.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象议会右侧的一“翼”：right 定方向，wing 表阵营。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture one wing of parliament sitting on the right: right gives the side, and wing gives the faction.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 saccharin 借自十九世纪的德语科学名称 Saccharin，名称采用表示“糖”的 sacchar- 词根。该词根经拉丁语 saccharum、希腊语 sakkharon 可追溯至梵语 śarkarā；名称指向其甜味，并不表示糖精就是糖。
etymology_story.en: English saccharin was borrowed from the nineteenth-century German scientific name Saccharin, formed with the sugar-related stem sacchar-. That stem traces through Latin saccharum and Greek sakkharon to Sanskrit śarkarā; the name refers to its sweetness rather than identifying it as sugar.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代科学构词分析：sacchar-（糖）+ -in（物质名称后缀）→ saccharin。相关词族与同根词包括 saccharine（甜的；甜腻做作的，不能与名词 saccharin 混写）、saccharide（糖类）、monosaccharide（单糖）、disaccharide（二糖）、polysaccharide（多糖）、saccharify（使糖化）和 saccharification（糖化）；这些同根词并非都由 saccharin 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Scientific morphological analysis: sacchar- ('sugar') + -in, a substance-name suffix → saccharin. Related family members and root relatives include saccharine ('sweet' or 'excessively sentimental'), saccharide, monosaccharide, disaccharide, polysaccharide, saccharify, and saccharification; these are not all direct derivatives of saccharin, and saccharine is a distinct adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: artificial sweetener（人工甜味剂）是包含糖精在内的上位词；sugar substitute（糖替代品）按用途分类，范围更广；benzoic sulfimide（苯甲酰磺酰亚胺）是糖精的化学名称。前两者不能在需要明确具体物质时完全替代 saccharin。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Artificial sweetener names a category that includes saccharin; sugar substitute is a broader term defined by use; benzoic sulfimide is a chemical name for saccharin itself. The first two are category terms rather than exact substitutes when the particular substance matters.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sacchar- 提示“糖、甜”，-in 提示“物质”：有糖的甜味，却是糖的替代品。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sacchar- signals sugar or sweetness, and -in signals a substance: sweetness from a sugar substitute.

etymology_story.zh: 由英语 zip 加形容词后缀 -y 构成；zip 原有模仿快速运动时短促声音的表达性用法，也发展出“迅速移动”和“活力”等意思。zippy 因而可形容动作、表达或味道上的轻快与带劲。
etymology_story.en: Zippy was formed from zip and the adjective suffix -y; zip has expressive uses imitating the brief sound of swift movement and developed senses involving speed and energy. Zippy consequently describes lively movement, expression, or flavor.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：zip（快速移动；活力）+ -y（具有……特点的）→ zippy，词尾 p 双写。常用词族：zippier（比较级）、zippiest（最高级）、zippily（轻快地）、zippiness（轻快；活力）；基础词 zip 的屈折形式有 zips、zipped、zipping。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: zip ('move quickly; energy') + -y ('having the qualities of') → zippy, with the final p doubled. Common family forms are zippier, zippiest, zippily, and zippiness; the base word zip also has the forms zips, zipped, and zipping.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: brisk（轻快迅速的）着重动作或节奏；lively（活泼的）着重活力与趣味，未必速度快；zesty（风味浓郁的、热情洋溢的）着重味觉刺激或感染力。zippy 是较口语化的词，常带轻巧、利落、令人愉快的感觉。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Brisk emphasizes quick movement or pace; lively emphasizes energy and interest without necessarily implying speed; zesty emphasizes stimulating flavor or enthusiasm. Zippy is informal and often suggests something pleasantly light, quick, or spirited.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: zip 是“嗖”的一下：车跑得快、曲调有活力、味道也带劲。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'zip!'—a quick burst of movement, energy, or flavor.

morphology.text: 历史短语 en + gogues → en gogues（处于欢乐中），经 agogge 演变为 agog；现代把 agog 作为独立词素记忆。

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语形式为 agogge，通常认为与中古法语 en gogues（兴高采烈、尽情欢乐）有关。词义后来集中于因期待消息或某件事情而产生的兴奋和急切。
etymology_story.en: The Middle English form agogge is generally connected with Middle French en gogues, meaning 'in high spirits' or 'in merriment'. Its meaning later centered on the excitement and eagerness produced by an anticipated event or piece of news.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 agog 是不可再作实用拆分的独立词，不宜把 a- 和 gog 当作可自由组合的现代词素。没有常用的派生词族；常见结构有 be agog（兴奋期待）、all agog（十分急切）、agog with excitement（兴奋不已）、agog to hear（急切想听到）；通常不用在名词前作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, agog is a single lexical unit without a useful productive breakdown into a- and gog. It has no common derivative family; usual constructions include be agog, all agog, agog with excitement, and agog to hear, and it is normally used predicatively rather than before a noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: eager（急切的）强调强烈想做某事；excited（兴奋的）强调情绪被激发，未必包含求知或等待；curious（好奇的）强调想知道原因或信息，情绪可以很平静。agog 把兴奋与急切期待结合在一起，语气较生动。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Eager emphasizes a strong desire to do something; excited emphasizes heightened emotion without necessarily implying anticipation or a wish to know; curious emphasizes wanting information and can describe a calm state. Agog vividly combines excitement with eager anticipation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“兴高采烈”连到“兴奋等消息”：全场伸长脖子、急着听下文，就是 all agog。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect high spirits with eager anticipation: everyone leans forward, excited to hear what comes next.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式常见读法；重音按音标中的 ˈ 标记。

forms: 表示反照率这一物理量时通常不可数；不同表面的数值可用复数 albedos。
family: albedometer 反照率测量仪。

morphology.text: 拉丁词根 alb-（白） + -edo（状态）→ albedo（白度）；英语中整词表示反照率。

etymology.text: 借自拉丁语 albedo，原义为“白度”。从白色表面反光的印象，记住它表示照来的光有多大比例被反射回去。

usage_note: 用于气候、天文和表面光学；常说 high 或 low albedo，不是表面自身发光的强度。

senses.meaning_zh: 反照率；表面反射的辐射量占入射辐射量的比例
senses.meaning_en: The proportion of incoming radiation reflected by a surface.
senses.english_definition: The albedo of a surface is the proportion of the radiation reaching it that it reflects.
senses.collocation_en: surface albedo; high albedo
senses.collocation_zh: 表面反照率；高反照率

etymology_story.zh: 借自拉丁语 albēdō，意为“白色、白度”，源于 albus“白的”。英语科学用法将“白度”发展为衡量表面反射入射辐射比例的术语。
etymology_story.en: Albedo was borrowed from Latin albēdō, meaning 'whiteness', from albus, 'white'. In scientific English, this idea developed into a measure of the proportion of incoming radiation that a surface reflects.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借词，不宜按英语词缀强行拆分；历史上可分析为拉丁语 alb-（白）＋-ēdō（构成状态或性质名词）。主要相关形式：albedos（复数）；相关术语有 surface albedo（表面反照率）、planetary albedo（行星反照率）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, albedo is an intact loanword rather than a productive root-and-affix formation; historically, Latin alb- means 'white' and -ēdō forms nouns of state or quality. The principal inflected form is albedos; related technical expressions include surface albedo and planetary albedo.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: reflectance（反射比）是最接近的技术近义词，具体定义可取决于波长和观测条件；reflectivity（反射能力、反射率）侧重材料反射辐射的性质。albedo 通常用于天文、气候和地表研究，强调反射辐射与入射辐射的比例。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Reflectance is the closest technical synonym, with its precise definition depending on wavelength and measurement conditions; reflectivity emphasizes a material's ability to reflect radiation. Albedo is especially common in astronomy, climate science, and surface studies, where it expresses the reflected fraction of incoming radiation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: alb- 联想到“白”：白雪把阳光反射回去，反回去的比例就是反照率。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect alb-, 'white', with white snow reflecting sunlight: the fraction reflected is its albedo.

meaning: 赋予非人事物以人的特征；拟人化
aliases: 赋予非人事物以人的特征

pronunciation.note: 采用英式常见读法；重音按音标中的 ˈ 标记。

forms: 英式 anthropomorphise；美式 anthropomorphize。过去式/过去分词 anthropomorphised；现在分词 anthropomorphising；第三人称 anthropomorphises。
family: anthropomorphism 拟人化；anthropomorphic 拟人的。

morphology.text: anthropo-（人） + morph（形态） + -ise（使成为）→ anthropomorphise（赋予人的特征）。

etymology.text: 英语利用源自希腊语 anthropos“人”和 morphe“形态”的词根，加动词后缀 -ise 构成。把动物或机器“想成人”就容易记住。

usage_note: 及物动词，后接动物、神或物体；人性化设计不一定是在赋予人的情感。

senses.meaning_zh: 把动物、物体或抽象事物拟人化；赋予非人事物人的特征、情感或意图
senses.meaning_en: To attribute human characteristics, feelings, or intentions to something nonhuman.

senses.collocation_en: anthropomorphise animals; anthropomorphise technology
senses.collocation_zh: 把动物拟人化；把技术产品拟人化

senses.sentence_zh: 我们常常把宠物拟人化，认为它们做错事时会感到内疚。

etymology_story.zh: 属于源自希腊语 anthrōpos“人”和 morphē“形态”的词族，与 anthropomorphism“拟人论、拟人化”相关。这个词族早期涉及赋予神以人的形态或性质，后来扩展到用人的特征解释动物、物体和其他非人事物。
etymology_story.en: Anthropomorphise belongs to a word family built from Greek anthrōpos, 'human being', and morphē, 'form', and is related to anthropomorphism. The family was associated with giving gods human forms or qualities before extending to human interpretations of animals, objects, and other nonhuman things.

morphology_enriched.zh: anthropo-（人）＋morph（形态）＋-ise（构成动词）；anthropomorphise 是英式拼写，对应 -ize 拼写 anthropomorphize。主要词族：anthropomorphised/anthropomorphized（过去式、过去分词）、anthropomorphising/anthropomorphizing（现在分词）、anthropomorphism（拟人论；拟人化）、anthropomorphic（拟人的）、anthropomorphically（以拟人方式）、anthropomorphisation/anthropomorphization（拟人化过程）、anthropomorphist（拟人论者）。
morphology_enriched.en: anthropo- ('human') + morph ('form') + -ise (a verb-forming suffix); anthropomorphise is a British spelling, corresponding to anthropomorphize. The main family includes anthropomorphised/anthropomorphized, anthropomorphising/anthropomorphizing, anthropomorphism (the attribution of human qualities), anthropomorphic (having or suggesting human qualities), anthropomorphically (in a humanizing manner), anthropomorphisation/anthropomorphization (the process), and anthropomorphist (someone who adopts this interpretation).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: personify（拟人化）常指文学上让事物像人一样说话或行动，也可指某人体现某种品质；humanise（使人性化）含义更广，可指使事物更有人情味；personalise（使个性化、人格化）常指按个人需要定制。anthropomorphise 特指向非人事物投射人的属性或心理。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Personify often means making something speak or act like a person in literature, and can also mean embodying a quality; humanise is broader and can mean making something more humane or relatable; personalise often means adapting something to an individual. Anthropomorphise specifically attributes human qualities or mental states to something nonhuman.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: anthropo- 是“人”，morph 是“形态”：给非人的事物套上人的模样和心理。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anthropo- means 'human' and morph means 'form': give something nonhuman a human shape or mind.

meaning: 蓬松隆起的（头发或衣服）

forms: 形容词本身不变形；名词 bouffant 可指蓬松发型，复数 bouffants。
family: bouffer 法语“鼓起”的动词，是历史上的关联词。

morphology.text: 法语 bouff-（鼓起） + -ant（现在分词词尾）→ bouffant（蓬起的）；英语中作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 借自法语 bouffant，是 bouffer“鼓起、蓬起”的现在分词。想象头发或裙摆像充了气一样隆起。

usage_note: 修饰 hair、hairstyle、skirt 等，强调蓬起的体积；英式读法的词尾 t 不发音，美式 /buːˈfɑːnt/ 的词尾 t 发音。

senses.meaning_zh: 头发蓬松高耸的；衣服蓬起宽大的

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 bouffant，是 bouffer“鼓起、蓬起”的现在分词。英语用它描写向外蓬起的衣服和头发，后来也把它用作名词，指高而丰盈的发型。
etymology_story.en: Bouffant was borrowed from French bouffant, the present participle of bouffer, 'to puff out'. English applied it to full, projecting clothing and hair, and also developed a noun use for a high, voluminous hairstyle.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借词，没有常用且能自由构词的英语前后缀；历史上的法语结构为 bouff-（蓬起）＋-ant（现在分词词尾）。主要形式为形容词 bouffant、名词 bouffant 及其复数 bouffants，没有常见的丰富派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, bouffant is an intact loanword without freely productive English affixes; its historical French structure is bouff- ('puff out') + -ant (the present-participle ending). Its principal forms are the adjective bouffant, the noun bouffant, and the plural bouffants; it has no extensive common derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: voluminous（丰盈宽大的）强调体积大、分量足；puffy（鼓起的）强调像充气一样膨起，有时带负面意味；full（丰满宽松的）是较中性的概括。bouffant 特别强调发型或衣服刻意塑造出的高蓬轮廓。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Voluminous emphasizes substantial volume; puffy suggests an inflated appearance and can be unfavorable; full is a more neutral description of ample shape. Bouffant specifically suggests a deliberately raised or puffed-out silhouette in hair or clothing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“蓬起”：头发或裙摆像充了气，向外鼓成圆润轮廓。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'puffed out': hair or a skirt swells outward into a full, rounded shape.

family: camphorated 含樟脑的。

morphology.text: camphor + -ate + -ed → camphorated（加有樟脑的）；camphor 本身作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 经古法语 camphore 或中古拉丁语 camphora 进入英语，可追溯到阿拉伯语 kafur。把它同樟树的强烈气味联系起来。

usage_note: 指具体化学物质，不能把所有防蛀丸都叫 camphor；不同产品的成分可能不同。

senses.meaning_zh: 樟脑；具有强烈气味的白色结晶状物质
senses.meaning_en: A strongly scented white crystalline substance obtained from camphor trees or made synthetically.
senses.english_definition: Camphor is a white substance with a strong smell that comes from camphor trees or is made synthetically and is used in some medicinal and insect-repellent products.

etymology_story.zh: 经法语和中古拉丁语 camphora 等形式传入英语，可追溯到阿拉伯语 kāfūr。这个词随着芳香物质的贸易传播，英语中沿用它来指樟脑这种气味强烈的物质。
etymology_story.en: Camphor entered English through French and medieval Latin forms such as camphora, ultimately tracing back to Arabic kāfūr. The name traveled with the trade in aromatic substances and remained the English term for this strongly scented material.

morphology_enriched.zh: camphor 在现代英语中是整体词干，不宜拆成无关的英语词素。主要词族：camphorate（用樟脑处理或加入樟脑）、camphorated（加有樟脑的）、camphorating（加入樟脑的过程；现在分词）、camphoric（樟脑的；与樟脑有关的）；常见复合词组有 camphor tree（樟树）、camphor oil（樟脑油）。
morphology_enriched.en: Camphor functions as a whole stem in modern English and should not be split into unrelated English elements. Its main family includes camphorate (to treat or mix with camphor), camphorated (containing or treated with camphor), camphorating (the participle), and camphoric (relating to camphor); common compounds include camphor tree and camphor oil.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有准确的常用近义词。gum camphor（块状或固态樟脑）是相关传统名称；borneol（龙脑、冰片）是气味相似但化学成分不同的物质；naphthalene（萘）可用于某些防蛀产品，但不是樟脑，不能把所有俗称“樟脑丸”的产品都等同于 camphor。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday synonym. Gum camphor is a traditional related name for solid camphor; borneol is a different chemical with a similar odor; naphthalene is used in some moth-repellent products but is not camphor, so mothballs and camphor are not interchangeable terms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词绑定“樟树的强烈清凉气味”：camphor 就是樟脑。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor the whole word to the strong, penetrating scent associated with a camphor tree: camphor is the scented substance.

etymology_story.zh: 经中古英语 canker 延续自古英语 cancer，早先借自拉丁语 cancer“蟹；癌；溃疡”。英语中逐渐用于侵蚀组织的溃疡和植物病害，并引申为腐蚀社会或人心的弊病。
etymology_story.en: Canker developed through Middle English canker from Old English cancer, borrowed from Latin cancer, 'crab; cancer; ulcer'. In English it came to denote destructive sores and plant diseases, then extended figuratively to influences that corrode society or a person's inner life.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 canker 是整体词干，名词可零派生为动词。主要词族：cankers（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、cankered（过去式、过去分词；也可作形容词，意为患溃疡的、腐坏的）、cankering（现在分词）、cankerous（溃疡性的；具有腐蚀性的）；相关复合词有 canker sore（口腔溃疡）、cankerworm（尺蠖类害虫）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, canker is a whole stem, with the verb formed from the noun by conversion. The main family includes cankers (plural noun or third-person singular verb), cankered (past tense, past participle, and an adjective meaning diseased or corrupted), cankering (present participle), and cankerous (ulcerous or corrosive); related compounds include canker sore and cankerworm.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ulcer（溃疡）侧重组织表面的开放性损伤；blight（枯萎病；祸害）常强调植物迅速受损或某种广泛的破坏影响；corrode（腐蚀）作为动词强调逐步侵蚀。canker 的特点是局部病损及其持续侵蚀的意象，具体近义词应随植物、医学或比喻语境选择。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ulcer emphasizes an open lesion in tissue; blight often suggests rapid plant damage or a broadly destructive influence; corrode, as a verb, emphasizes gradual erosion. Canker characteristically evokes a localized lesion and its persistent destructive effects, so the closest alternative depends on the botanical, medical, or figurative context.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it historically with cancer: picture a damaged patch eating into bark, then extend that image to a corrupting influence; the words are not interchangeable in modern medicine.

etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word from French céphalopode, formed from Greek kephalē, meaning “head,” and pous, with the stem pod-, meaning “foot.” The name describes the arrangement of the arms or tentacles around the mouth at the head.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代科技构词：cephalo-（头）＋-pod（足；具有某种足的动物）→ cephalopod。常用相关形式：cephalopods（复数）、cephalopodan（头足类的；头足动物）；分类学名称 Cephalopoda（头足纲）使用相同词根。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern scientific formation: cephalo- (“head”) + -pod (“foot; an animal with a particular kind of foot”) → cephalopod. Related forms include cephalopods, the plural, and cephalopodan, an adjective or noun; the taxonomic name Cephalopoda uses the same roots.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cephalopodan is a technical near-equivalent. Mollusc names a broader group, while octopus names only one kind of cephalopod and cannot replace the name of the whole group.

meaning: 手性的；与镜像不能重合的

pronunciation.note: 常见读法 /ˈkaɪrəl/；开头 ch 发 /k/，第一音节含双元音 /aɪ/。

morphology.text: chir-（手） + -al（形容词后缀）→ chiral（具有左右手般镜像差异的）。

etymology.text: 由希腊语 kheir“手”配英语后缀 -al 构成。左右手看似镜像，却不能在同一方向完全叠合，是最直观的助记。

usage_note: 用于化学和几何，关键是物体与镜像不能通过旋转、平移完全重合；常见读音以 /k/ 开头。

senses.meaning_zh: 手性的；与自身镜像不能完全重合的

etymology_story.zh: chiral 由希腊语 kheir“手”和形容词后缀 -al 构成，开尔文勋爵在十九世纪末用它描述不能与镜像重合的形状。左右手互为镜像却不能完全叠合，因此成为这一几何性质的命名依据。
etymology_story.en: Chiral was formed from Greek kheir, meaning “hand,” and the adjective suffix -al; Lord Kelvin introduced it in the late nineteenth century for shapes that cannot be superimposed on their mirror images. The name draws on the relationship between the left and right hands.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：chir-（手）＋-al（形容词后缀）→ chiral。主要词族：chirality（手性）、chirally（以手性方式）、achiral（非手性的）、achirality（非手性）、homochiral（同手性的）、homochirality（同手性）、heterochiral（异手性的）、heterochirality（异手性）、prochiral（前手性的）、prochirality（前手性）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: chir- (“hand”) + -al, an adjective suffix, → chiral. The principal word family includes chirality, chirally, achiral, achirality, homochiral, homochirality, heterochiral, heterochirality, prochiral, and prochirality.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: handed（具有左右手性之分的）是直观近义表达；asymmetric（不对称的）范围更广，并非所有不对称对象都有手性；enantiomeric（对映异构的）强调两个分子互为不能重合的镜像。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Handed is an intuitive near-equivalent. Asymmetric is broader, since not every asymmetric object is chiral. Enantiomeric specifically describes the relationship between molecules that are non-superimposable mirror images.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: chir- 就是“手”：镜子能把左手变成右手的样子，却不能让两只手完全叠合。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Chir- means “hand”: your hands are mirror partners, but turning them cannot make them match exactly.

etymology_story.zh: clade 源于希腊语 klados“树枝”，在二十世纪进入现代演化生物学术语。它把谱系比作树：一个分枝连同其上全部小枝，代表一个祖先及其所有后代。
etymology_story.en: Clade comes from Greek klados, meaning “branch,” and entered modern evolutionary terminology in the twentieth century. It applies the image of a tree branch, including every smaller branch growing from it, to an ancestor and all its descendants.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 clade 是不可再按常见英语词缀拆分的名词，复数为 clades。相关词族共享 clad-／clado-（分枝）词根：cladistic（支序分类的）、cladistics（支序分类学）、cladistically（按支序分类方法）、cladogram（支序图）、cladogenesis（分支演化）、cladogenetic（分支演化的）；这些词不宜全部机械地分析成 clade 加后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, clade is a simple noun with the plural clades. Related words share the root clad- or clado-, meaning “branch”: cladistic, cladistics, cladistically, cladogram, cladogenesis, and cladogenetic. These are related root formations, rather than all being straightforward suffix additions to clade.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: monophyletic group（单系群）是严格对应的术语；lineage（谱系）侧重祖先到后代的传承线，不一定涵盖全部分枝；taxon（分类单元）是更宽泛的分类名称，不一定构成演化支。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Monophyletic group is the precise equivalent. Lineage emphasizes a line of descent and need not include every branch. Taxon is a broader classification term and does not necessarily identify a clade.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Circle one whole branch of the tree of life: include its starting point and every twig.

etymology_story.zh: gigolo 借自法语，通常被解释为由 gigolette 逆构而成；后者曾指年轻女子或舞伴，相关词源与跳舞有关。英语中的用法逐渐集中于接受女性报酬或经济供养的男性伴侣。

In English, its meaning became centred on a male companion paid or financially supported by a woman.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 gigolo 是整体借入的单纯词，没有可供常规拆解的英语词根和词缀；复数为 gigolos。它没有常用的派生词族，不宜为了补全词族而把罕见的临时造词当作常用词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, gigolo is a simple borrowed word with no productive English root-and-affix breakdown; its plural is gigolos. It has no established common family of derivatives, so rare occasional formations should not be presented as everyday vocabulary.

etymology_story.zh: gonad 来自科学拉丁语 gonas（词干 gonad-），最终源于希腊语 gonos“生育、后代、种子”。它先用于指产生生殖细胞的器官，后来在非正式英语中专指睾丸，复数又可进一步引申为“胆量”。
etymology_story.en: Gonad comes from scientific Latin gonas, with the stem gonad-, ultimately from Greek gonos, meaning “generation, offspring, or seed.” It names an organ producing reproductive cells; informal English later used it specifically for the testicles and extended the plural to mean courage.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词以 gonad 为词基：gonad＋-al → gonadal（性腺的），复数 gonads。主要相关词族：gonadectomy（性腺切除术）、gonadotropin／gonadotrophin（促性腺激素）、gonadotropic／gonadotrophic（促性腺的）、gonadogenesis（性腺发生）、hypogonadism（性腺功能减退）、hypogonadal（性腺功能减退的）、hypergonadism（性腺功能亢进）、hypergonadal（性腺功能亢进的）、gonadotoxic（对性腺有毒的）、gonadotoxicity（性腺毒性）。复合词中常用连接形式 gonado-。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formations use gonad as a base: gonad + -al → gonadal; the plural is gonads. Principal related forms include gonadectomy, gonadotropin or gonadotrophin, gonadotropic or gonadotrophic, gonadogenesis, hypogonadism, hypogonadal, hypergonadism, hypergonadal, gonadotoxic, and gonadotoxicity. Compounds commonly use the combining form gonado-.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sex gland（性腺）是常见对应表达；ovary（卵巢）特指产生卵细胞的性腺；testis（睾丸）特指产生精子的性腺。俚语“胆量”义则接近 guts，而不是这些解剖学名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sex gland is a common equivalent. Ovary specifies an egg-producing gonad, while testis specifies a sperm-producing gonad. In the slang sense of courage, gonads is close to guts rather than to these anatomical terms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“生殖种子”的来源：性腺就是制造卵细胞或精子的器官。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to reproductive “seed”: a gonad is an organ that makes eggs or sperm.

etymology_story.zh: 经中古英语和盎格鲁法语 manicle，最终源于拉丁语 manicula，后者是 manus（手）的指小形式。词义从与手有关的器具发展为腕部镣铐，并引申为剥夺自由的束缚。
etymology_story.en: Through Middle English and Anglo-French manicle, the word ultimately comes from Latin manicula, a diminutive of manus, meaning 'hand.' Its meaning developed into a restraint for the wrists and extended figuratively to restrictions on freedom.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 manacle 是不可再按常用英语词缀拆分的词基，名词可直接转作动词。词形与词族：manacles（复数名词或动词第三人称单数）、manacled（过去式、过去分词，也可作形容词，意为“戴着手铐的；受束缚的”）、manacling（现在分词）；另有较少见的 unmanacle（解开手铐）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, manacle is a base without a productive internal English affix structure; the noun also functions as a verb through conversion. Forms and family members include manacles, manacled, and manacling; manacled also has adjectival use, meaning 'restrained with manacles' or 'restricted.' The less common verb unmanacle means 'to remove manacles from.'

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: handcuff（手铐；给……戴手铐）是现代日常及执法用语；shackle（镣铐；给……上镣铐）可涉及手腕或脚踝，也常比喻束缚；fetter（脚镣；束缚）原指脚部镣铐，现代比喻用法较突出。manacle 尤其指腕部束具，语体较正式或带历史色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Handcuff is the usual modern everyday and policing term; shackle can refer to restraints on wrists or ankles and is common figuratively; fetter originally refers to a restraint for the feet and is now prominent in figurative use. Manacle particularly suggests a wrist restraint and often has a formal or historical tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住历史词根 manus（手）：铐住手，就是 manacle；限制自由，就是抽象的“手铐”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to historical manus, 'hand': a manacle holds the hands, and figurative manacles hold back freedom.

etymology_story.zh: 借自拉丁语 opprobrium（责难、耻辱），由 ob-（向着、针对）与 probrum（可耻之事、责难）构成，其中前缀发生了辅音同化。英语保留了“受到谴责”以及“因此蒙受耻辱”这两个相连的意义。
etymology_story.en: Borrowed from Latin opprobrium, meaning 'reproach' or 'disgrace,' the word combines ob-, 'towards' or 'against,' with probrum, 'a disgraceful act' or 'reproach,' with consonant assimilation in the prefix. English preserves both the condemnation and the resulting disgrace.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 opprobrium 通常作为完整的借入词处理，不宜把 -ium 当作可自由造词的普通英语后缀。主要词族：opprobrious（辱骂的；招致耻辱的）、opprobriously（辱骂地；可耻地）、opprobriousness（辱骂性；可耻性，少见）；opprobrium 通常为不可数名词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats opprobrium as a whole borrowed base; -ium is not a freely productive ordinary English suffix here. Its main family includes opprobrious, meaning 'abusive' or 'disgraceful,' opprobriously, and the uncommon noun opprobriousness. Opprobrium is normally uncountable.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: condemnation（谴责）强调明确而强烈的否定判断；obloquy（公众的辱骂、诋毁）更突出言语攻击；disgrace（耻辱）强调名誉受损的状态。opprobrium 把公众鄙斥与道德上的羞耻紧密联系起来。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Condemnation emphasizes an explicit, strongly negative judgment; obloquy highlights public verbal abuse or denunciation; disgrace emphasizes the resulting loss of honour. Opprobrium closely links public disapproval with moral shame.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 以“责难 → 公愤 → 耻辱”为意义链：opprobrium 是众人的谴责及其留下的恶名。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the chain 'reproach → public condemnation → disgrace': opprobrium is the blame people direct at someone and the shame it brings.

senses.meaning_zh: 半官方机构；独立运作的国有或国家控股企业
senses.meaning_en: An organization or enterprise owned or controlled by the state and operated with some independence.
senses.english_definition: A parastatal is an organization that the government owns or controls but that operates separately from its ordinary departments.
senses.collocation_en: reform parastatals; a loss-making parastatal
senses.collocation_zh: 改革国有或半官方机构；一家亏损的国有或国家控股企业
senses.sentence_en: Several parastatals depend on annual government subsidies.
senses.sentence_zh: 几家由国家控制的独立运营机构依赖政府每年的补贴。

etymology_story.zh: 这是20世纪形成的行政用语，由源自希腊语、表示“在旁”的 para- 与表示“国家的”的 statal 构成。它描写位于政府行政体系旁侧、与国家保持所有权或控制关系的机构，并非专指国家持股恰好一半的企业。
etymology_story.en: This twentieth-century administrative term combines Greek-derived para-, meaning 'alongside,' with statal, meaning 'of the state.' It describes bodies operating alongside government administration while remaining linked to state ownership or control, without specifying a particular ownership percentage.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：para-（在旁、与……并行）+ statal（国家的）；statal 可分析为 stat(e)（国家）+ -al（形容词后缀）。parastatal 可由形容词直接转作可数名词，复数为 parastatals；相关词有 state（国家）和 statal（国家的），直接派生词较少。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: para-, 'alongside,' + statal, 'of the state'; statal can be analyzed as stat(e) + the adjective suffix -al. Parastatal also becomes a count noun through conversion, with the plural parastatals. Related words include state and statal; direct derivatives are limited.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: state-owned（国有的）明确强调所有权；state-controlled（国家控制的）强调控制权，不必等于完全所有；quasi-governmental（半官方的）强调与政府有关联但保持一定独立性。parastatal 通常兼有国家所有或控制与独立运营的含义，具体制度因国家而异。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: State-owned explicitly concerns ownership; state-controlled concerns control, which need not involve complete ownership; quasi-governmental emphasizes a government connection with some institutional independence. Parastatal usually combines state ownership or control with separate operation, although arrangements vary by country.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: para-＝在旁，statal＝国家的：在政府“旁边”独立运作，背后仍有国家。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Para- means 'alongside' and statal means 'of the state': picture an organization beside the government, with the state still behind it.

usage_note: 常见 phenolic compounds 和 phenolic resin；有这种化学结构不代表一定有益或有害，须看具体物质。

etymology_story.zh: 由19世纪化学命名中的 phenol（酚）加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，最初表示“与酚有关的”。随着酚类化学和合成树脂工业的发展，该词也用作名词，指酚类物质或酚醛树脂材料。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed by adding the adjective suffix -ic to phenol, a name from nineteenth-century chemical nomenclature, to mean 'relating to phenol.' As phenol chemistry and synthetic resins developed, phenolic also became a noun for phenolic compounds and resin materials.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：phenol（酚）+ -ic（……的）→ phenolic；名词用法由形容词转化而来，复数为 phenolics。主要相关词族：phenol（酚）、phenolate（酚盐；酚氧负离子）、phenolic（酚的；酚类物质）、polyphenol（多酚）、polyphenolic（多酚的）、polyphenols（多酚，复数）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: phenol + -ic, 'relating to,' → phenolic; the noun arises through conversion and has the plural phenolics. The main related family includes phenol, phenolate, meaning a phenol-derived salt or anion, phenolic, polyphenol, polyphenolic, and the plural polyphenols.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: phenol-derived（酚衍生的）强调来源，衍生物不一定保留酚羟基；phenol-containing（含酚的）强调含有酚，但不必与 phenolic 的结构意义完全一致；polyphenolic（多酚的）范围更窄，通常涉及多个酚羟基。phenolic 是较广泛的结构或材料类别用语，这些表达不能处处互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Phenol-derived emphasizes origin, and a derivative need not retain a phenolic hydroxyl group; phenol-containing emphasizes the presence of phenol rather than necessarily describing molecular structure; polyphenolic is narrower and generally involves multiple phenolic hydroxyl groups. Phenolic is a broader structural or materials term, so these expressions are not universally interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: phenol 是“酚”，加 -ic 就是“酚的”；形容词名词化后，可指酚类物质或酚醛材料。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with phenol and add -ic: 'relating to phenol.' Used as a noun, it names a phenolic compound or resin material.

etymology_story.zh: 源自中古英语 pikois 等形式，进一步来自古法语 picois（一种尖头挖掘工具）。后来英语使用者将其与 pick 和 axe 联系起来，改造了词形，形成现代拼写 pickaxe；其中 axe 是后来的民间词源联想。
etymology_story.en: The word descends from Middle English forms such as pikois, from Old French picois, a pointed digging tool. English speakers later reshaped it through association with pick and axe, producing pickaxe; the axe element reflects folk etymology.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可按重新分析的复合结构 pick（尖头挖掘工具）+ axe（斧）理解，但这不等于它最初的历史构词方式。名词直接转作动词；词形有 pickaxes、pickaxed、pickaxing；美式英语另有拼写 pickax，相应形式为 pickaxes、pickaxed、pickaxing。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern speakers can interpret it as the reanalyzed compound pick + axe, although that is not its original historical formation. The noun converts directly into a verb; forms include pickaxes, pickaxed, and pickaxing. The alternative American spelling pickax has the corresponding forms pickaxes, pickaxed, and pickaxing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pick（镐）在挖掘工具语境中常可直接替代 pickaxe；mattock（鹤嘴锄、十字镐）通常有较宽的锄刃，用于刨土和断根；axe（斧）主要靠刃口劈砍木材。pickaxe 的突出特点是用尖头击破坚硬地面或岩石。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pick is often interchangeable with pickaxe in digging contexts; a mattock typically has a broad digging blade for working soil and cutting roots; an axe mainly chops wood with a cutting edge. A pickaxe is especially associated with using a pointed head to break hard ground or rock.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把现代词形看成 pick 的尖头加 axe 的挥砍动作：挥起尖头重工具，凿开硬地。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the modern spelling as a hook: the point of a pick plus the swinging action of an axe breaks hard ground.

meaning: 装腔作势的人；故作姿态者

morphology.text: 法语 pos-（poser“摆姿态”的词干） + -eur（做某事的人）→ poseur（故作姿态者）。

etymology.text: 借自法语 poseur，与 poser“摆姿势”有关。把一心摆出某种形象、却没有实际内涵的人作为记忆画面。

usage_note: 含贬义，通常指为博取印象而假装有某种品位、知识或身份。

senses.meaning_zh: 装腔作势的人；故作高深或冒充内行的人
senses.meaning_en: Someone who pretends to have qualities, interests, or knowledge in order to impress others.
senses.english_definition: A poseur is someone who behaves as if they have particular qualities or interests, usually to impress people, although they do not really have them.
senses.collocation_en: an intellectual poseur; a pretentious poseur
senses.collocation_zh: 冒充知识分子的人；装腔作势的人

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 poseur，原指摆姿势或故作姿态的人，来自 poser“放置；摆姿势”。英语沿用了其贬义，用来指刻意营造某种形象却缺乏相应内涵的人。
etymology_story.en: Borrowed from French poseur, meaning someone who poses or adopts an affected manner, from poser, 'to place; to pose.' English retained its disapproving sense of someone cultivating an impressive image without the substance to support it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 poseur 作为完整借词处理；其法语内部结构为 pos-（poser 的词干，摆姿势）+ -eur（施事者后缀）。常用复数为 poseurs；相关英语词有 pose（姿势；摆姿势）、posed（摆好的；摆过姿势的）、posing（摆姿势）和 poser（故作姿态者；另可指难题），但它们并非全部由 poseur 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, poseur is normally treated as a whole borrowed word; its French structure is pos-, the stem of poser, 'to pose,' + the agent suffix -eur. Its regular plural is poseurs. Related English forms include pose, posed, posing, and poser, although these are not all derivatives of poseur.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: poser：最接近的常用近义词，但也可表示“难题”；pretender：强调冒称某种身份、能力或资格；show-off：强调炫耀，所炫耀的本领可能真实存在，而 poseur 更突出形象与实际不符。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Poser is the closest everyday equivalent, though it can also mean a difficult question. Pretender emphasizes a false claim to an identity, ability, or entitlement. Show-off emphasizes attention-seeking display, which may involve real abilities, whereas poseur stresses an inauthentic image.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 pose“摆姿势”联想：姿态摆得足，内涵未必有。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of pose: a poseur strikes the impressive pose without necessarily having the substance.

etymology_story.zh: Pyrex 是康宁于1915年推出的玻璃产品商标。其名称通常被解释为与 pie“派”及玻璃品牌常见的 -ex 结尾有关；后来，这个商标也被用来指该品牌的玻璃器皿。
etymology_story.en: Pyrex was introduced by Corning in 1915 as a trademark for glass products. Its name is commonly explained as referring to pie, together with the -ex ending used in glass brand names; the trademark subsequently also came to denote the brand's glassware.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 Pyrex 是不可按普通词根、词缀规则拆解的品牌名称，不宜把它分析为具有稳定意义的 pie + r + -ex。没有常用的规则派生词族；常见组合有 Pyrex glass（派热克斯玻璃）、Pyrex dish（派热克斯烤盘）和 Pyrex glassware（派热克斯玻璃器皿）。Pyrex dish 中的 Pyrex 是名词作前置修饰语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Pyrex is an indivisible brand name rather than a transparent root-and-affix formation; pie + r + -ex is not a productive morphological formula. It has no common regular derivative family. Frequent combinations include Pyrex glass, Pyrex dish, and Pyrex glassware. In Pyrex dish, the brand name functions as a noun modifier.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: heat-resistant glass（耐热玻璃）是材料类别，范围比 Pyrex 广；ovenproof glassware（可用于烤箱的玻璃器皿）按用途分类，不限定品牌；borosilicate glass（硼硅酸盐玻璃）按成分分类，与部分 Pyrex 产品有关，但不能与整个品牌画等号。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Heat-resistant glass is a broader material category. Ovenproof glassware describes glassware by its intended use without specifying a brand. Borosilicate glass describes a composition associated with some Pyrex products, but it is not an exact synonym for the entire brand.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 Pyrex 与一个盛着 pie“派”的玻璃烤盘联系起来，记住它是品牌名。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a pie in a Pyrex baking dish, and remember that Pyrex names the brand.

meaning: 科学至上主义（认为科学是获得一切知识的唯一途径）
aliases: 科学至上主义（认为科学是获得一切知识的唯一途径）

pronunciation.note: 采用英式常见读法；重音按音标中的 ˈ 标记。

forms: 本课作为观点名称，通常不可数。
family: science 科学；scientistic 科学至上主义的。

morphology.text: scient-（科学，见 scientific） + -ism（主义）→ scientism（科学至上主义）。

etymology.text: 英语用源自拉丁语 scientia“知识”的 scient- 加 -ism 构成。它把“科学”推成包办一切问题的主张。

usage_note: 常用于哲学批评；支持科学研究不等于持有 scientism，重点在是否声称科学独占一切知识途径。

etymology_story.zh: 这是19世纪出现的英语构词，由与 science“科学”相关的 scient- 加 -ism 构成，最终可追溯至拉丁语 scientia“知识”。它早期可指科学特有的做法或表达，后来常带批评意味，指对科学权威或适用范围的过度推崇。
etymology_story.en: This nineteenth-century English formation combines scient-, associated with science, and -ism, ultimately drawing on Latin scientia, 'knowledge.' Earlier uses could refer to practices or expressions characteristic of science; later usage often became critical, describing excessive claims for scientific authority or scope.

morphology_enriched.zh: scient-（与科学、知识相关的词干）+ -ism（学说、主义）→ scientism。直接相关派生词有 scientistic（科学主义的）和 scientistically（以科学主义的方式）；更广的词族包括 science（科学）、scientist（科学家）、scientific（科学的）、scientifically（科学地）和 unscientific（不科学的）。Scientist 本身不表示“科学主义者”。
morphology_enriched.en: Scient- (a stem associated with science or knowledge) + -ism (a doctrine or outlook) forms scientism. Directly related derivatives include scientistic and scientistically. The broader family includes science, scientist, scientific, scientifically, and unscientific. Scientist does not itself mean an advocate of scientism.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: scientific imperialism（科学帝国主义）是相关批评用语，强调科学方法向其他领域扩张；scientific reductionism（科学还原论）强调用较基础层次的科学解释复杂现象；positivism（实证主义）强调经验性知识与验证。这些概念与 scientism 有交集，但并非完全同义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Scientific imperialism is a related critical term emphasizing the expansion of scientific methods into other domains. Scientific reductionism emphasizes explaining complex phenomena through more basic scientific processes. Positivism emphasizes empirical knowledge and verification. These concepts overlap with scientism but are not exact synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: science 加上 -ism：把科学提升为包办所有知识问题的主义。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Science plus -ism: science elevated into a doctrine claiming authority over every kind of knowledge.

etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word in the sixteenth century through French forms such as cimeterre, related to Italian scimitarra; its earlier origin is uncertain. In European usage, it became a general name for various curved swords associated with the Middle East and neighboring regions.

morphology_enriched.zh: scimitar 在现代英语中是不可进一步分析的借词，不应拆成具有虚构意义的词根。复数为 scimitars；常见复合形式有 scimitar-shaped（弯刀形的）、scimitar-like（似弯刀的）和 scimitar-toothed（长着弯刀状牙齿的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Scimitar is a morphologically indivisible loanword in modern English and should not be split into invented meaningful roots. Its plural is scimitars. Established descriptive compounds include scimitar-shaped, scimitar-like, and scimitar-toothed.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sabre（马刀）通常指单刃、常有弧度的军用刀剑，尤其与骑兵有关；cutlass（短弯刀）刀身较短而宽，常与水手有关；sword（剑；刀剑）是上位词，既可指直刃也可指弯刃武器。Scimitar 更突出其弯刃外形及中东文化关联。

Sword is the broader category and includes both straight and curved weapons. Scimitar particularly evokes a curved blade and Middle Eastern associations.

meaning: 正是同一个的；完全同一的

pronunciation.note: 采用英式常见读法；重音按音标中的 ˈ 标记。

forms: 形容词，不分比较级。
family: self 本身；same 同一的。

morphology.text: self（本身） + same（同一的）→ selfsame（正是同一个的）。

etymology.text: 源于中古英语 self same，把 self 与 same 连用来加强“就是同一个”的意思，后来连写。想象在照片里认出当年那把椅子。

usage_note: 偏书面、文学，常用 the selfsame，强调对象身份完全相同而非仅仅相似。

senses.meaning_zh: 正是同一个的；完全相同的，常用于强调，带文学色彩
senses.meaning_en: Exactly the same, used for emphasis, especially in literary language.
senses.english_definition: You use selfsame to emphasize that something is exactly the same person or thing as one already mentioned.
senses.collocation_en: the selfsame place; the selfsame day
senses.collocation_zh: 正是同一个地方；就在同一天
senses.sentence_en: Years later, she returned to the selfsame village where they had first met.
senses.sentence_zh: 多年以后，她回到了他们初次相遇的那个村庄，正是同一个地方。

etymology_story.zh: 源于中古英语中 self 与 same 的连用，当时 self 可用于加强“本身；正是”的意思。两词后来合写，保留了对“恰好就是同一个”的强调，现代多见于文学性或刻意郑重的表达。
etymology_story.en: The word developed from the Middle English combination of self and same, with self serving as an intensifier meaning 'very' or 'itself.' The combination became a single word retaining emphatic identity, now chiefly used in literary or deliberately formal expression.

morphology_enriched.zh: self（本身；用作强调）+ same（相同的）→ selfsame。这是形容词复合词，通常置于名词前，常与 the 连用；没有常用的直接派生词族，一般不用于比较级或最高级。相关基础词有 self（自我；自身）和 same（相同的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Self (used emphatically, 'itself' or 'very') + same forms the compound adjective selfsame. It usually appears before a noun, commonly after the, and has no common direct derivative family or ordinary comparative and superlative forms. Its related base words are self and same.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: same（同一个的；相同的）是中性常用词；identical（完全相同的）常强调特征毫无差别，但两个 identical objects 仍可指两件不同物品；very 在 the very same 等结构中强调“正是”。Selfsame 通常更强调同一人或同一事物的身份连续性，并带文学色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Same is the neutral everyday term. Identical often emphasizes an exact match in characteristics, although two identical objects can still be separate things. Very adds emphasis in expressions such as the very same. Selfsame usually stresses the identity of the particular person or thing and carries a literary tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: self“它本身”+ same“同一个”：就是原来的那一个。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Self plus same: the very thing itself, exactly the one encountered before.

morphology.text: thalam-（thalamus 的词干） + -ic → thalamic（丘脑的）；thalamus 本身作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 经拉丁语 thalamus 借入，源于希腊语 thalamos“内室”。用脑部深处的一个“内室”帮助记位置，但丘脑并不是空腔。

usage_note: 神经解剖学术语；与下丘脑 hypothalamus 不同。丘脑是成对结构，参与感觉等信息的传递。

senses.meaning_zh: 丘脑；脑内参与感觉信息中继、运动调节和意识活动的结构
senses.meaning_en: a brain structure involved in relaying sensory information, regulating movement, and supporting consciousness
senses.english_definition: The thalamus is a structure deep inside the brain that helps pass information to the cerebral cortex and supports functions such as movement, attention, and consciousness.
senses.collocation_en: the human thalamus; thalamus and cortex
senses.collocation_zh: 人类丘脑；丘脑与大脑皮层

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 thalamus，最终来自希腊语 thalamos，意为“内室、寝室”。这个古老的空间名称后来用于脑部深处的解剖结构；丘脑本身是神经组织，并非空腔。
etymology_story.en: The word comes through Latin thalamus from Greek thalamos, meaning an inner chamber or bedchamber. This old spatial term was later applied to a structure deep in the brain; the thalamus itself is neural tissue, not a hollow chamber.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为完整的医学词基使用，不宜拆成普通英语词缀。词干 thalam- + -ic → thalamic（丘脑的）；复数为 thalami。主要相关构词包括 thalamocortical（丘脑与大脑皮层的）、intrathalamic（丘脑内的）和 thalamotomy（丘脑切开术）；hypothalamus（下丘脑）和 epithalamus（上丘脑）是共享词源的相关解剖名称。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, thalamus functions as a complete medical base rather than a combination of ordinary English affixes. The stem thalam- + -ic gives thalamic; the plural is thalami. Major related formations include thalamocortical, intrathalamic, and thalamotomy; hypothalamus and epithalamus are related anatomical names sharing the same historical base.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有常用的严格同义词。optic thalamus 是较旧的名称；sensory relay center（感觉中继中心）是功能描述，不能涵盖丘脑的全部作用；diencephalon（间脑）是包含丘脑在内的更大脑区，不能互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym. Optic thalamus is an older name; sensory relay center describes a function without covering all thalamic functions; diencephalon names the larger brain region that contains the thalamus and is not interchangeable with it.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “内室”提示深处的位置：脑深处的信息中继站；记位置，不把它想成空房间。
mnemonic_anchor.en: “Inner chamber” cues its deep location: an information relay deep in the brain. Remember the location without imagining an empty room.
