etymology_story.zh: vernal 于十六世纪进入英语，借自拉丁语 vernalis，最终源于表示“春天”的 ver。英语由季节本义发展出“清新、年轻”的文学比喻义。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/vernal)
etymology_story.en: Vernal entered English in the sixteenth century from Latin vernalis, ultimately based on ver, meaning spring. Its seasonal meaning also developed literary associations with freshness and youth. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/vernal)

morphology_enriched.zh: 学习构词可分析为 vern-（拉丁语来源的黏着词根，表示“春”）+ -al（形容词后缀）；整词在历史上是借入词。主要词族：vernally（在春季；如春天般地）、vernalize/vernalise（使春化）、vernalization/vernalisation（春化作用）、devernalize/devernalise（使去春化）、devernalization/devernalisation（去春化作用）；vernality（春日特性；青春活力）较少见。
morphology_enriched.en: For learning purposes, analyze vernal as vern-, a Latin-derived bound root meaning spring, + adjectival -al; historically, the whole adjective was borrowed. The principal family includes vernally, meaning in spring or in a springlike manner; vernalize/vernalise and vernalization/vernalisation, referring to inducing flowering through cold treatment; and devernalize/devernalise and devernalization/devernalisation, referring to reversing that effect. Vernality, meaning springlike character or youthful vitality, is uncommon.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: spring（春季的，用作名词定语）最日常，如 spring flowers；springlike（像春天的）强调具有春天的感觉，不限定实际季节；youthful（年轻的、显年轻的）对应 vernal 的比喻义，不带明确的季节含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Spring, used as a noun modifier, is the everyday choice, as in spring flowers; springlike describes spring's qualities even outside that season; youthful overlaps with the figurative sense of vernal without necessarily suggesting a season.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: vern-＝春 → 春季的；春意味着新生 → 清新、有青春活力。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Vern- means spring: the season gives the literal meaning, and spring's renewal gives freshness and youth.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 anaphylaxis 出现于二十世纪初，通过医学拉丁语与法语 anaphylaxie 相联系。这个名称仿照 prophylaxis（预防、防护）构成，用来表达与预期保护作用相反的过敏现象。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/anaphylaxis)
etymology_story.en: Anaphylaxis appeared in English in the early twentieth century through medical Latin, with a connection to French anaphylaxie. The term was modeled on prophylaxis, meaning prevention or protection, to name a hypersensitive response contrary to the protection expected. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/anaphylaxis)

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是含希腊语来源成分的医学构词：ana- + phylaxis（防护）；“与防护相反”是历史命名线索，不表示 ana- 在所有词中都意为“相反”。主要词族：anaphylactic（严重过敏反应的）、anaphylactically（以严重过敏反应的方式）；形容词采用 anaphylact- 词干加 -ic，副词再加 -ally。专业复数为 anaphylaxes；anaphylactoid（类过敏反应的）是相关的传统医学术语。
morphology_enriched.en: This medical formation contains Greek-derived ana- + phylaxis, meaning protection. The contrast with protection explains the historical naming, rather than establishing opposite as the meaning of ana- in every word. Principal derivatives are anaphylactic, relating to anaphylaxis, and anaphylactically, in an anaphylactic manner: the adjective uses anaphylact- + -ic, followed by -ally for the adverb. The specialist plural is anaphylaxes; anaphylactoid, meaning resembling anaphylaxis, is a related traditional medical term.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: severe systemic allergic reaction（严重全身性过敏反应）是解释性近义表达；allergic reaction（过敏反应）范围更广，也包括轻微反应；anaphylactic shock（过敏性休克）指伴有循环衰竭的严重情况，并非所有 anaphylaxis 都发展为休克。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Severe systemic allergic reaction is an explanatory near-equivalent; allergic reaction is broader and includes mild reactions; anaphylactic shock describes anaphylaxis with circulatory failure, so anaphylaxis does not always involve shock.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 以“防护的反面”记名称：身体遇到某种物质后，出现危险的全身过敏反应。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the naming contrast with protection: exposure produces a dangerous systemic allergic response.

etymology_story.zh: 浓汤义于十七世纪借自法语 bisque，更早来源尚无定论；甜点义也见于英语词典。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bisque) 陶瓷义另由 biscuit（素烧陶瓷）缩略变化而来，并关联颜色义及相应形容词；运动让分义也是来自法语的同形词。[柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/bisque)
etymology_story.en: The soup word was borrowed from French bisque in the seventeenth century, with its earlier origin uncertain; dictionaries also record the dessert sense. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bisque) The ceramic word developed separately as an alteration of biscuit, meaning unglazed fired ware, and is associated with the color noun and adjective; the sporting allowance is another French-derived homonym. [Collins Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/bisque)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 bisque 是完整词基，不宜把浓汤义强拆为 bis- 加其他成分。陶艺动词由名词零派生，屈折形式为 bisques、bisqued、bisquing；名词复数为 bisques。常见相关构词有 bisqueware（素烧陶器）、bisque-fired（经过素烧的）和 bisque firing（素烧工序）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern bisque is a complete base; the soup word should not be forced into a bis- plus remainder analysis. The pottery verb is formed by conversion from the noun and inflects as bisques, bisqued, and bisquing; the noun plural is bisques. Related formations include bisqueware, meaning unglazed fired pottery; bisque-fired, meaning having undergone a bisque firing; and bisque firing, the firing process.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 浓汤义：cream soup（奶油浓汤）强调奶油或乳脂口感，puréed soup（泥状浓汤）强调食材打成泥，chowder（杂烩浓汤）通常保留明显食材块。陶瓷义的 biscuit ware（素烧陶器）接近对应；颜色义的 beige（米色）通常不突出粉色；动词义可用 bisque-fire（素烧）表达；运动义属于 handicap allowance（让分或让击优惠）的一种。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For soup, cream soup emphasizes cream or creaminess, puréed soup emphasizes blended ingredients, and chowder usually contains recognizable chunks. In ceramics, biscuit ware is a close equivalent; for color, beige does not specifically emphasize a pink tint. The verb can be expressed as bisque-fire, while the sporting noun names a particular handicap allowance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 分两条主线记：餐桌上的细滑浓汤；窑炉中的无釉素瓷及其浅粉棕色。运动义另记为“给较弱者一次额外机会”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep two main images: smooth soup on the table, and unglazed pottery with its pale tan coloring. Remember the sporting homonym separately as an extra opportunity for the weaker player.

senses.meaning_en: a cage-shaped fullerene molecule, especially the sixty-carbon molecule C₆₀
senses.english_definition: A buckyball is a molecule whose carbon atoms form a hollow cage, especially the roughly spherical molecule containing sixty carbon atoms.

senses.sentence_zh: 一个 C₆₀ 巴克球含有六十个碳原子，这些原子排列成中空的笼状结构。

etymology_story.zh: buckyball 出现于二十世纪八十年代，名称关联建筑师 R. Buckminster Fuller，Bucky 是其昵称。球笼状分子的结构让人联想到与富勒相关的测地穹顶，因此形成了这个形象化名称。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/buckyball)
etymology_story.en: Buckyball appeared in the 1980s and draws its name from architect R. Buckminster Fuller, known as Bucky. The molecular cage suggested the geodesic domes associated with Fuller, inspiring the visual name. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/buckyball)

morphology_enriched.zh: Bucky（人名昵称，用作命名成分）+ ball（球）→ buckyball，是复合名词；复数为 buckyballs，没有常用的固定后缀派生词。相关命名词包括 buckminsterfullerene（巴克明斯特富勒烯，通常指 C₆₀）、fullerene（富勒烯，较广的类别名称）和 buckytube（巴克管，即碳纳米管的别称）；这些是相关词，不全是 buckyball 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Bucky, a personal nickname used as a naming element, + ball forms the compound noun buckyball. Its plural is buckyballs, and it has no common established suffix derivatives. Related names include buckminsterfullerene, usually referring to C₆₀; fullerene, the broader category; and buckytube, another name for a carbon nanotube. These are related terms rather than all being direct derivatives of buckyball.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: buckminsterfullerene（巴克明斯特富勒烯）在指 C₆₀ 时最精确；C60 molecule（C₆₀ 分子）直接说明分子组成；fullerene（富勒烯）范围更广，还包括其他大小和形状的封闭碳笼分子。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Buckminsterfullerene is the precise equivalent when C₆₀ is intended; C60 molecule states the molecular composition directly; fullerene is broader and includes closed carbon cages of other sizes and shapes.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Bucky 的穹顶 + ball 的球形 → 碳原子搭成的微型空心球笼。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bucky's dome + ball → a tiny hollow cage built from carbon atoms.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经西班牙语 cacique 借自泰诺语中表示首领的词，最初用于加勒比地区的原住民领袖。后来，它也指西班牙和拉丁美洲的地方政治头目，并被用作某类热带美洲鸟的名称。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through Spanish cacique, from a Taíno word for a chief, originally referring to Indigenous Caribbean leaders. It later acquired the meaning of a local political boss in Spain and Latin America and also became a name for certain tropical American birds.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，cacique 是不可进一步拆分的借入词干，不宜按英语前后缀硬拆。相关形式：caciques（复数）；caciquism（地方头人政治，cacique 去掉末尾 e 加 -ism）；caciquismo（同义的西班牙语借词）；caciquist（头人政治的支持者；与头人政治有关的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cacique is an unanalyzed borrowed base rather than a combination of English roots and affixes. Related forms include caciques, the plural; caciquism, political domination by local bosses, formed by dropping final e and adding -ism; caciquismo, a related Spanish borrowing; and caciquist, a supporter of or adjective relating to this system.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chief（首领）范围最广；chieftain（部族首领）更突出传统部族组织；political boss（政治头目）对应其政治引申义，强调对地方政治的实际控制。鸟类义没有可直接替换的通用近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chief is the broadest term for a leader; chieftain particularly suggests traditional tribal leadership; political boss matches the extended political sense and emphasizes practical control over local politics. The bird sense has no interchangeable general synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“地方首领”：从原住民首领延伸到地方政治头目；鸟名义另行关联。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor the word to a local chief: an Indigenous leader becomes, by extension, a local political boss; learn the bird name separately.

etymology_story.zh: clomp 是模仿沉重脚步声形成的词，与同样可以表示脚步沉重地行走的 clump 密切相关。它的声音形式直接表现鞋靴落地时的沉重响声。
etymology_story.en: Clomp is an imitative word closely related to clump, which can also mean to walk heavily. Its sound evokes the heavy impact of footwear striking the ground.

morphology_enriched.zh: clomp 是独立的拟声词根，名词和动词同形。词形包括 clomps（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、clomped（过去式及过去分词）、clomping（现在分词或动名词）；较少见的 clomper = clomp + -er，指脚步沉重的人。
morphology_enriched.en: Clomp is an independent imitative base used as both a noun and a verb. Its forms are clomps, the plural noun or third-person singular verb; clomped, the past tense and past participle; and clomping, the present participle or gerund. The less common derivative clomper combines clomp with -er to mean someone who walks heavily.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: clump（脚步沉重地走）与 clomp 很接近；stomp（跺脚；重步走）常带用力或生气的意味；trudge（艰难地走）强调疲惫和费力，不一定强调声音。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Clump is very close in meaning to clomp; stomp often suggests deliberate force or anger; trudge emphasizes tiredness and effort without necessarily suggesting noise.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 读出 clomp，想象厚靴“咚”地落地：既是沉重地走，也是那一声脚步。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Say clomp and picture a heavy boot hitting the floor: the word names both the noisy movement and the sound.

etymology_story.zh: cotta 借自意大利语 cotta，可追溯至中世纪拉丁语中表示外衣或袍子的 cotta，其更早来源通常被认为属于日耳曼语衣物词系。原本较宽泛的衣物名称，在英语中专指一种短式白色礼拜服。
etymology_story.en: Cotta comes from Italian cotta, going back to Medieval Latin cotta, a coat or tunic, generally traced further to a Germanic garment word. In English, this broader clothing term became specialized as the name of a short white liturgical garment.

morphology_enriched.zh: cotta 是整体借入的名词，现代英语中没有可分析的常用前后缀。常用屈折形式为 cotta + -s → cottas（复数）；没有通行的英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Cotta is a borrowed noun with no productive internal division into modern English roots and affixes. Its regular plural is cotta + -s → cottas; it has no established productive family of English derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: surplice（白色罩衣）是上位近义词，cotta 通常指较短的款式；rochet（小白衣）是相关但不同的礼拜服，通常袖子较窄；alb（白长衣）通常长及脚踝，不能与 cotta 直接互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Surplice is the broader near-synonym, with cotta usually naming a shorter version; a rochet is a related but distinct vestment, generally with narrower sleeves; an alb is normally ankle-length and is not interchangeable with cotta.

etymology_story.zh: cyanobacteria 是现代科学名称，由源自希腊语 kyanos（深蓝色）的 cyano- 与 bacteria（细菌）组合而成。这个名称强调了它们的色素特征和细菌身份，取代了容易让人误以为它们属于真核藻类的旧称“蓝藻”。
etymology_story.en: Cyanobacteria is a modern scientific formation combining cyano-, from Greek kyanos meaning dark blue, with bacteria. The name highlights their pigmentation and bacterial identity, replacing the older description blue-green algae, which can misleadingly suggest that they are eukaryotic algae.

morphology_enriched.zh: cyano-（蓝色）+ bacteria（bacterium 的复数，细菌）→ cyanobacteria。相关形式：cyanobacterium（单数，一个蓝细菌个体）；cyanobacterial（形容词，蓝细菌的）；cyanobacteria 在普通英语中按复数使用，单数个体用 a cyanobacterium 表达。
morphology_enriched.en: Cyano- meaning blue + bacteria, the plural of bacterium, forms cyanobacteria. Related forms are cyanobacterium, the singular noun for one organism, and cyanobacterial, the adjective. In ordinary English, cyanobacteria is plural; one organism is a cyanobacterium.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: blue-green bacteria（蓝绿细菌）是描述性近义名称；blue-green algae（蓝藻）是仍常见的传统名称，但在分类上容易引起误解；cyanophytes（蓝藻类）是基于旧式藻类分类的名称，现代细菌学通常使用 cyanobacteria。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Blue-green bacteria is a descriptive alternative; blue-green algae is a still-common traditional name that can be taxonomically misleading; cyanophytes reflects an older classification alongside algae, whereas modern bacteriology generally uses cyanobacteria.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cyano- 表示蓝色，bacteria 表示细菌：记住“会光合作用的蓝细菌”，且并非所有种类外观都呈蓝色。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cyano- means blue and bacteria means bacteria: picture photosynthetic bacteria, while remembering that their visible colors vary.

etymology_story.zh: deviled 来自动词 devil，其烹饪义把辛辣刺激的味道与魔鬼及地狱之火相联系；后来，一些固定菜名中的食物也可以调味温和。devil 经古英语 dēofol 和拉丁语 diabolus，最终源自希腊语 diabolos，原义为诽谤者或控告者。
etymology_story.en: Deviled comes from the verb devil, whose culinary use associated pungent seasoning with the Devil and the fires of hell; some dishes retaining the name can now be mildly seasoned. Devil passed through Old English dēofol and Latin diabolus from Greek diabolos, meaning a slanderer or accuser.

morphology_enriched.zh: devil + -ed → deviled，是美式常用拼写；英式通常写作 devilled，添加后缀时双写 l。相关词形与派生词包括 devil（魔鬼；烦扰；用辛香调料烹制）、devils、deviling/devilling、devilish（魔鬼般的；淘气的）、devilishly（极其；恶魔般地）、devilishness（恶魔般的性质；淘气）、devilry/deviltry（恶作剧；恶行）、devilment（恶作剧；捣乱），以及带前缀的 bedevil（困扰）和 bedevilment（困扰；混乱）。
morphology_enriched.en: Devil + -ed forms deviled, the usual American spelling; British English generally uses devilled, doubling the l. Related forms and derivatives include devil, devils, deviling/devilling, devilish, devilishly, devilishness, devilry/deviltry, devilment, and the prefixed forms bedevil and bedevilment. These cover the ideas of a devil, mischievous or wicked behavior, harassment, and strongly seasoned cooking.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: spiced（加香料的）范围更广，不一定采用 deviled 的特定做法；stuffed（填馅的）强调填入馅料，不保证使用辛香调料；pestered（被纠缠的；烦扰了）对应非烹饪动词义，强调反复打扰。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Spiced is broader and does not imply a particular deviled preparation; stuffed emphasizes a filling without necessarily implying pungent seasoning; pestered matches the nonculinary verb sense and emphasizes repeated annoyance.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Add -ed to devil: food gets a devilishly pungent preparation, while a person gets persistently troubled.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：dog（狗）+ leg（腿）→ dogleg；名词还可转用为动词和形容词。屈折形式：复数及第三人称单数 doglegs，过去式和过去分词 doglegged，现在分词 doglegging；相关形容词 doglegged、dog-legged 表示“有明显弯折的”。

etymology_story.en: Drawdown developed as a noun from the phrasal verb draw down, with the underlying image of lowering a level or reducing a reserve. Its uses extend to withdrawals of funds, declines in investment value, and reductions in deployed troops.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：draw（抽取、拉动）+ down（向下）→ drawdown，属于动词与小品词组合形成的名词；复数为 drawdowns。对应动词必须分写为 draw down，其变化为 draws down、drew down、drawn down、drawing down；这些是短语动词的形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: draw + down → drawdown, a noun formed from a verb–particle combination; its plural is drawdowns. The corresponding verb is written separately as draw down, with forms draws down, drew down, drawn down, and drawing down.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: depletion（消耗、枯竭）强调储量因使用而减少；withdrawal（提取、撤出）强调取出资金或撤离人员的动作；decline（下降）泛指数量或价值降低。drawdown 根据语境可特指提取过程、兵力撤减或投资从高点回落的幅度。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Depletion emphasizes the using up of reserves; withdrawal emphasizes taking out money or removing personnel; decline broadly describes a fall in quantity or value. etymology_story.zh: gentamicin 是20世纪60年代出现的抗生素名称，所指药物最初从紫色小单孢菌（Micromonospora purpurea）的培养物中分离获得。文献中也可见 gentamycin 这一变体拼法，但这不足以证明该词由 gentian violet 和 kanamycin 两个名称拼合而成。
etymology_story.en: Gentamicin is an antibiotic name dating from the 1960s; the substance was first isolated from cultures of Micromonospora purpurea. The variant spelling gentamycin also occurs, but this alone does not establish a blend of the names gentian violet and kanamycin.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形态上应把 gentamicin 作为整体药名学习；词尾 -micin 可识别为抗生素命名成分，其余部分不宜强拆成有确定含义的现代词根。相关复合表达有 gentamicin-resistant（耐庆大霉素的）、gentamicin-sensitive／gentamicin-susceptible（对庆大霉素敏感的）；gentamycin 是变体拼法，不是派生词。没有常用的动词、副词或独立形容词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern morphology, gentamicin is best learned as a whole drug name; -micin is recognizable as an antibiotic naming element, while the remainder should not be forced into a transparent root analysis. Related compounds include gentamicin-resistant and gentamicin-sensitive or gentamicin-susceptible; gentamycin is a spelling variant, not a derivative. There are no common derived verbs, adverbs, or independent adjectives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gentamycin 是同一药名的变体拼法；gentamicin sulfate（硫酸庆大霉素）指其硫酸盐形式，范围更具体；aminoglycoside（氨基糖苷类抗生素）是上位类别名称。这里没有可随意互换的不同药物近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gentamycin is a variant spelling of the same name; gentamicin sulfate identifies its sulfate salt more specifically; aminoglycoside names the broader antibiotic class. Different drugs in that class are not interchangeable synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 -micin 连到“抗生素”，再把整个药名 gentamicin 对应“庆大霉素”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Let -micin cue 'antibiotic,' then attach the complete name gentamicin to this particular drug.

etymology_story.en: Lector entered through Middle English from Latin lēctor, 'reader,' related to legere, 'to read,' which also had earlier senses of gathering or choosing. English preserves its church use and also uses it for a university teaching title in some education systems.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Reader is the closest equivalent in church contexts but has other meanings; lecturer is a more widely used university teaching title; instructor broadly emphasizes teaching knowledge or skills. A lector's precise duties and rank depend on the church or national education system.

etymology_story.en: Microclimate is a modern scientific formation combining micro-, from Greek mikros, 'small,' with climate. Climate ultimately comes from Greek klima, 'inclination' or 'zone,' whose meaning developed from a latitude-related region to a place's characteristic weather conditions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：micro-（小范围）+ climate（气候）→ microclimate；复数为 microclimates。主要词族：microclimatic（小气候的）、microclimatically（从小气候角度）、microclimatology（小气候学）、microclimatological（小气候学的）、microclimatologist（小气候学家）；派生时可见 climat- 这一词干形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: micro- ('small-scale') + climate → microclimate; the plural is microclimates. The main family includes microclimatic, microclimatically, microclimatology, microclimatological, and microclimatologist, with climat- appearing as the stem in these formations.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Local climate is broader and need not contrast with surrounding conditions; microenvironment also includes nonclimatic factors such as soil and chemical conditions; mesoclimate generally describes a larger local area. mnemonic_anchor.en: Micro- means small: even one wall or patch of shade can have a climate of its own.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：pedo-（足；步行）+ -meter（测量仪器）→ pedometer（计步器）；复数为 pedometers。相关技术词包括 pedometry（步测法）和 pedometric（步测的）；这里的 pedo- 表示“足”，不是表示“儿童”的另一同形词根。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: pedo- ('foot' or 'walking') + -meter ('measuring instrument') → pedometer; the plural is pedometers. Related technical terms include pedometry and pedometric. Here pedo- means 'foot,' rather than the separate combining form meaning 'child.'

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Step counter is the direct everyday equivalent; an activity tracker generally records additional activity data; a fitness tracker often combines step counting with features such as heart-rate monitoring. Pedometer specifically emphasizes counting steps.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pedo- 是“脚”，-meter 是“测量器”：脚每走一步，它就记一次。

etymology_story.zh: shakedown 由短语动词 shake down 名词化而来，早期可指把铺盖抖开后做成的简易床铺。该短语还发展出彻底搜查、胁迫交钱和逐渐磨合稳定等用法，由此形成现代的搜查、勒索及试运行义。
etymology_story.en: Shakedown developed as a noun from the phrasal verb shake down, with an early use for an improvised bed made by shaking out bedding. Other uses of the phrase involved thorough searching, extracting money through pressure, and settling into working order, producing the modern search, extortion, and trial-run senses.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：shake（摇动）+ down（向下；充分完成）组成短语动词 shake down，再名词化为 shakedown；复数为 shakedowns，并可作形容词置于名词前。对应短语动词的形式为 shakes down、shook down、shaken down、shaking down；动词通常分写，不能把单词 shakedown 直接当作常用动词。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: shake + the particle down → the phrasal verb shake down → the noun shakedown, with the plural shakedowns and an attributive adjective use. The corresponding verb forms are shakes down, shook down, shaken down, and shaking down; the verb is normally written as two words.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: extortion（勒索）是更正式的用语，强调以威胁获取钱财；search（搜查）含义更广，而 shakedown 通常暗示彻底搜查；trial run（试运行）强调正式使用前的测试，与 shakedown 的测试义接近。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Extortion is the more formal term for obtaining money through threats; search is broader, while shakedown usually suggests a thorough search; trial run closely matches the testing sense and emphasizes a test before regular use.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 super-（超越通常程度）与 fluid（流体；流动的）组成，产生于20世纪的低温物理学研究。它用于描述液氦等物质的特殊量子状态，随后也用作这种状态下流体的名称。
etymology_story.en: The word combines super-, meaning beyond the ordinary, with fluid and arose in twentieth-century low-temperature physics. It describes a special quantum state found in substances such as liquid helium and also names a fluid in that state.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：super-（超常、超越）+ fluid（流体；流动的）→ superfluid（超流的；超流体）；形容词与名词同形。核心词族：superfluids（超流体，复数）、superfluidity（超流性）；基础词族包括 fluid（流体；流动的）、fluidity（流动性）和 fluidly（流畅地）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: super- (beyond the ordinary) + fluid → superfluid, used as both an adjective and a noun. The core family includes superfluids and superfluidity; the base family includes fluid, fluidity, and fluidly.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: zero-viscosity fluid（零黏度流体）突出无黏滞阻力这一性质；quantum fluid（量子流体）范围更广，并不必然具有超流性。这些是相关表达，不能在所有语境中与 superfluid 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Zero-viscosity fluid emphasizes the absence of viscous resistance; quantum fluid is broader and does not necessarily imply superfluidity. These are related expressions rather than interchangeable synonyms in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: super（超常）+ fluid（流体）：流动超乎寻常，黏滞阻力消失。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Super + fluid: extraordinary flow, with no viscous resistance.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 sure（可靠的、确定的）和 fire（开火、击发）组成，以枪械可靠击发的意象表达结果有保证。后来它广泛用于方法、计划和作品，表示说话者确信其必定奏效或成功。
etymology_story.en: The compound joins sure and fire, drawing on the image of a firearm firing reliably to suggest a dependable result. Its use broadened to methods, plans, and works that the speaker confidently expects to succeed.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：sure（确定的、可靠的）+ fire（击发）→ surefire；也常写作 sure-fire。该复合形容词没有常用的直接派生形式；基础词 sure 的常见词族包括 surely（肯定地）、sureness（确信；稳当）和 unsure（不确定的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: sure + fire → surefire, also commonly written sure-fire. The compound has no common direct derivatives; the family of its base sure includes surely, sureness, and unsure.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: reliable（可靠的）强调一贯表现可信；foolproof（不会因操作失误而失败的）强调容易正确使用；guaranteed（有保证的）强调明确承诺或强烈确信。surefire 较口语化，着重表达对成功结果的信心。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Reliable emphasizes consistently dependable performance; foolproof emphasizes resistance to user error; guaranteed suggests an explicit promise or strong assurance. Surefire is relatively informal and stresses confidence in a successful outcome.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Sure + fire: it fires when triggered, so the method works when used.

etymology_story.zh: 地质义借自法语 talus，意为斜坡或坡面，英语用它指崖脚堆积的碎石及其形成的斜坡。解剖义则直接承自拉丁语 talus（踝、距骨）；两义经不同借词路径进入英语。
etymology_story.en: The geological sense comes from French talus, meaning a slope or sloping surface, and denotes fallen rock and the slope it forms below a cliff. The anatomical sense comes directly from Latin talus, meaning ankle or anklebone; the two senses entered English through different borrowing routes.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 talus 是不可再作常用词根与词缀拆分的借词。地质义通常作不可数集合名词，指多个独立岩屑堆时可用 taluses；解剖义为可数名词，复数为 tali，相关形容词 talar 意为“距骨的”。常见地质复合词有 talus slope（岩屑坡）和 talus cone（岩屑锥）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, talus is a borrowed base without a productive root-and-affix breakdown. The geological sense is usually a mass noun, with taluses available for separate accumulations; the anatomical sense is countable, has the plural tali, and forms the adjective talar. Common geological compounds include talus slope and talus cone.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: scree（山坡碎石、碎石坡）与地质义高度重叠，常侧重覆盖坡面的松散碎石；rockfall debris（崩落岩屑）强调材料来自岩石崩落，不限定形成特定坡形；astragalus（距骨）是解剖义的另一专业名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Scree overlaps strongly with the geological sense and often emphasizes loose stones covering a slope; rockfall debris emphasizes the material's origin without requiring a particular slope form. Astragalus is another technical name for the anatomical talus.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经葡萄牙语 tapioca 借自巴西图皮语中表示木薯加工制品的名称。随着木薯食品传播，英语用它指木薯淀粉，也进一步指用这种淀粉制作的布丁。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed tapioca through Portuguese from a Brazilian Tupi name for a cassava preparation. As cassava foods spread, the English word came to name the starch and, by extension, a pudding made from it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 tapioca 是整体借入的独立词基，不能合理拆成常用英语词根与词缀。原料义和布丁义通常不可数，没有常用的直接派生词；常见复合表达包括 tapioca starch（木薯淀粉）、tapioca flour（木薯粉）、tapioca pearls（木薯珍珠粉圆）和 tapioca pudding（木薯布丁）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, tapioca is a borrowed base without a meaningful productive root-and-affix breakdown. Both the starch and pudding senses are normally uncountable, and there are no common direct derivatives; common compounds include tapioca starch, tapioca flour, tapioca pearls, and tapioca pudding.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cassava starch（木薯淀粉）是原料义的直接对应表达；tapioca pudding（木薯布丁）明确限定甜点义；sago（西米）在烹饪中用途相似，但传统上来自棕榈类植物的淀粉，不能视为严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cassava starch directly matches the ingredient sense; tapioca pudding explicitly identifies the dessert sense. Sago has similar culinary uses but traditionally comes from palm starch, so it is not a strict synonym.

etymology_story.zh: tourney 经中古英语来自古法语中表示骑士比武的词，与表示“转动、转身”的动词有关。它早于英语中的 tournament，后来保留为 tournament 较简短、较口语化的对应词，尤见于体育报道。
etymology_story.en: Tourney entered Middle English from an Old French word for a knightly tournament, related to a verb meaning to turn. It predates tournament in English and survives as a shorter, more informal alternative, especially in sports reporting.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 tourney 作为独立词基使用，不宜简单分析成 tournament 去掉后缀；两词有历史联系。复数为 tourneys，元音字母 e 后的 y 保留，再加 -s；相关词包括 tournament（锦标赛）。历史上也有动词 tourney（参加骑士比武），其形式为 tourneys、tourneyed、tourneying，但不属于现代常用词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern tourney functions as an independent base rather than a straightforward suffix removal from tournament; the two words are historically related. Its plural is tourneys, retaining y after the vowel e. The related word tournament is standard; the historical verb tourney, with forms tourneys, tourneyed, and tourneying, is not a common active modern use.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tournament（锦标赛）最接近，语体更中性；competition（比赛、竞赛）范围更广，不一定包含多轮对阵；championship（冠军赛、锦标赛）强调争夺冠军头衔。tourney 常带轻松的体育报道语气，不能一概译为“联赛”。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tournament is the closest equivalent and is more neutral in register; competition is broader and need not involve a series of matches; championship emphasizes competition for a title. Tourney often has an informal sports-reporting tone and does not specifically mean a league.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从骑士比武到球场争冠：tourney 是 tournament 的简短口语对应词。
mnemonic_anchor.en: From knights competing to teams playing: tourney is the shorter, informal counterpart of tournament.

etymology_story.zh: 该词属于以希腊语 anthrōpos（人）和 metron（尺度、测量工具）为基础形成的现代科学词族。其含义集中于测量人体的尺寸与比例，并用于生长评估、人体工学等领域。
etymology_story.en: The word belongs to a modern scientific family built from Greek anthrōpos, meaning 'human being,' and metron, meaning 'measure.' Its meaning concerns measuring human dimensions and proportions, with applications such as growth assessment and ergonomics.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：anthropo-（人、人类）+ metr-（测量）+ -ic（……的）；也可联系 anthropometry 去掉词尾 -y 后形成的形容词。核心词族：anthropometry（人体测量学）、anthropometric（人体测量的）、anthropometrical（同义形容词变体）、anthropometrically（以人体测量方式）、anthropometrist（人体测量人员）、anthropometer（人体测量仪）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: anthropo- ('human') + metr- ('measurement') + -ic ('relating to'); it can also be related to anthropometry with its final -y replaced. The core family includes anthropometry (the study or practice of measuring human bodies), anthropometric, anthropometrical (an alternative adjective), anthropometrically (by means of body measurement), anthropometrist (a practitioner), and anthropometer (a measuring instrument).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: anthropometrical（人体测量的）是意义相同但较少见的变体；somatometric（身体测量的）强调身体的物理测量；biometric（生物特征测量的）范围更广，现代语境中常涉及指纹、人脸等身份识别特征，并非可随意替换的同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Anthropometrical is a less common equivalent. Somatometric emphasizes physical measurements of the body. Biometric is broader and often concerns identifying features such as fingerprints or facial characteristics, so it is not freely interchangeable with anthropometric.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 back（向后）和 pedal（踩踏板）组合而成，最初描写倒踩自行车踏板的动作。此后，“向后”的动作意象扩展为身体后退，以及在言论、政策或承诺上退让。
etymology_story.en: Backpedal combines back with pedal and originally described turning bicycle pedals backward. The image of backward movement later extended to stepping backward and retreating from statements, policies, or promises.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：back（向后）+ pedal（踩踏板），构成复合动词。词形包括 backpedals；美式常用 backpedaled、backpedaling，英式常用 backpedalled、backpedalling；backpedaling/backpedalling 也可作动名词，表示“改口、退缩”或“倒踩踏板”。相关复合动词：backtrack（原路返回；改变立场）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: back ('backward') + pedal ('operate pedals'), forming a compound verb. Forms include backpedals; backpedaled and backpedaling are usual in American English, while backpedalled and backpedalling are usual in British English. The -ing form can function as a verbal noun for retreating from a position or pedaling backward. A related compound is backtrack ('retrace a route or change a position').

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: backtrack（改变先前立场）与比喻义最接近，也可表示原路返回；retract（正式撤回）强调明确收回已经发表的言论；retreat（退却、退让）范围更广，可用于位置、策略或立场，未必涉及先前说过的话。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Backtrack is close to the figurative meaning and can also mean retracing a route. Retract emphasizes explicitly withdrawing a statement, often formally. Retreat is broader and can concern a location, strategy, or position without involving an earlier statement.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a promise as forward pedaling: pedaling backward means retreating from that promise.

etymology_story.en: Breadfruit is an English compound of bread and fruit, named for the breadlike texture of the starchy fruit when baked. The name refers both to the fruit and to the tropical tree that bears it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：bread（面包）+ fruit（果实），构成复合名词，没有需要进一步拆解的派生词缀。作食物总称时通常不可数；指单个果实或树木时可数，复数可见 breadfruit 或 breadfruits。常见组合：breadfruit tree（面包果树）、breadfruit flour（面包果粉）；没有常用的独立派生动词、副词或形容词。

synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no widely used exact English synonym. ʿUlu, the Hawaiian name, and ʻuru, the Tahitian name, can refer to breadfruit in regional contexts. Jackfruit is a related but different fruit and is not a synonym.

etymology_story.en: The name buckwheat is associated with Dutch boekweit and its Middle Dutch ancestor, literally 'beech wheat,' because the seeds resemble beech nuts. Wheat reflects its grainlike use, although the plant is neither wheat nor a member of the grass family.

etymology_story.zh: 该词见于十九世纪英语，早期也有 butterscot 的写法，后来形成 butterscotch。butter 指制作糖果所用的黄油，后半部分的确切来源尚无定论；把它解释为“苏格兰”或“切划糖块”都不宜当作已确定的词源。
etymology_story.en: The word appears in nineteenth-century English, with butterscot among its early spellings before butterscotch became established. Butter names an ingredient, but the origin of the second element remains uncertain; explanations involving Scotland or scoring the candy should not be treated as established facts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形式：butter（黄油）+ scotch（此处来源未定的历史成分），宜按整体复合词掌握。butterscotch 作物质名词通常不可数，指一颗颗糖时可用复数 butterscotches；butterscotch-colored/butterscotch-coloured 表示“奶油糖色的”。butterscotch sauce、butterscotch chips 等组合中的 butterscotch 通常是名词修饰语，不必另设一个表示口味的形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern form: butter + scotch, with the second element historically uncertain; learn it as a whole compound. Butterscotch is normally uncountable as a substance, while butterscotches can refer to individual sweets. Butterscotch-colored or butterscotch-coloured means 'having the color of butterscotch.' In combinations such as butterscotch sauce and butterscotch chips, butterscotch normally functions as a noun modifier rather than requiring a separate flavor adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: toffee（太妃糖）通常更突出糖果质地，常较硬或有嚼劲；caramel（焦糖）以糖加热后产生的焦糖风味为核心，未必含黄油；butterscotch（奶油红糖糖）通常突出黄油与红糖的组合。这些是相近的糖果或风味名称，并非完全等义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Toffee usually emphasizes a firm or chewy confection. Caramel centers on the flavor produced by heating sugar and does not necessarily contain butter. Butterscotch typically emphasizes the combination of butter and brown sugar. These are neighboring confectionery and flavor terms rather than exact equivalents.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 以 butter 为锚：黄油加红糖，熬出金棕色的糖与风味；scotch 不强拆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to butter: butter plus brown sugar produces a golden-brown sweet and flavor; leave scotch unanalyzed.

etymology_story.zh: 该词于19世纪进入英语人类学术语，由源自希腊语 endon（内部）的 endo- 与源自 gamos（婚姻）的 -gamy 构成。其核心含义是把婚姻对象限定在某个群体内部，并不必然指近亲结婚。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English anthropological terminology in the nineteenth century, combining endo-, from Greek endon meaning 'within,' with -gamy, from gamos meaning 'marriage.' It describes marriage within a defined group and does not necessarily imply marriage between close relatives.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：endo-（内部）+ -gamy（婚姻制度或婚配方式）→ endogamy。词族包括 endogamous、endogamic（内婚的），endogamously（以群体内婚方式）和 endogamist（实行或主张内婚者）；对照词 exogamy（外婚制）使用 exo-（外部）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: endo- 'within' + -gamy 'a marriage system or mating practice' → endogamy. Family members include endogamous and endogamic 'relating to endogamy,' endogamously 'in an endogamous manner,' and endogamist 'someone who practices or advocates endogamy'; the contrasting term exogamy uses exo- 'outside.'

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: in-marriage（群体内婚）是直接近义表达；homogamy（同类婚配）强调配偶在背景或特征上相似；inbreeding（近亲繁殖）强调具有亲缘关系的个体之间繁殖，不能与 endogamy 等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: In-marriage is a direct equivalent; homogamy emphasizes similarity between partners in background or characteristics; inbreeding concerns reproduction between related individuals and is not equivalent to endogamy.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: endo- 是“内部”，-gamy 是“婚姻”：婚姻圈画在群体内部。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Endo- means 'within' and -gamy means 'marriage': draw the marriage circle inside the group.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借用新拉丁语植物属名 Ginkgo，该名称源于日语 ginkyō，即汉字“銀杏”的一种读法，字面意为“银色的杏”。现代拼写沿用了早期欧洲植物学文献中记录的形式。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the New Latin genus name Ginkgo, derived from Japanese ginkyō, a reading of the characters 銀杏 meaning 'silver apricot.' The modern spelling preserves the form recorded in early European botanical writing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 ginkgo 是不可再作常规词缀拆分的借入词；复数可写作 ginkgoes 或 ginkgos，另有拼写变体 gingko。常见相关表达包括 ginkgo tree（银杏树）、ginkgo leaf（银杏叶）和 ginkgo nut（白果，即银杏种子的可食部分），均为组合表达。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, ginkgo is a borrowed base without a productive internal root-and-affix division; its plurals are ginkgoes and ginkgos, and gingko is a spelling variant. Common combinations include ginkgo tree, ginkgo leaf, and ginkgo nut 'the edible part of a ginkgo seed'; these are combinations rather than affixal derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Maidenhair tree is another common name for the same tree, referring to its leaves' resemblance to maidenhair fern foliage; Ginkgo biloba is the scientific species name used in botanical contexts.

etymology_story.en: The word combines golden with rod, naming the plant after its yellow flower clusters and upright stems. The flowers later supplied the word's additional meaning as a golden-yellow color.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：[gold（金）+ -en（构成形容词）] + rod（杆）→ goldenrod；表示多株或多种植物时，复数为 goldenrods。相关词族包括 gold（金；金色）、golden（金色的）、goldenrod（金黄色；金黄色的）；颜色义通常不可数，形容词也不另加词缀。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: [gold + adjectival -en] + rod → goldenrod; the plural goldenrods refers to multiple plants or kinds. Related forms include gold, golden, and the noun and adjective color uses of goldenrod; the color noun is normally uncountable, and the adjective requires no additional suffix.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 植物义可用 Solidago（一枝黄花属）作分类学对应，但该属名指一个属，且部分属外植物也有 goldenrod 这一俗名；颜色义接近 golden yellow（金黄色），而 gold（金色）还常带有金属光泽的联想。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the plant, Solidago is the principal taxonomic counterpart, although it names a genus and some plants outside it also have goldenrod in their common names. For the color, golden yellow is a close equivalent, while gold often additionally suggests a metallic appearance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: golden + rod：一根开满金黄小花的“金色花杆”，也给这种黄色取了名。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Golden + rod: picture an upright rod covered in golden flowers, then use the flowers to remember the color.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：green（绿色的）+ back（背面）→ greenback；复数为 greenbacks。greenback 指单张美钞时可数，the greenback 指美元这一货币；历史相关词包括 Greenbacker（绿背纸币政策支持者）和 Greenbackism（绿背纸币政策主张），二者现主要见于历史语境。

etymology_story.zh: 借自日语 hanchō（班长），其中 han 表示“班组”，chō 表示“长、首领”；英语在第二次世界大战前后通过美国军人接触日语而吸收了这个词。它后来泛指组织中的头儿，并进一步转用为表示“主管”的动词。
etymology_story.en: Honcho was borrowed from Japanese hanchō, meaning “squad leader,” with han meaning “group” and chō meaning “chief,” through American military contact around the Second World War. It broadened into an informal term for a boss and subsequently became a verb meaning “to manage.”

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中把 honcho 视为不可再分析的借入词干；名词 honcho 可通过零派生转为动词 honcho。常用词形包括 honchos（复数或动词第三人称单数）、honchoed（过去式及过去分词）、honchoing（现在分词）；没有常用的后缀派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, honcho is an unanalyzed borrowed base; the noun becomes a verb through zero derivation. Regular forms include honchos, honchoed, and honchoing; there is no established family of common suffix-derived words.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: boss（老板、上司）最通用，侧重管理权；chief（首领、主管）侧重最高职位或领导身份；leader（领导者）侧重带领他人，不一定具有正式职权。honcho 更口语化，常带轻松或略带调侃的语气。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Boss is the most general term for someone with managerial authority; chief emphasizes a leading position; leader emphasizes guiding others and need not imply formal authority. Honcho is more colloquial and often sounds playful or mildly irreverent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“班长”想到“头儿”：honcho 是拿主意的人，也可以表示亲自负责。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think “squad leader → boss”: a honcho calls the shots; to honcho something is to run it.

etymology_story.zh: 可追溯至中古英语 hukster，通常认为与中古荷兰语中表示“小贩、贩卖”的词有关，但更早的词源并不完全确定。它原指零售小贩，后来逐渐带上强行推销、夸大宣传的贬义。
etymology_story.en: Huckster goes back to Middle English hukster and is generally connected with Middle Dutch words for petty selling or a petty trader, although its deeper origin is uncertain. Originally a small-scale seller, it later acquired disapproving associations with aggressive promotion and exaggerated claims.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代用法中以 huckster 为整体词干，不把 huck 当作常用独立词根；历史上的 -ster 是表示从业者的后缀。huckster 可兼作名词和动词；词形及派生词包括 hucksters、huckstered、huckstering，以及 hucksterism（夸大兜售的做派）和 hucksterish（带有招摇兜售作风的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats huckster as a whole base rather than combining it productively with an independent root huck; historically, -ster is an agent suffix. The base functions as both noun and verb, with hucksters, huckstered, and huckstering, plus derivatives hucksterism and hucksterish.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: peddler（流动小贩）强调四处售卖，本身不必含欺骗意味；hawker（叫卖商贩）强调公开招徕顾客；salesperson（销售人员）是中性职业名称。huckster 在现代语境中通常额外暗示夸张宣传或不可信。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Peddler emphasizes selling goods from place to place without necessarily implying dishonesty; hawker emphasizes openly calling attention to goods; salesperson is a neutral occupational term. In modern contexts, huckster usually adds a suggestion of exaggeration or untrustworthiness.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a street seller whose loud sales pitch grows into exaggerated promises.

etymology_story.zh: 由 lion 的比喻义“受瞩目的名人”加动词后缀 -ise 构成；这个比喻义与人们争相观看珍奇狮子等名胜的历史习惯有关。lion 本身经古法语追溯至拉丁语 leo，最终源自希腊语 leōn。
etymology_story.en: Lionise combines -ise with lion in its figurative sense of a celebrated person, a sense associated with the historical attraction of notable sights such as captive lions. Lion itself came through Old French from Latin leo, ultimately from Greek leōn.

morphology_enriched.zh: lion（狮子；比喻为名人）+ -ise（使成为、按某种身份对待）→ lionise；常见于英式英语，美式通常拼作 lionize。词形和派生词包括 lionises、lionised、lionising、lionisation（追捧）、lioniser（追捧者）；对应的 -ize 系列为 lionizes、lionized、lionizing、lionization、lionizer，基础词族另有 lion 和 lioness（母狮）。
morphology_enriched.en: Lion + -ise forms lionise, meaning to treat someone as a celebrated figure; this spelling is common in British English, while American English normally uses lionize. Forms and derivatives include lionises, lionised, lionising, lionisation, and lioniser, with corresponding -ize forms lionizes, lionized, lionizing, lionization, and lionizer; the underlying noun family includes lion and lioness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: celebrate（赞颂）强调公开表扬成就；idolise（崇拜）强调强烈甚至不加批判的个人仰慕；glorify（颂扬、美化）强调赋予荣耀，有时暗示过度美化。lionise 特别强调把某人当作名流来关注和礼遇。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Celebrate emphasizes publicly praising achievements; idolise suggests intense, sometimes uncritical admiration; glorify emphasizes presenting someone as glorious, sometimes excessively. Lionise specifically suggests giving someone the attention and treatment of a celebrity.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: lion 是众人围观的“名狮”；lionise 就是把某人捧成众人瞩目的名流。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A figurative lion attracts everyone's attention; to lionise someone is to make them the celebrity everyone admires.

etymology_story.en: Merlot was borrowed from French merlot, traditionally explained as a diminutive of merle, meaning “blackbird,” and thus literally “little blackbird.” The grape name subsequently also became the name of wine made from that grape.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 merlot 是整体借入的简单词干，没有可自由组合的英语词缀；merle + -ot 属于法语历史构词分析。酒类总称和品种名通常不用复数，merlots 可指不同款的梅洛葡萄酒；Merlot grape、Merlot wine 是词组，没有常用的英语后缀派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, merlot is a simple borrowed base with no productive English affixes; merle + -ot describes its historical French formation. The wine and variety names are usually uncountable, while merlots can denote different Merlot wines; Merlot grape and Merlot wine are phrases, and there are no common English suffix-derived forms.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Merlot wine（梅洛葡萄酒）明确指酒，是酒义的同义表达；Merlot grape（梅洛葡萄）明确指葡萄，是葡萄义的对应表达；red wine（红葡萄酒）是更宽泛的上位词，不能准确替代具体品种名。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Merlot wine explicitly identifies the wine and is equivalent to the wine sense; Merlot grape explicitly identifies the fruit and corresponds to the grape sense; red wine is a broader category and does not identify this particular variety.

etymology_story.zh: 名称来自 Nacho，这是西班牙语人名 Ignacio 的常见昵称；这道菜通常被认为由墨西哥的 Ignacio “Nacho” Anaya 创制，并以他的昵称命名。英语采用了这个食品名称，尤其常用复数 nachos 指整道菜。
etymology_story.en: The name comes from Nacho, a familiar Spanish nickname for Ignacio; the dish is generally credited to Ignacio “Nacho” Anaya in Mexico and named after him. English adopted the food name, especially the plural nachos for the prepared dish.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 nacho 是整体借入词干，nacho + -s → nachos；Nacho 与 Ignacio 的关系属于西班牙语昵称形成，不能分析为英语词根加后缀。nacho 可在 nacho cheese（纳乔用奶酪或奶酪酱）、nacho chips（纳乔玉米片）中作名词定语，这并不构成常用的独立形容词词性；没有常用的后缀派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats nacho as a borrowed base: nacho + -s → nachos; the relationship between Nacho and Ignacio is Spanish nickname formation, not English root-and-affix morphology. Nacho functions as a noun modifier in nacho cheese and nacho chips, which does not establish a common separate adjective sense; there is no established family of common suffix-derived words.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tortilla chip names the basic chip without necessarily implying toppings; cheese nachos explicitly include cheese; loaded nachos emphasize numerous additional toppings such as meat and beans. The latter two name particular preparations rather than being interchangeable with nacho in every context.

etymology_story.zh: 这个科学术语由 neuro-（神经）和 chemistry（化学）组合而成；neuro- 源自希腊语 neuron，原指筋腱，也指神经。该词既表示研究神经系统化学过程的学科，也表示这些化学过程本身。
etymology_story.en: This scientific term combines neuro-, meaning 'nerve,' with chemistry; neuro- comes from Greek neuron, meaning 'sinew' or 'nerve.' The word names both the study of nervous-system chemistry and the chemical processes themselves.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：neuro-（神经）+ chemistry（化学）→ neurochemistry。核心词族：neurochemical（神经化学的；神经化学物质）、neurochemically（从神经化学角度）、neurochemist（神经化学研究者）；相关基础词有 chemistry（化学）、chemical（化学的；化学物质）、chemist（化学家）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: neuro- ('nerve; nervous system') + chemistry → neurochemistry. The core family includes neurochemical (adjective: relating to neurochemistry; noun: a chemical involved in nervous-system activity), neurochemically (adverb), and neurochemist (a researcher in neurochemistry). Related base words include chemistry, chemical, and chemist.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 相关表达：neural chemistry（神经系统化学活动）与其过程义接近；brain chemistry（脑内化学活动）更通俗，但范围限于脑；biochemistry（生物化学）研究生物体中的化学过程，范围更广，不能直接替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Related expressions: neural chemistry is close to its process meaning; brain chemistry is more conversational but specifically concerns the brain; biochemistry covers chemical processes throughout living organisms and is therefore broader, not interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: neuro- 指神经，chemistry 指化学：研究神经怎样靠化学物质工作。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Neuro- means nerves, and chemistry means chemicals: how the nervous system works through chemistry.

etymology_story.en: The word comes from Middle English newefangel, originally describing someone fond of novelty; its second element is related to Old English fōn, 'to seize or take.' Its meaning later shifted from liking new things to describing new inventions or fashions, often disapprovingly.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 newfangled 作为整体形容词使用，不宜机械拆成 new + fangled 并把 fangled 当作常用独立词。词族：newfangledness（新奇性；追新倾向）、newfangledly（以新奇时髦的方式，罕用）；词尾 -ed 在这里不表示一个常用现代动词的过去式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, newfangled is normally treated as a whole adjective, rather than as new plus a commonly used independent word fangled. Its family includes newfangledness (novelty or a fondness for novelty) and the rare adverb newfangledly. The ending -ed does not represent the past tense of an ordinary modern verb here.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: novel 强调新颖、不同寻常，通常较中性；modern 强调属于现代，通常不含贬义；trendy 强调当下流行。newfangled 则突出说话者对新玩意儿的怀疑或不以为然，有时带幽默感。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Novel emphasizes being new or unusual and is usually fairly neutral; modern means belonging to the present age without inherent criticism; trendy emphasizes current fashion. Newfangled adds skepticism or disapproval toward novelty, sometimes humorously.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史线索是“抓住新东西”：别人追新，说话者却嫌它花哨。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the historical idea of 'grabbing new things': others embrace the novelty, but the speaker distrusts the fuss.

forms: nitpicks；nitpicked；nitpicking。

morphology.text: nit（虱卵）+ pick（挑出）→ nitpick，从挑虱卵引申为纠缠极小的毛病。

etymology.text: 英语复合词，原本挑拣虱卵的细小动作变成对微小缺点的苛刻挑剔；用“连虱卵那么小的问题也不放过”助记。

usage_note: 常用 nitpick about 或 nitpick over；有贬义，区别于有必要的认真审查。

etymology_story.zh: 该词与 nit-picking 有关，字面意思是挑出虱卵；nit 指附着在毛发上的虱卵。现代比喻义把这种细小而费力的挑拣动作转化为对微不足道的问题反复挑剔。
etymology_story.en: The word is associated with nit-picking, literally removing nits, the eggs of lice attached to hair. Its modern figurative meaning turns this painstaking attention to tiny objects into excessive criticism of insignificant faults.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 nit（虱卵）+ pick（挑出）；动词通常被分析为由 nit-picking 逆构而来，名词则与动词同形。词族：nitpicks（动词第三人称单数；名词复数）、nitpicked（过去式及过去分词）、nitpicking（现在分词；吹毛求疵；吹毛求疵的）、nitpicker（爱挑小毛病的人）、nitpicky（爱挑剔的，非正式）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern components are nit ('a louse egg') + pick ('remove by picking'); the verb is generally analyzed as a back-formation from nit-picking, with an identical noun form. The family includes nitpicks (third-person singular verb or plural noun), nitpicked (past tense and participle), nitpicking (participle, noun, or adjective), nitpicker (a person who finds trivial faults), and informal nitpicky (overly concerned with minor faults).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: quibble 强调对措辞或小问题提出异议；split hairs 强调作过分细微的区分；carp 强调不断抱怨或挑错。nitpick 尤其强调所挑的问题太小，不值得如此关注。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Quibble emphasizes objections about wording or minor points; split hairs emphasizes excessively fine distinctions; carp emphasizes persistent complaining or fault-finding. Nitpick particularly suggests that the faults are too small to deserve so much attention.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 连虱卵那么小的毛病都要挑出来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picking out faults as tiny as lice eggs.

morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: primp is a simple verb without a productive root-and-affix division; the final -p is not a meaningful suffix. senses.meaning_zh: 精神运动的；涉及心理活动与身体运动相互联系的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to the connection between mental activity and physical movement.
senses.english_definition: Psychomotor abilities or processes involve mental activity working together with physical movement.
senses.collocation_en: psychomotor skills; psychomotor development
senses.collocation_zh: 心理运动技能；心理运动发育
senses.sentence_en: The activity helps children develop psychomotor skills such as hand-eye coordination.
senses.sentence_zh: 这项活动帮助儿童发展手眼协调等心理运动技能。

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 psycho-（心理、心智）与 motor（运动的）组合而成：前者源自希腊语 psykhē（生命、灵魂、心灵），后者最终源自拉丁语 motor（推动者）。这个科学术语用来描述心理活动与身体动作之间的联系。
etymology_story.en: The word combines psycho-, 'mind,' with motor, 'relating to movement': the first ultimately comes from Greek psykhē, 'life, soul, or mind,' and the second from Latin motor, 'mover.' The scientific term describes the connection between mental activity and bodily movement.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：psycho-（心理）+ motor（运动的）→ psychomotor。相关词族包括 psychomotorically（在心理运动方面，较少见）和 psychomotricity（心理与运动功能的整合，专业名词）；psycho- 同根词有 psychology（心理学）、psychological（心理的），motor 相关词有 motoric（运动的，专业用语）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: psycho- ('mind; mental activity') + motor ('relating to movement') → psychomotor. Related family members include the less common adverb psychomotorically and the specialist noun psychomotricity, referring to the integration of mental and motor functions. Words sharing psycho- include psychology and psychological; motoric is a specialist adjective related to motor.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 相关而非完全同义的词：sensorimotor 强调感觉输入与动作的配合；neuromotor 强调神经系统对运动的控制；motor 只泛指运动或运动功能。psychomotor 特别强调心理活动与身体动作之间的联系。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Related terms rather than exact synonyms: sensorimotor emphasizes coordination between sensory input and movement; neuromotor emphasizes nervous-system control of movement; motor refers broadly to movement or movement functions. Psychomotor specifically emphasizes the relationship between mental activity and bodily action.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: psycho- 是心，motor 是动：心中处理，身体行动。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Psycho- is mind; motor is movement: mental processing connects with physical action.

morphology.text: sept-（中隔，见 septum）+ -al（……的）→ septal（中隔的）。

senses.meaning_zh: 中隔的；与分隔腔室的隔膜或隔壁有关的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to a wall or membrane that separates cavities or compartments.
senses.english_definition: Something that is septal relates to a septum, a wall or membrane separating two spaces in an organism.
senses.collocation_en: atrial septal defect; nasal septal perforation
senses.collocation_zh: 房间隔缺损；鼻中隔穿孔
senses.sentence_en: The scan revealed a small atrial septal defect.
senses.sentence_zh: 扫描检查发现了一处小的房间隔缺损。

etymology_story.zh: septal 由 septum（中隔）加形容词后缀 -al 构成；septum 源自拉丁语 saeptum，意为“围栏、围起的区域或隔断”。实体隔断的概念后来用于生物体内分隔腔室的结构。[词源参考](https://www.etymonline.com/word/septum)
etymology_story.en: Septal combines septum with the adjective suffix -al; septum comes from Latin saeptum, meaning a fence, enclosure, or partition. The idea of a physical partition was applied to structures separating spaces within organisms. [Etymology reference](https://www.etymonline.com/word/septum)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：sept-（septum 去掉拉丁语词尾 -um 后的词干，表示“隔”）+ -al（……的）→ septal。相关词族：septum（中隔，复数 septa）；septate／septated（有隔的）；aseptate（无隔的）；septation（分隔形成）；interseptal（隔间的）；septoplasty（中隔成形术）；septectomy（中隔切除术）；septostomy（中隔造口术）。这些词共享词干，并非都直接派生自 septal。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: sept-, the stem of septum without its Latin ending -um, + -al, meaning relating to, → septal. Related family: septum, a partition, plural septa; septate/septated, having septa; aseptate, lacking septa; septation, partition formation; interseptal, between septa; septoplasty, surgical reconstruction of a septum; septectomy, surgical removal of septal tissue; septostomy, surgical creation of an opening in a septum. These share a stem rather than all deriving directly from septal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 相关近义表达：septate（有隔的）、septated（具有分隔结构的）、partitioned（被分隔的）。septal 表示“与中隔有关”，septate 和 septated 强调“具有隔”，partitioned 则是更宽泛的日常表达，三者都不能在所有语境中替换 septal。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Related near-synonyms: septate, septated, and partitioned. Septal means relating to a septum; septate and septated emphasize the presence of partitions, while partitioned is a broader everyday description, so none is universally interchangeable with septal.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 septum 想成体内的一堵隔墙：septal 就是“这堵隔墙的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a septum as an internal dividing wall: septal means relating to that wall.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式教学读音；重音符号 ˈ 后为主重读音节。

forms: 复数 skipjack 或 skipjacks；指鱼肉时通常不可数。
family: skipjacks 鲣鱼的复数；skipjack tuna 鲣鱼

etymology_story.zh: skipjack 是 skip（轻跳）与 jack 的英语复合词；Jack 原为人名，后来广泛用于动物和器物名称。鱼名体现了鱼在水面跳跃的特点，而现代 skipjack 也有一种浅底帆船的独立词义。[词义参考](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/skipjack)
etymology_story.en: Skipjack compounds skip, meaning to jump lightly, with jack, a personal name that became a common element in animal and object names. The fish name evokes surface-jumping behavior, while modern skipjack also has a separate shallow-bottomed sailboat sense. [Usage reference](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/skipjack)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：skip（跳跃）+ jack（用于命名动物或器物的成分）→ skipjack。鱼类义复数可用 skipjack 或 skipjacks；帆船义通常用 skipjacks。常见复合表达：skipjack tuna（鲣鱼）、skipjack herring（一种俗称跳鲱的鱼）；没有常用的直接派生形容词或动词。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: skip, meaning jump, + jack, an element used in names for animals or objects, → skipjack. Fish plurals include skipjack and skipjacks; the boat plural is normally skipjacks. Common compounds include skipjack tuna and skipjack herring. There are no common directly derived adjectives or verbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: skipjack tuna（鲣鱼）明确指食用鱼种 Katsuwonus pelamis；tuna（金枪鱼类）范围更广，还包括长鳍金枪鱼、黄鳍金枪鱼等；sloop（单桅纵帆船）在帆船义上有重叠，但表示帆装类型，并不专指这种浅底采牡蛎船。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Skipjack tuna specifically identifies Katsuwonus pelamis; tuna is broader and includes species such as albacore and yellowfin. Sloop overlaps with the boat sense but describes a sailing rig rather than specifically identifying this shallow-bottomed oyster boat.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: skip 是“跳”：先记水面跃起的鲣鱼，再单独记住“浅底帆船”这一词义。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Let skip suggest a fish jumping at the surface; learn the shallow-bottomed sailboat meaning as a separate sense.

senses.meaning_zh: 超声图像；利用超声回波生成的体内影像
senses.meaning_en: An image of internal body structures produced using ultrasound echoes.

senses.meaning_en: A visual representation of sound frequencies and their intensity over time.

etymology_story.zh: sonogram 是二十世纪形成的科学词，由源自拉丁语 sonus（声音）的 sono- 与源自希腊语 gramma（写下或画出的记录）的 -gram 组合而成。它既用于声音的可视化记录，也用于超声诊断产生的影像。[词源参考](https://www.etymonline.com/word/sonogram)；[词义参考](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/sonogram)
etymology_story.en: Sonogram is a twentieth-century scientific formation combining sono-, from Latin sonus, meaning sound, with -gram, from Greek gramma, meaning something written or drawn. It is used both for visual records of sound and for images produced by diagnostic ultrasound. [Etymology reference](https://www.etymonline.com/word/sonogram); [usage reference](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/sonogram)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：sono-（声音）+ -gram（记录、图像）→ sonogram；复数 sonograms。相关词族：sonograph（声谱记录仪）；sonography（超声成像法）；sonographer（超声检查技师）；sonographic（超声成像的）；sonographically（通过超声成像）；ultrasonogram（超声图像）；ultrasonography（超声检查法）；ultrasonographer（超声检查技师）；ultrasonographic（超声检查的）。这些是共享构词成分的相关形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: sono-, meaning sound, + -gram, meaning a record or image, → sonogram; plural sonograms. Related family: sonograph, an instrument for recording sound patterns; sonography, ultrasound imaging; sonographer, an ultrasound practitioner; sonographic, relating to sonography; sonographically, by sonographic means; ultrasonogram, an ultrasound image; ultrasonography, ultrasound examination; ultrasonographer, an ultrasound practitioner; ultrasonographic, relating to ultrasound examination. These are related formations sharing combining elements.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ultrasonogram（超声图像）明确表示医学超声影像；echogram（回波图）强调通过反射回波形成记录；spectrogram（频谱图、声谱图）对应声学义，用于展示频率随时间的变化，不是医学超声影像的通用替换词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ultrasonogram explicitly identifies an ultrasound image; echogram emphasizes a record formed from reflected echoes. Spectrogram matches the acoustic sense by displaying frequency content over time and is not a general substitute for a medical ultrasound image.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sono- 是“声”，-gram 是“图”：把声音变成看得见的图。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sono- is sound and -gram is a picture or record: sound made visible.

morphology.text: tail（尾部）+ spin（旋转）→ tailspin（飞机螺旋下坠，后比喻失控恶化）。

etymology.text: 二十世纪航空英语把 tail 与 spin 合成飞机失控下坠的名称，后来引申到经济、情绪等急剧恶化的情形。先想象旋转着下坠，再记住比喻义。

senses.meaning_en: A sudden, uncontrolled decline or a state of emotional turmoil.
senses.english_definition: If something goes into a tailspin, it becomes much worse very quickly, or a person becomes extremely upset and unable to cope.
senses.collocation_en: send someone into a tailspin; an economic tailspin
senses.collocation_zh: 使某人情绪骤然失控；经济的失控式恶化

senses.meaning_en: To descend in a spiral, used intransitively.
senses.english_definition: If an aircraft tailspins, it falls rapidly while rotating.
senses.collocation_en: an aircraft tailspins; tailspin toward the ground
senses.collocation_zh: 飞机进入尾旋；螺旋着向地面下坠
senses.sentence_en: The damaged aircraft began to tailspin toward the ground.
senses.sentence_zh: 受损的飞机开始螺旋着向地面下坠。

senses.meaning_zh: 急剧恶化；失控地下滑，作不及物动词
senses.meaning_en: To deteriorate sharply or decline uncontrollably, used intransitively.
senses.english_definition: If a situation tailspins, it gets worse rapidly and becomes difficult to control.
senses.collocation_en: the economy tailspins; tailspin into chaos
senses.collocation_zh: 经济急剧恶化；迅速陷入混乱
senses.sentence_en: Without new funding, the business could tailspin into bankruptcy.
senses.sentence_zh: 如果没有新的资金，这家企业可能迅速恶化，最终破产。

etymology_story.zh: tailspin 由 tail（尾部）与 spin（旋转）组成，二十世纪初首先用于描述飞机螺旋下坠。后来，这种失去控制、不断下坠的形象被用于经济衰退、局势恶化和情绪失控。[词源参考](https://www.etymonline.com/word/tailspin)
etymology_story.en: Tailspin combines tail and spin and entered early twentieth-century aviation vocabulary for an aircraft's spiraling descent. Its image of uncontrolled downward movement was later extended to economic decline, deteriorating situations, and emotional turmoil. [Etymology reference](https://www.etymonline.com/word/tailspin)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：tail（尾部）+ spin（旋转）→ tailspin；名词可零派生为不及物动词。屈折形式：tailspins（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、tailspinning（现在分词）；过去式和过去分词可见 tailspun 或 tailspinned。tailspinning 也可作分词修饰语，表示“急剧恶化的”。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: tail + spin → tailspin; the noun also functions as an intransitive verb through conversion. Inflected forms include tailspins, the plural noun or third-person singular verb; tailspinning, the present participle; and tailspun or tailspinned, attested past-tense and past-participle forms. Tailspinning can also modify a noun participially, meaning deteriorating rapidly.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: spin（旋转；飞机螺旋下降）对应航空义，但普通语义不一定包含下坠；downturn（下滑）表示形势转差，未必严重或失控；downward spiral（不断加剧的恶性下滑）强调恶化相互推动，而 tailspin 更突出突然失控。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Spin matches the aviation sense but does not inherently imply descent in everyday use. Downturn describes worsening conditions without necessarily suggesting severity or lost control; downward spiral emphasizes self-reinforcing deterioration, while tailspin particularly suggests a sudden loss of control.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 尾部旋转、整机下坠：从“飞机失控下降”联想到“局势或情绪失控恶化”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a spinning aircraft dropping: transfer that loss of control to a situation or someone's emotions.

senses.sentence_en: As a triathlete, she trains in swimming, cycling, and running every week.
senses.sentence_zh: 作为一名铁人三项运动员，她每周都进行游泳、自行车和跑步训练。

etymology_story.zh: triathlete 是现代体育英语结合 triathlon（三项赛）与 athlete（运动员）形成的名称。tri- 源自希腊语中表示“三”的构词成分，athlete 则经拉丁语追溯到希腊语 athlētēs，意为“竞赛者”。[词源参考](https://www.etymonline.com/word/triathlete)
etymology_story.en: Triathlete is a modern sporting term formed through the association of triathlon and athlete. Tri- comes from Greek and means three, while athlete reached English through Latin from Greek athlētēs, meaning a contestant in athletic games. [Etymology reference](https://www.etymonline.com/word/triathlete)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代分析：tri-（三）+ athlete（运动员）→ triathlete；这一形式同时受到 triathlon 的影响。复数：triathletes。核心相关词：triathlon（铁人三项赛）；triathletic（铁人三项运动的，较少见）。更广的 athlete 词族包括 athletic（运动的；健壮的）、athletically（在运动方面；以运动员般的方式）、athleticism（运动能力）和 athletics（田径运动；体育运动）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: tri-, meaning three, + athlete → triathlete, with the formation also influenced by triathlon. Plural: triathletes. Core related forms include triathlon, the three-discipline race, and triathletic, a less common adjective relating to triathlon. The broader athlete family includes athletic, relating to sport or physically capable; athletically, in an athletic manner; athleticism, athletic ability; and athletics, track-and-field sports or sporting activities.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: triathlon competitor（铁人三项参赛者）是最接近的释义表达；multisport athlete（多项目运动员）范围更广，不一定参加铁人三项；Ironman triathlete（Ironman 铁人三项运动员）通常特指参加该品牌长距离赛事的运动员，范围更窄。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Triathlon competitor is the closest explanatory equivalent. Multisport athlete is broader and need not refer to a triathlon participant; Ironman triathlete is narrower and usually identifies someone competing in the branded long-distance events.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: tri-＝三，athlete＝运动员：一名运动员连续完成游泳、骑车、跑步三项。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Tri- means three and athlete means competitor: one athlete swims, cycles, and runs.

senses.meaning_zh: 以人类为中心的；以人类利益或经验为首要标准的
senses.meaning_en: Treating humans, their interests, or their experience as central or most important.
senses.english_definition: An anthropocentric view treats human beings and their interests as more important than other living things or interprets the world mainly through human experience.
senses.collocation_en: an anthropocentric worldview; anthropocentric thinking
senses.collocation_zh: 以人类为中心的世界观；以人类为中心的思维
senses.sentence_en: The essay challenges the anthropocentric assumption that nature exists mainly to serve human needs.
senses.sentence_zh: 这篇文章质疑了这样一种以人类为中心的假设：自然的存在主要是为了满足人类的需要。

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 anthropo-（人类）和 centric（以……为中心的）构成，相关成分分别源于希腊语 anthrōpos（人）和 kentron（尖点，后引申为中心）。它在近代学术讨论中用于描述把人类置于解释或价值判断中心的观点。
etymology_story.en: The word combines anthropo-, meaning human, with centric, meaning centered; these elements ultimately come from Greek anthrōpos, human being, and kentron, a sharp point and later a center. It developed in modern scholarly discussion to describe views that place humanity at the center of interpretation or value.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：anthropo-（人类）+ centr-（中心）+ -ic（形容词后缀）。主要词族：anthropocentrism（人类中心主义）、anthropocentrically（以人类为中心地）；另有较少见的 anthropocentricity（人类中心性）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: anthropo- (human) + centr- (center) + -ic (adjective suffix). The principal family includes anthropocentrism, the corresponding outlook or doctrine, and anthropocentrically, the adverb; anthropocentricity, the quality of being human-centered, is less common.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: human-centered（以人为中心的）较中性，常强调设计或服务满足人的需要；human-centric（以人为中心的）与其接近，常见于技术和商业语境；anthropocentric 常用于哲学和生态讨论，尤其强调人类相对于其他生命的优先地位。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Human-centered is relatively neutral and often describes design or services organized around people's needs; human-centric is similar and common in technology and business. Anthropocentric is especially associated with philosophy and ecology, often emphasizing human priority over other forms of life.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: anthropo- 是“人”，centr- 是“中心”：把人放在圆心。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anthropo- means human and centr- means center: picture humanity placed at the center of a circle.

senses.meaning_zh: 鸡油菌；通常呈黄色或橙色、菌盖呈漏斗状的食用菌
senses.meaning_en: An edible mushroom, typically yellow or orange, with a funnel-shaped cap.
senses.english_definition: A chanterelle is an edible wild mushroom that usually has a yellow or orange cap shaped like a shallow funnel.
senses.collocation_en: wild chanterelles; sautéed chanterelles
senses.collocation_zh: 野生鸡油菌；煎炒鸡油菌
senses.sentence_en: The chef served sautéed chanterelles on toasted bread.
senses.sentence_zh: 厨师把煎炒好的鸡油菌配在烤面包上端了出来。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自法语 chanterelle，其名称通过拉丁语形式最终可追溯至希腊语 kantharos，意为一种饮酒杯。这个名称与菌盖的杯状或漏斗状外形有关。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed chanterelle from French; through Latin forms, the name ultimately goes back to Greek kantharos, a type of drinking cup. The name refers to the mushroom's cup-like or funnel-shaped cap.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中为不可进一步作实用拆分的借入名词，不宜把它拆成英语 chant 和其他成分。复数为 chanterelles；无常用派生词族，常见组合有 chanterelle mushroom（鸡油菌）和 chanterelle sauce（鸡油菌酱汁）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is a borrowed noun without a useful productive internal breakdown; it should not be analyzed as English chant plus additional elements. Its plural is chanterelles. It has no established common derivational family; combinations include chanterelle mushroom and chanterelle sauce.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: girolle（鸡油菌）是烹饪语境中的近义名称，通常指金黄色鸡油菌；mushroom（蘑菇）是范围更广的上位词，并不特指鸡油菌。不同地区对 chanterelle 和 girolle 的具体使用范围可能有所差异。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Girolle is a culinary near-synonym, usually referring to a golden chanterelle; mushroom is the broader category and does not identify this particular kind. The precise scope of chanterelle and girolle can vary regionally.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住词源中的“小杯”意象：金黄菌盖像浅浅的小漏斗。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the cup behind the name: a golden mushroom cap shaped like a shallow funnel.

senses.meaning_zh: 西班牙或拉丁美洲风味的调味香肠，常用红椒粉或辣椒调味
senses.meaning_en: A strongly seasoned Spanish or Latin American sausage, often flavored with paprika or chili.
senses.english_definition: Chorizo is a type of sausage associated with Spain and Latin America that is strongly seasoned, often with paprika or chili.
senses.collocation_en: sliced chorizo; chorizo sausage
senses.collocation_zh: 切片的乔里索香肠；乔里索香肠
senses.sentence_en: She added sliced chorizo to the stew for extra flavor.
senses.sentence_zh: 她往炖菜里加入了切片的乔里索香肠，使味道更加浓郁。

etymology_story.zh: 英语直接借用了西班牙语 chorizo，沿用了这种调味香肠的名称。西班牙语词的更早来源尚无定论；随着这种食物传播，该词也用于指拉丁美洲的地方品种。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed chorizo directly from Spanish as the name of the seasoned sausage. The Spanish word's earlier origin is uncertain; as the food spread, the name also came to cover regional Latin American varieties.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中为不可进一步拆分的借入名词；-o 不是此处可独立分析的英语后缀。可作可数名词，复数为 chorizos，也可作不可数名词表示作为食材的香肠；无常用英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, chorizo is an unanalyzed borrowed noun; its final -o is not a productive English suffix here. It can be countable, with the plural chorizos, or uncountable when referring to sausage as an ingredient. It has no established common English derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sausage（香肠）是上位词；pepperoni（佩珀罗尼辣香肠）通常是意大利裔美式的风干香肠，常作披萨配料；salami（萨拉米香肠）泛指多种发酵或风干香肠。后二者都不能准确替代 chorizo，后者的风味和制作方式还随地区变化。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sausage is the general category; pepperoni is an Italian American cured sausage commonly used on pizza; salami covers various fermented or cured sausages. Neither pepperoni nor salami is an exact substitute for chorizo, whose seasoning and preparation also vary by region.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把整个词与“红椒调味、风味浓郁的香肠”绑定记忆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the whole word to one vivid image: a richly seasoned, red-pepper-flavored sausage.

senses.meaning_zh: 基督论的；有关耶稣基督的本性、身份和作用的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to the theological study of Jesus Christ's nature, identity, and role.
senses.english_definition: A Christological question or belief concerns who Jesus Christ is, especially his divine and human nature and his role in salvation.
senses.collocation_en: Christological doctrine; Christological debates
senses.collocation_zh: 基督论教义；基督论争论
senses.sentence_en: The course examines the Christological debates of the early church.
senses.sentence_zh: 这门课程研究早期教会有关基督论的争论。

etymology_story.zh: 该词是 Christology（基督论）的形容词形式；Christology 结合了 Christ（基督）与源自希腊语的 -logy（研究、论述）。Christ 最终源于希腊语 Khristos，意为“受膏者”。
etymology_story.en: Christological is the adjective corresponding to Christology, which combines Christ with the Greek-derived element -logy, meaning study or discourse. Christ ultimately comes from Greek Khristos, meaning the anointed one.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：Christo-（基督）+ -logical（有关某项研究或学说的），也可理解为 Christology 的 -logy 变为 -logical。主要词族：Christology（基督论）、Christological（基督论的）、Christologically（从基督论角度）、Christologist（基督论研究者）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: Christo- (Christ) + -logical (relating to a field of study or doctrine); alternatively, Christology changes its ending from -logy to -logical. The principal family consists of Christology, Christological, Christologically, and Christologist, a scholar of Christology.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Christ-centered（以基督为中心的）强调信仰或实践的中心；theological（神学的）范围更广，涉及上帝和宗教教义；Christian（基督教的）可描述整个宗教传统。只有 Christological 特指基督的身份、本性及相关教义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Christ-centered emphasizes the focus of belief or practice; theological is broader and concerns God and religious doctrine; Christian can describe the whole religious tradition. Christological specifically concerns Christ's identity, nature, and the doctrines surrounding them.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Christ 加“学说的”：围绕“基督是谁、具有何种本性”的讨论。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Christ plus the study-related ending: discussion of who Christ is and what his nature is.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式教学读音；重音符号 ˈ 后为主重读音节。

senses.meaning_zh: 腓骨；小腿外侧较细的长骨

senses.meaning_zh: 古代扣针；用于固定衣物的搭扣或胸针
senses.meaning_en: An ancient brooch or pin used to fasten clothing.
senses.english_definition: A fibula is a brooch or pin that people in ancient societies used to hold their clothing together.
senses.collocation_en: a bronze fibula; a Roman fibula
senses.collocation_zh: 青铜扣针；古罗马扣针

etymology_story.zh: 该词直接借自拉丁语 fibula，原指扣针或搭扣。它后来成为腓骨的解剖学名称，因为腓骨与胫骨的排列被比作扣针的结构；原来的器物义仍用于考古学。
etymology_story.en: The word comes directly from Latin fibula, meaning a clasp or fastening pin. It became an anatomical name because the arrangement of the fibula and tibia was compared to a clasp; the original object sense survives in archaeology.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中为不可再作实用拆分的拉丁语借词，复数为 fibulae 或 fibulas。解剖学词族包括 fibular（腓骨的）、fibul-／fibulo-（表示腓骨的组合形式）；tibiofibular（胫腓骨的）由 tibio-（胫骨）和 fibular 构成。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, fibula is an unanalyzed Latin borrowing, with the plurals fibulae and fibulas. Its anatomical family includes fibular, meaning relating to the fibula, and the combining forms fibul- and fibulo-. Tibiofibular combines tibio-, referring to the tibia, with fibular.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 骨骼义可通俗地描述为 outer lower-leg bone（小腿外侧骨），没有同样常用而精确的普通英语单词替代。器物义的近义词有 brooch（胸针，强调佩戴和装饰）、clasp（搭扣，强调连接固定）和 fastening pin（扣针，强调针状固定结构）。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the bone sense, outer lower-leg bone is a plain-language description rather than an established one-word synonym. For the artifact sense, brooch emphasizes a wearable ornament, clasp emphasizes fastening, and fastening pin emphasizes the pin-like mechanism.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“扣针”记到“腓骨”：小腿外侧的细骨，如同扣针的细长一边。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move from clasp to bone: picture the slender outer leg bone as the narrow side of a fastening pin.

senses.meaning_zh: （车辆）尾部失控地左右甩动；甩尾
senses.meaning_en: For a vehicle's rear end to swing uncontrollably from side to side.
senses.english_definition: If a vehicle fishtails, its back end slides from side to side while it is moving.
senses.collocation_en: fishtail on ice; start to fishtail

senses.meaning_zh: 鱼尾状物；鱼尾式编发或裙摆
senses.meaning_en: A shape or design resembling a fish's tail, especially in a hairstyle or skirt.
senses.english_definition: A fishtail is a shape or design that looks like the tail of a fish, such as a braid or a flared skirt hem.
senses.collocation_en: a fishtail braid; a fishtail skirt
senses.collocation_zh: 鱼尾辫；鱼尾裙
senses.sentence_en: She wore her hair in a loose fishtail braid.
senses.sentence_zh: 她把头发编成了一条松松的鱼尾辫。

etymology_story.zh: 由 fish（鱼）和 tail（尾巴）复合而成，先用于指鱼尾及鱼尾状物。动词义通过形象比喻发展而来：车辆尾部左右滑摆，就像鱼尾摆动。
etymology_story.en: The word combines fish and tail and was first used for a fish's tail and things resembling it. The vehicle verb developed through a visual comparison between a swinging rear end and a moving fish's tail.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：fish（鱼）+ tail（尾巴）→ fishtail；名词直接转作动词。常用变化：fishtails（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、fishtailed（过去式及过去分词）、fishtailing（现在分词，亦可作名词表示甩尾现象）；常见复合表达有 fishtail braid（鱼尾辫）、fishtail skirt（鱼尾裙）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: fish + tail → fishtail, with conversion from noun to verb. Common forms are fishtails, fishtailed, and fishtailing; fishtailing can also name the vehicle movement. Common compounds include fishtail braid and fishtail skirt.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 动词近义词：skid（打滑）泛指轮胎失去抓地力后的滑动；swerve（突然转向）强调行进方向骤变，可能出于主动操作；fishtail 特指车尾反复左右滑摆。名词的造型义通常直接用 fish-tail-shaped design（鱼尾状设计）解释，没有适用于各种物件的通用近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the verb, skid broadly describes sliding after losing traction, while swerve emphasizes a sudden change of direction and may be deliberate; fishtail specifically describes the rear end swinging from side to side. The noun's design sense is best paraphrased as a fish-tail-shaped design, since no single synonym covers all the objects involved.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fish + tail＝鱼尾：外形像鱼尾，动作像摆尾。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Fish + tail: either shaped like a fish's tail or swinging like one.

senses.pos: n. 复数名词，亦作不可数名词表示菜品
senses.meaning_zh: 意式团子，常用土豆和面粉制成
senses.meaning_en: Small Italian dumplings, often made with potato and flour.
senses.english_definition: Gnocchi are small Italian dumplings, often made from potato and flour, that are usually cooked in water and served with a sauce.
senses.collocation_en: potato gnocchi; gnocchi with tomato sauce
senses.collocation_zh: 意式土豆团子；配番茄酱的意式团子
senses.sentence_en: We made potato gnocchi and served them with butter and sage.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们做了意式土豆团子，配上黄油和鼠尾草一起享用。

etymology_story.zh: 借自意大利语 gnocchi，是 gnocco（团子）的复数形式。更早的来源尚不完全确定，通常与表示节结或小硬块的词联系起来，名称体现了团子小块状的外形。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Italian gnocchi, the plural of gnocco, meaning a dumpling. Its earlier origin is uncertain, but it is generally associated with words for knots or small lumps, reflecting the dumplings' shape.

morphology_enriched.zh: 在现代英语中，gnocchi 是整体借入的词，不宜拆成英语词根和词缀；在意大利语中，gnocco 的词干 gnocc- 加复数词尾 -i 构成 gnocchi。英语通常保留这一形式，也可把它作为菜品名称作不可数用法；单数 gnocco 偶见于谈论单个团子的语境。没有常用的英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, gnocchi is a whole-word borrowing rather than a combination of English roots and affixes. In Italian, the stem gnocc- takes plural -i, replacing the singular ending -o in gnocco. English normally retains gnocchi and also uses it as a mass noun for the dish; singular gnocco occurs occasionally when discussing one dumpling. There is no established family of common English derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dumpling（团子；面团制食品）是范围更广的上位词；potato dumpling（土豆团子）能描述常见的土豆版 gnocchi，但其他菜系也有土豆团子；pasta（意大利面食）是经常与 gnocchi 联系起来的食物类别，并非严格近义词，且 gnocchi 不一定含土豆。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dumpling is a broader category. Potato dumpling describes the common potato variety, but also includes dishes from other cuisines. Pasta is a related food category rather than an exact synonym, and gnocchi need not contain potato.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住一盘小面团块：gnocchi 的意大利语 -i 表示复数。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a plate of little dough lumps: Italian -i marks the plural.
