senses.meaning_zh: 以奉承、花言巧语或欺骗诱使某人做某事
senses.meaning_en: To persuade someone to do something through flattery, clever talk, or deception.
senses.english_definition: If you inveigle someone into doing something, you persuade them by flattering them or using clever or dishonest methods.
senses.collocation_en: inveigle someone into doing something; inveigle someone into an agreement
senses.collocation_zh: 用花言巧语诱使某人做某事；诱使某人接受协议
senses.sentence_en: He inveigled me into taking on most of the work.
senses.sentence_zh: 他用花言巧语诱使我承担了大部分工作。

senses.meaning_zh: 用巧言、奉承或欺骗谋得；设法混入
senses.meaning_en: To obtain something or gain entry through flattery, clever persuasion, or deception.
senses.english_definition: If you inveigle something out of someone or inveigle your way into a place, you obtain it or get in by using clever persuasion or deception.
senses.collocation_en: inveigle an invitation out of someone; inveigle one's way into a party
senses.collocation_zh: 用巧言从某人那里讨得邀请；用巧计混入聚会
senses.sentence_en: She managed to inveigle an invitation out of the host.
senses.sentence_zh: 她设法用巧言从主人那里讨到了一份邀请。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经盎格鲁法语 envegler 等词形进入英语，与古法语 aveugler“使失明”有关。字面的“蒙住眼睛”转化为使人看不清真实情况，继而发展出以奉承或欺骗诱使他人的含义。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through Anglo-French forms such as envegler and is related to Old French aveugler, meaning 'to blind.' Literal blindness developed into the figurative idea of clouding someone's judgment and thus persuading them through flattery or deception.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜把 inveigle 作为整体词基，不把开头 in- 解释为否定前缀。屈折形式：inveigles、inveigled、inveigling，后者加 -ing 时去掉词尾 e。派生词：inveiglement（诱骗；巧言诱使的行为）、inveigler（诱骗者，较少用）；inveigling 也可作分词修饰语，表示“诱人的、带有诱骗意味的”。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat inveigle as a whole base in modern English; its initial in- is not a negative prefix. Inflected forms are inveigles, inveigled, and inveigling, with final e dropped before -ing. Derivatives include inveiglement, the act of inveigling, and the less common inveigler, a person who inveigles. Inveigling can also function as a participial modifier meaning enticing or deceptively persuasive.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cajole（哄劝）强调耐心劝说或奉承，不一定涉及欺骗；coax（哄劝、劝诱）强调温和、持续地争取配合；wheedle（用甜言蜜语骗取）强调讨好式纠缠，尤其常用于从别人那里谋得东西。inveigle 更突出巧妙操纵，使人接受安排或让自己获得机会。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cajole emphasizes persistent persuasion or flattery without necessarily implying deception; coax suggests gentle, sustained encouragement; wheedle emphasizes ingratiating appeals, especially to obtain something. Inveigle more strongly suggests calculated manipulation to secure someone's cooperation or gain an opportunity.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史核心是“使看不见”：甜言蜜语蒙住判断，让人不知不觉答应。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The historical image is 'blinding': smooth talk clouds judgment until someone agrees.

pronunciation.note: 本卡选用英式读音；先听完整单词，再留意重读音节。

forms: 可数名词；复数 japes。本课不考同形动词。

senses.meaning_zh: 玩笑；恶作剧；戏谑之举（文学或旧式用语）
senses.meaning_en: A joke, prank, or playful act, chiefly in literary or old-fashioned use.
senses.english_definition: A jape is something that someone says or does to amuse people, sometimes by playing a trick.
senses.collocation_en: a harmless jape; youthful japes
senses.collocation_zh: 无伤大雅的玩笑；年轻时的恶作剧
senses.sentence_en: What began as a harmless jape soon annoyed the entire household.
senses.sentence_zh: 起初只是个无伤大雅的玩笑，很快却惹恼了全家人。

senses.meaning_zh: 开玩笑；戏谑；取笑（文学或旧式用语）
senses.meaning_en: To joke, jest, or make fun of someone, chiefly in literary or old-fashioned use.
senses.english_definition: If someone japes, they speak or behave playfully, often to make other people laugh.
senses.collocation_en: jape about something; jest and jape
senses.collocation_zh: 拿某事开玩笑；说笑打趣
senses.sentence_en: They japed about his grand plans, but he remained perfectly serious.
senses.sentence_zh: 他们拿他的宏伟计划打趣，他却始终一本正经。

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语已有动词 japen，表示开玩笑或戏弄，名词由相关动词用法发展而来。它可能与古法语 japer“吠叫、嚷叫”有关，但更早的来源并不确定。
etymology_story.en: Middle English had the verb japen, meaning to joke or trick someone, and the noun developed from the related verbal use. A connection with Old French japer, meaning to bark or yap, has been suggested, but the earlier origin is uncertain.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 jape 是不可再作常用词缀分析的基础词，名词和动词形式相同。词族包括 japes（复数或第三人称单数）、japed（过去式和过去分词）、japing（现在分词）、japer（说笑者）和 japery（戏谑、滑稽举动）；japed、japing、japer、japery 都涉及词尾不发音 e 的省略或合并。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, jape is a base word without a productive internal affix structure, and the same form serves as noun and verb. Its family includes japes, japed, japing, japer, and japery; the final silent e is dropped or merged when forming japed, japing, japer, and japery.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: joke（玩笑）最普通，既可指话语也可指行为；jest（戏言）偏文学，强调说笑；prank（恶作剧）强调实际捉弄人的行为。jape 带有文学、旧式或故作诙谐的色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Joke is the everyday term for humorous words or actions; jest is more literary and often concerns playful speech; prank emphasizes a practical trick. Jape sounds literary, old-fashioned, or deliberately whimsical.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 jape 记成“说一句逗趣的话，或做一个逗趣的动作”：名词是玩笑，动词是开玩笑。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a playful remark or trick: a jape is the joke, and to jape is to make it.

meaning: 元语言的；关于语言本身的
aliases: 元语言的；关于语言本身的

pronunciation.note: 本卡选用英式读音；先听完整单词，再留意重读音节。

forms: 形容词；一般不用比较级或最高级。
family: metalanguage 元语言；metalinguistically 从元语言角度地。

morphology.text: meta-（超出一层、谈论其本身）+ linguistic（语言的）→ metalinguistic（关于语言本身的）。
morphology.source: 作者教学分析，结合本批事实表及 https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/metalinguistic

etymology.text: 20世纪40年代英语中出现，由 meta- 和 linguistic 构成；meta- 延续希腊语词形成分。“用语言来谈语言”，就是把视角抬高一层。

usage_note: 语言学术语。解释一个词的意思、讨论句子结构，都是把语言本身当作对象。

senses.meaning_zh: 元语言的；涉及对语言本身进行描述、思考或分析的
senses.meaning_en: Concerned with describing, thinking about, or analyzing language itself.
senses.english_definition: Metalinguistic knowledge or activity involves thinking or talking about language and how it works.
senses.collocation_en: metalinguistic awareness; metalinguistic knowledge
senses.collocation_zh: 元语言意识；元语言知识
senses.sentence_en: Explaining why a sentence is ambiguous requires metalinguistic awareness.
senses.sentence_zh: 解释一个句子为什么有歧义，需要具备元语言意识。

etymology_story.zh: 该词于20世纪由 meta- 与 linguistic 组合而成，用来描述以语言本身为对象的讨论和分析。meta- 源自希腊语，在这里表示从更高一层来考察某个系统。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in the twentieth century from meta- and linguistic to describe discussion and analysis directed at language itself. Meta- comes from Greek and here signals examining a system at a higher descriptive level.

morphology_enriched.zh: 直接构词为 meta-（以某事物本身为研究对象）+ linguistic（语言的）；linguistic 又可联系 linguist（语言学家、通晓语言者）与 -ic（形容词后缀）。相关词族包括 linguistics（语言学）、linguistically（在语言方面）、metalinguistically（从元语言角度）、metalinguistics（元语言研究）及 metalanguage（元语言）。
morphology_enriched.en: The immediate structure is meta- ('about the system itself') + linguistic; linguistic can also be related to linguist and the adjective suffix -ic. Related family members include linguistics, linguistically, metalinguistically, metalinguistics, and metalanguage.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: metalingual（元语言的）含义最接近，常用于语言功能的讨论；linguistic（语言的）范围更广，不一定把语言本身当作分析对象；metacommunicative（元交际的）涉及对交际过程的说明，也可涵盖语气、手势和互动规则。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Metalingual is the closest alternative and often appears in discussions of language functions; linguistic is broader and need not involve reflection on language itself; metacommunicative concerns communication about communication, including tone, gesture, and interactional rules.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: linguistic 是“用语言”，meta- 把视角抬高一层：用语言来谈语言。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move one level above ordinary language use: use language to talk about language.

pronunciation.note: 本卡选用英式读音；先听完整单词，再留意重读音节。

forms: 可数名词；复数 somata，也可用 somas。
family: somatic 躯体的；somata 胞体的复数。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；somat-（soma 的词干形式）+ -ic → somatic（躯体的）。
morphology.source: 作者教学分析，结合本批事实表及 https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/soma

etymology.text: 经新拉丁语借入英语，来自希腊语 sōma“身体”。神经细胞的主要“身体”也就叫 soma，可和伸出去的轴突作对照。

usage_note: 本课选神经科学中的胞体义，通常含有细胞核。另有来自梵语的同形词，指古代祭饮，不混用。

senses.meaning_zh: 神经元胞体；神经细胞中含细胞核的主体部分
senses.meaning_en: The main, nucleus-containing body of a neuron.
senses.english_definition: The soma of a neuron is the main part of the cell that contains its nucleus, rather than its axon or dendrites.
senses.collocation_en: neuronal soma; the soma of a neuron
senses.collocation_zh: 神经元胞体；一个神经元的胞体
senses.sentence_en: The nucleus lies within the soma of the neuron.
senses.sentence_zh: 细胞核位于神经元的胞体内。

senses.meaning_zh: 躯体；与心灵相对的身体，或与生殖细胞相区别的身体部分（专业用语）
senses.meaning_en: The physical body, especially as distinguished from the mind or from reproductive cells.
senses.english_definition: In technical writing, the soma is the body considered separately from the mind or, in biology, from the cells that produce offspring.
senses.collocation_en: soma and psyche; germ line and soma
senses.collocation_zh: 躯体与心灵；生殖系与躯体
senses.sentence_en: The distinction between germ line and soma is central to this account of inheritance.
senses.sentence_zh: 生殖系与躯体之间的区别，是这一遗传理论的核心。

senses.meaning_zh: 苏摩；古代吠陀仪式中的神圣饮料及其原料植物
senses.meaning_en: A sacred drink used in ancient Vedic ritual, or the plant from which it was prepared.
senses.english_definition: Soma is a sacred drink described in ancient Vedic texts, and the word also names the plant used to make it.
senses.collocation_en: soma juice; a soma sacrifice
senses.collocation_zh: 苏摩汁；苏摩祭
senses.sentence_en: The priests prepared soma for the ritual offering.
senses.sentence_zh: 祭司们制备苏摩，供仪式献祭之用。

etymology_story.zh: 解剖学和生物学中的 soma 经学术拉丁语取自希腊语 sōma“身体”，后来也用于神经元的主体部分。表示吠陀祭饮的 soma 则独立借自梵语 soma，与“压榨”有关，指压榨植物制得的汁液；两者同形而不同源。
etymology_story.en: The anatomical and biological soma comes through scholarly Latin from Greek sōma, meaning 'body,' and was extended to the main body of a neuron. The Vedic drink name was borrowed independently from Sanskrit soma, associated with pressing out plant juice; the two words have separate origins.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 soma 通常作为完整基础词使用；生物学义的复数为 somas 或 somata。希腊语词干变体 somat- 构成 somatic（躯体的），并见于 somatically（在躯体方面）、somatology（人体学）、somatotype（体型）和 psychosomatic（身心相关的）；这些词不属于梵语祭饮义的词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats soma as a whole base; biological plurals include somas and somata. The Greek stem variant somat- appears in somatic and related formations such as somatically, somatology, somatotype, and psychosomatic; these do not belong to the Sanskrit drink word's family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 神经解剖学中，cell body（细胞体）是更通俗的对应表达，perikaryon（核周体、胞体）是专业近义词，严格使用时可侧重核周细胞质；body（身体）只对应较宽泛的躯体义。这些词都不能替代祭饮义的 soma。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: In neuroanatomy, cell body is the more accessible equivalent, while perikaryon is a technical near-synonym that can more narrowly emphasize cytoplasm surrounding the nucleus. Body matches only the broader physical sense; none of these replaces soma as the Vedic drink name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 生物学 soma 抓住“身体”：神经元也有一个装着细胞核的“身体”；祭饮 soma 是另一来源的独立词。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For biological soma, remember 'body': a neuron has a nucleus-containing body too. Keep the independently derived ritual drink name separate.

senses.meaning_zh: 士的宁；番木鳖碱，一种剧毒生物碱
senses.meaning_en: A highly poisonous alkaloid obtained from certain plants of the genus Strychnos.
senses.english_definition: Strychnine is a highly poisonous substance obtained from certain plants and formerly used in some poisons for killing animals.
senses.collocation_en: strychnine poisoning; strychnine nitrate
senses.collocation_zh: 士的宁中毒；硝酸士的宁
senses.sentence_en: The laboratory detected strychnine in the sample.
senses.sentence_zh: 实验室在样本中检出了士的宁。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在19世纪经法语 strychnine 进入英语，由植物属名 Strychnos 加化学物质后缀构成。属名最终源于希腊语 strukhnos，一个用于某些茄科植物的古代名称，后来被用于命名另一植物属。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English in the nineteenth century through French strychnine, formed from the plant genus name Strychnos with a chemical suffix. The genus name ultimately reflects Greek strukhnos, an ancient name for certain nightshade plants that was later applied to a different botanical genus.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可作科学命名分析：strychn-（来自属名 Strychnos）+ -ine（常见化学物质后缀）。相关专业词包括 strychnic（士的宁的）和 strychninism（士的宁中毒状态）；strychnia 是旧式异名，Strychnos 是来源属名。
morphology_enriched.en: Its scientific naming structure is strychn- (from Strychnos) + -ine, a common chemical suffix. Related technical words include strychnic ('relating to strychnine') and strychninism ('strychnine poisoning'); strychnia is an older alternative name, and Strychnos is the source genus name.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: strychnia 是士的宁的旧称，属于真正的同义名称；alkaloid（生物碱）和 poison（毒物）只是上位词，前者说明化学类别，后者说明毒性作用，均不能精确替代 strychnine。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Strychnia is an older name for the same substance. Alkaloid and poison are broader category terms rather than exact synonyms: alkaloid identifies the chemical class, while poison identifies the harmful action.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 植物属名 Strychnos 留下 strychn-，加上化学词尾 -ine：来自该属植物的剧毒生物碱。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect Strychnos with the chemical ending -ine: the plant name anchors the name of its poisonous alkaloid.

meaning: 锛；刃口横向安装的木工斧
aliases: 锛；刃口横向安装的木工斧
刃口横向安装的木工斧

pronunciation.note: 本卡选用英式读音；先听完整单词，再留意重读音节。

forms: 可数名词；复数 adzes；美式另可拼作 adz。
family: adz 美式拼写；adzed 用锛削过的。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；adze + -ed → adzed（用锛削过的），词尾 e 与后缀衔接。
morphology.source: 作者教学分析，结合本批事实表及 https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/adze

etymology.text: 承自古英语 adesa，是英语中很早就有的木工工具名。记住它的刃口横着装在柄上，像向自己刮削木材的斧。

usage_note: 刃口通常与柄成直角，用于削平或挖削木材；不同于普通斧头的刃口方向。

senses.meaning_zh: 锛；刃口与柄横向垂直的木工削切工具
senses.meaning_en: A woodworking tool with a cutting edge set at right angles to its handle.
senses.english_definition: An adze is a tool with a curved blade set across its handle, used for shaping or smoothing wood.
senses.collocation_en: a carpenter's adze; shape wood with an adze
senses.collocation_zh: 木工锛；用锛修整木材
senses.sentence_en: The carpenter used an adze to shape the curved surface.

senses.meaning_zh: 用锛削；用锛修整（木工专业用语）
senses.meaning_en: To shape or smooth wood with an adze.
senses.english_definition: If you adze a piece of wood, you shape or smooth it by cutting it with an adze.
senses.collocation_en: adze a beam; adze timber
senses.collocation_zh: 用锛修整梁木；用锛削木料

etymology_story.zh: adze 承自古英语 adesa，是历史悠久的木工工具名称，更早的来源不明确。其主要含义一直围绕这种横刃工具，后来又由名词转用为动词，表示用锛削木。
etymology_story.en: Adze descends from Old English adesa, an old name for a woodworking tool whose earlier origin is unclear. Its central meaning has remained tied to the transverse-bladed tool, and the noun also became a verb meaning to work wood with it.

morphology_enriched.zh: adze 是基础词，动词由名词零派生而来；美式英语也有拼写 adz。词族包括 adzes（复数或第三人称单数）、adzed（过去式、过去分词及“用锛削过的”）、adzing（现在分词）和 adzer（用锛削木者）；adzed、adzing、adzer 分别接 -ed、-ing、-er 时省去词尾 e。
morphology_enriched.en: Adze is a base word, with the verb formed from the noun by conversion; adz is an alternative American spelling. Its family includes adzes, adzed, adzing, and adzer; the final e is dropped before -ed, -ing, and -er.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: axe（斧）、hatchet（短柄小斧）和 gouge（圆凿）是相关工具，均非严格同义词：axe 的刃口通常与柄所在方向平行，hatchet 强调小巧、可单手使用，gouge 用弧形刃凿削；adze 的特征是横向安装的刃口。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Axe, hatchet, and gouge name related tools rather than exact synonyms: an axe generally has its edge aligned with the handle, a hatchet is a small one-handed axe, and a gouge cuts with a curved chisel edge. An adze is distinguished by its transverse cutting edge.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“横刃削木”：工具叫 adze，用它削木也叫 adze。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the sideways cutting edge: the tool is an adze, and using it to shape wood is to adze.

meaning: 矫情的；煽情而显得可笑的
aliases: 矫情的；煽情而显得可笑的

pronunciation.note: 本卡选用英式读音；先听完整单词，再留意重读音节。

forms: 形容词；通常用 more bathetic、most bathetic。
family: bathos 矫情的煽情；bathetically 矫情地。

morphology.text: bathos（过度煽情）+ -etic → bathetic（矫情的）；词尾 -os 被 -etic 替换，形式仿照 pathetic。
morphology.source: 作者教学分析，结合本批事实表及 https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/bathetic

etymology.text: 在英语中由 bathos 仿照 pathetic 的样子构成。bathos 原是希腊语“深度”，后来用于写作中从崇高跌向浅薄的效果，因而带上“煽情过头”的意思。

usage_note: 常带贬义，形容文艺作品或言辞过分煽情、缺乏真情；也可涉及从庄严突降到可笑的效果。

senses.meaning_zh: 煽情过度而显得可笑的；矫情的
senses.meaning_en: Excessively sentimental in a way that seems ridiculous.
senses.english_definition: If something is bathetic, it tries so hard to make people feel strong emotions that it seems silly or insincere.
senses.collocation_en: bathetic sentimentality; a bathetic ending
senses.collocation_zh: 过度而可笑的伤感；矫情的结尾
senses.sentence_en: The film's bathetic ending left the audience laughing instead of crying.
senses.sentence_zh: 这部电影的结尾煽情过度，观众非但没有落泪，反而笑了起来。

senses.meaning_zh: 从崇高骤降至平庸而显得可笑的；令人泄气的
senses.meaning_en: Absurdly anticlimactic through a descent from the elevated to the commonplace.
senses.english_definition: A bathetic change or conclusion moves from something grand or serious to something ordinary or trivial, often with a ridiculous effect.
senses.collocation_en: a bathetic conclusion; a bathetic contrast
senses.collocation_zh: 陡然落入平庸的收尾；崇高与琐碎之间的滑稽反差
senses.sentence_en: After promising to change the world, he ended with a bathetic reminder about parking permits.
senses.sentence_zh: 他先承诺要改变世界，最后却提醒大家办理停车证，崇高骤然跌入琐碎，令人啼笑皆非。

etymology_story.zh: bathetic 在英语中由 bathos 仿照 pathetic 构成。bathos 源自希腊语中表示“深度”的词，后来成为文学批评术语，指从崇高跌入平庸的效果，并进一步关联到过度煽情造成的可笑效果。
etymology_story.en: Bathetic was formed in English from bathos on the model of pathetic. Bathos comes from a Greek word meaning “depth” and became a literary term for a descent from the elevated to the commonplace, later also associated with ridiculous effects produced by excessive sentimentality.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词关系：bathos（突降法；过度煽情）→ bathetic（具有这种效果的），形式仿照 pathetic；不能机械地把它分析为 bathos 加一个常规的 -etic 后缀。核心词族：bathos（名词）、bathetic（形容词）、bathetically（副词：矫情地；以突降方式）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: bathos → bathetic, with the adjective shaped on the model of pathetic; it is not a straightforward attachment of a regular suffix -etic to bathos. The core family is bathos, the adjective bathetic, and the adverb bathetically.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mawkish（伤感得令人腻烦的）侧重甜腻的感伤；sentimental（感伤的；多愁善感的）未必带贬义；anticlimactic（未达高潮而令人失望的）侧重期待落空。bathetic 尤其突出煽情失败或格调骤降所产生的可笑效果。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mawkish emphasizes cloying sentiment; sentimental can describe emotion without necessarily criticizing it; anticlimactic emphasizes disappointed expectations. Bathetic particularly suggests the ridiculous effect of failed emotional grandeur or a sudden drop in tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bathos 的“深度”变成格调的“跌落”：情感拔得太高，落下来反而可笑。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the “depth” of bathos with a downward drop in tone: emotion reaches too high, then falls into absurdity.

pronunciation.note: 本卡选用英式读音；先听完整单词，再留意重读音节。

forms: 第三人称 circumlocutes；过去式及过去分词 circumlocuted；现在分词 circumlocuting。
family: circumlocution 迂回表达；circumlocutory 拐弯抹角的。

morphology.text: circumlocution（名词：拐弯抹角的说法）→ circumlocute（动词：说话拐弯抹角），是由名词逆构出动词；词源助记：circum-（绕着）+ locut-（说话）→ “绕着说”。末尾 e 是拼写的一部分，不是后缀。

etymology.text: 英语从 circumlocution 逆构出这个动词；该名词源于拉丁语 circumlocutio“绕着说话”。把语言想成绕圈而没有直接到达重点。

usage_note: 不及物动词，较少见且正式；日常更常说 beat about the bush。

senses.meaning_zh: 说话拐弯抹角；用迂回冗长的方式表达
senses.meaning_en: To express something indirectly or in unnecessarily many words.
senses.english_definition: If someone circumlocutes, they use indirect or unnecessarily long expressions instead of saying something simply and directly.
senses.collocation_en: tend to circumlocute; circumlocute rather than answer
senses.collocation_zh: 往往说话拐弯抹角；绕着说而不直接回答
senses.sentence_en: When asked why the project had failed, he began to circumlocute.
senses.sentence_zh: 被问到项目为何失败时，他开始拐弯抹角地说话。

etymology_story.zh: circumlocute 是从英语名词 circumlocution 逆构而来的较少见动词。该名词最终源自拉丁语 circumlocutio，结合了“绕着”和“说话”的成分，字面意象就是“绕着说”。
etymology_story.en: Circumlocute is a relatively uncommon verb back-formed from the English noun circumlocution. The noun ultimately comes from Latin circumlocutio, combining elements meaning “around” and “speaking”: literally, speaking around something.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词关系：circumlocution（迂回表达）→ circumlocute（迂回地说），属于名词逆构动词；词源成分为 circum-（绕着）和 locut-（说）。核心词族：circumlocute、circumlocution、circumlocutory（迂回表达的）、circumlocutionary（迂回表达的）；动词形式为 circumlocutes、circumlocuted、circumlocuting。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: circumlocution → circumlocute, a noun-to-verb back-formation; the historical components are circum- “around” and locut- “speak.” The core family includes circumlocute, circumlocution, circumlocutory, and circumlocutionary; verb forms are circumlocutes, circumlocuted, and circumlocuting.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: equivocate（含糊其辞）强调借模糊措辞逃避明确表态；prevaricate（支吾搪塞）通常暗示有意回避真相；beat around the bush（绕圈子）是常用的非正式表达。circumlocute 更侧重表达迂回或冗长，并不必然表示撒谎。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Equivocate emphasizes avoiding a definite position through ambiguity; prevaricate usually suggests deliberately avoiding the truth; beat around the bush is a common informal expression for delaying the main point. Circumlocute focuses on indirectness or wordiness and does not necessarily imply dishonesty.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: circum-＝绕着，locut-＝说：话绕了一圈，还没到重点。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Circum- means “around” and locut- means “speak”: the words circle the point.

pronunciation.note: 本卡选用英式读音；先听完整单词，再留意重读音节。

forms: 英式 hydrolyse；美式 hydrolyze。第三人称 hydrolyses；过去式及过去分词 hydrolysed；现在分词 hydrolysing。
family: hydrolysis 水解；hydrolytic 水解的。

morphology.text: hydro-（水）+ -lyse（分解）→ hydrolyse（通过与水反应而分解）。
morphology.source: 作者教学分析，结合本批事实表及 https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/hydrolyze

etymology.text: 19世纪英语从 hydrolysis 形成相应动词，保留了希腊语的水与分解两个成分；-lyse 是英式形式，-lyze 是美式形式。

usage_note: 化学用语，可及物也可不及物。英美两种拼写表达同一反应，不另作不同词义。

senses.meaning_zh: 使水解；通过与水反应而分解
senses.meaning_en: To break a substance down through a chemical reaction with water.
senses.english_definition: If something hydrolyses a substance, it causes bonds in that substance to break through a chemical reaction involving water.
senses.collocation_en: hydrolyse proteins; hydrolyse an ester
senses.collocation_zh: 水解蛋白质；水解酯
senses.sentence_en: These enzymes hydrolyse proteins into smaller peptides.
senses.sentence_zh: 这些酶将蛋白质水解成较小的肽。

senses.meaning_zh: 发生水解；与水反应而分解
senses.meaning_en: To undergo chemical breakdown by reacting with water.
senses.english_definition: If a substance hydrolyses, bonds in it break as it reacts with water.
senses.collocation_en: hydrolyse readily; hydrolyse slowly
senses.collocation_zh: 容易水解；缓慢水解
senses.sentence_en: The compound hydrolyses slowly in water at room temperature.
senses.sentence_zh: 这种化合物在室温下会在水中缓慢水解。

etymology_story.zh: hydrolyse 是19世纪根据 hydrolysis（水解）形成的动词，其希腊语词源成分分别表示“水”和“松开、分解”。hydrolyse 是英式拼写，hydrolyze 是美式拼写，二者表示同一化学过程。
etymology_story.en: Hydrolyse developed in the nineteenth century as a verb corresponding to hydrolysis, whose Greek elements mean “water” and “loosening or breaking apart.” Hydrolyse is the British spelling and hydrolyze the American spelling of the same chemical process.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词可分析为 hydro-（水）+ -lyse（使分解）。核心词族：hydrolyse／hydrolyze（水解）、hydrolysis（水解作用）、hydrolytic（水解的）、hydrolytically（通过水解）、hydrolysable／hydrolyzable（可水解的）、hydrolysate（水解产物）；英式动词形式为 hydrolyses、hydrolysed、hydrolysing。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: hydro- “water” + -lyse “break down.” The core family includes hydrolyse/hydrolyze, hydrolysis, hydrolytic, hydrolytically, hydrolysable/hydrolyzable, and hydrolysate, meaning a product of hydrolysis. British verb forms are hydrolyses, hydrolysed, and hydrolysing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: decompose（分解）泛指物质发生化学分解；cleave（裂解）强调化学键断裂；break down（分解）是较通俗的概括。hydrolyse 专指水参与反应导致的键断裂，不能等同于单纯溶解。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Decompose broadly describes chemical breakdown; cleave emphasizes the breaking of a bond; break down is a less technical general expression. Hydrolyse specifically involves bond cleavage through reaction with water and is different from simply dissolving.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hydro- 水 + -lyse 分解：水参与反应，把化学键拆开。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hydro- is water and -lyse is breaking apart: water participates in splitting chemical bonds.

meaning: 头脑昏沉的；思路不清的

usage_note: 主要用于英式口语，常说 feel muzzy，也可形容影像或轮廓模糊；本课学人的头脑状态。

senses.meaning_zh: 头脑昏沉的；思维不清的
senses.meaning_en: Mentally confused or unable to think clearly.
senses.english_definition: If you feel muzzy, you cannot think clearly, often because you are tired, unwell, or have drunk alcohol.
senses.collocation_en: feel muzzy; a muzzy head
senses.collocation_zh: 感到头脑昏沉；昏沉的脑袋
senses.sentence_en: I still felt muzzy when I woke up after the long flight.
senses.sentence_zh: 长途飞行后醒来时，我仍觉得头脑昏沉。

senses.meaning_zh: 模糊不清的；不明确的
senses.meaning_en: Indistinct, blurred, or lacking clear detail.
senses.english_definition: If an image, impression, or idea is muzzy, it is not clear or sharply defined.
senses.collocation_en: a muzzy image; muzzy thinking
senses.collocation_zh: 模糊的图像；含混的思考
senses.sentence_en: The old television showed a muzzy image of the match.
senses.sentence_zh: 那台旧电视播出的比赛画面模糊不清。

etymology_story.zh: muzzy 在18世纪的英语中已有记录，但确切来源不明；有词源解释将它与表示迷糊或醉态的 muzz 联系起来。它后来既可描述头脑昏沉，也可描述图像、印象或想法模糊不清；与 fuzzy 的联想可作助记，不能视为确定词源。
etymology_story.en: Muzzy is recorded in eighteenth-century English, but its precise origin is uncertain; some accounts connect it with muzz, associated with bewilderment or intoxication. It came to describe both mental cloudiness and indistinct images, impressions, or ideas; its resemblance to fuzzy is useful for memory but is not an established derivation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习中宜把 muzzy 作为整体词干，不强行拆分不确定的词根。词族及变化：muzzier（更昏沉的）、muzziest（最昏沉的）、muzzily（昏沉地；模糊地）、muzziness（昏沉；模糊）、muzzy-headed（头脑昏沉的）；接比较级、最高级或相关后缀时通常将 y 改为 i。
morphology_enriched.en: For modern learning, treat muzzy as a whole stem rather than forcing an uncertain root analysis. Its family and inflections include muzzier, muzziest, muzzily, muzziness, and muzzy-headed; final y normally changes to i before the relevant endings.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: groggy（昏昏沉沉的）常强调睡眠不足、药物或疾病造成的虚弱迟钝；fuzzy（模糊的）可形容思维或轮廓不清；dazed（发懵的）常指受惊、受伤或震动后的短暂失神。muzzy 多见于英式非正式表达，突出头脑像蒙着雾。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Groggy often suggests weakness or sluggishness after sleep loss, medication, or illness; fuzzy describes unclear thinking or outlines; dazed often suggests temporary confusion after shock or injury. Muzzy is chiefly informal British usage and evokes a clouded mental state.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 muzzy 联想成脑中蒙着一层雾：人昏沉，东西也看不清。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Imagine a mist over the mind: you feel clouded, and things seem indistinct.

senses.meaning_zh: 橄榄石：常呈橄榄绿色的镁铁硅酸盐矿物
senses.meaning_en: A usually olive-green magnesium–iron silicate mineral.
senses.english_definition: Olivine is a mineral containing magnesium, iron, silicon, and oxygen that is usually green and is common in many rocks from the Earth's mantle.
senses.collocation_en: olivine crystals; olivine-rich rocks
senses.collocation_zh: 橄榄石晶体；富含橄榄石的岩石
senses.sentence_en: Small green crystals of olivine were visible in the basalt.
senses.sentence_zh: 这块玄武岩中可以看到细小的绿色橄榄石晶体。

etymology_story.zh: olivine 于18世纪末从德语 Olivin 进入英语，名称来自表示“橄榄”的 Olive，指这种矿物常见的橄榄绿色。它的命名依据是颜色，而非与橄榄植物有成分上的联系。
etymology_story.en: Olivine entered English in the late eighteenth century from German Olivin, named from Olive, meaning “olive,” because of the mineral's characteristic olive-green colour. The name refers to its appearance rather than any material connection with the plant.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是借入的矿物名称；现代形式可联系 olive（橄榄；橄榄色）去掉末尾 e，再加矿物名称词尾 -ine，但这不是英语内部最初造词的历史过程。相关形式：olivines（指不同种类或成分的橄榄石时的复数）、olivinic／olivinous（橄榄石的；含橄榄石的，专业用语）；olivine-rich 表示“富含橄榄石的”。
morphology_enriched.en: This is a borrowed mineral name; its modern form can be associated with olive minus final e plus the mineral-name ending -ine, although it was not originally coined this way within English. Related forms include olivines for different varieties or compositions, the technical adjectives olivinic and olivinous, and the compound olivine-rich.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: peridot（贵橄榄石）指宝石级橄榄石，并非所有橄榄石都适用；forsterite（镁橄榄石）是橄榄石固溶体系列的富镁端元；fayalite（铁橄榄石）是富铁端元。三者都是相关名称，不能在所有语境中与 olivine 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Peridot is gem-quality olivine and does not describe every specimen; forsterite is the magnesium end member of the olivine solid-solution series; fayalite is the iron end member. These are related names rather than universally interchangeable synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: olive 橄榄绿 → olivine 橄榄石：先记颜色，再记矿物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Olive green → olivine: remember the mineral through its characteristic colour.

pronunciation.note: 本卡选用英式读音；先听完整单词，再留意重读音节。

forms: 不可数疾病名称，通常不用复数。
family: peritoneum 腹膜；peritonitic 腹膜炎的。

morphology.text: periton-（peritoneum 腹膜的词干）+ -itis（炎症）→ peritonitis（腹膜炎）。
morphology.source: 作者教学分析，结合本批事实表及 https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/peritonitis

etymology.text: 18世纪由 peritoneum 的词干加 -itis 形成；前者经拉丁语来自希腊语表示包围腹部的膜，后者是希腊语来源的炎症词尾。记住“腹膜发生炎症”。

usage_note: 医学疾病名；注意 peritoneum 是组织名称，peritonitis 是发生在该组织的炎症。

senses.meaning_zh: 腹膜炎
senses.meaning_en: inflammation of the peritoneum
senses.english_definition: Peritonitis is inflammation of the thin membrane that lines the abdominal cavity and covers many of its organs.
senses.collocation_en: acute peritonitis; bacterial peritonitis
senses.collocation_zh: 急性腹膜炎；细菌性腹膜炎
senses.sentence_en: The examination revealed signs of acute peritonitis.
senses.sentence_zh: 检查发现了急性腹膜炎的体征。

etymology_story.zh: 该词由医学拉丁语 peritoneum（腹膜）的词干与表示炎症的 -itis 构成。Peritoneum 源自希腊语 peritonaion，其相关动词意为“在周围伸展”，描绘了腹膜包覆腹腔内结构的形态。
etymology_story.en: The word combines the stem of medical Latin peritoneum with -itis, meaning inflammation. Peritoneum comes from Greek peritonaion, related to a verb meaning to stretch around, describing the membrane's enveloping position.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代医学构词：periton-（腹膜；与 peritone- 同源的词干形式）+ -itis（炎症）→ peritonitis。主要相关词：peritoneum（腹膜）、peritoneal（腹膜的）、peritonitic（腹膜炎的）、intraperitoneal（腹膜腔内的）、retroperitoneal（腹膜后的）。CEFR-C2 为编辑估级，并非官方逐词定级。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern medical formation: periton- (peritoneum, a stem form related to peritone-) + -itis (inflammation) → peritonitis. Principal related forms include peritoneum, peritoneal, peritonitic, intraperitoneal, and retroperitoneal. CEFR-C2 is an editorial estimate, not an official word-level classification.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: peritoneal inflammation（腹膜炎症）是直接同义改述；serositis（浆膜炎）范围更广，也包括其他浆膜的炎症；intra-abdominal infection（腹腔内感染）是相关概念，但并非所有腹膜炎都由感染引起。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Peritoneal inflammation is a direct descriptive equivalent. Serositis is broader and includes inflammation of other serous membranes. Intra-abdominal infection is related, but it is not equivalent because peritonitis can have noninfectious causes.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: periton- 指腹膜，-itis 指炎症：腹膜发炎就是 peritonitis。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Periton- names the membrane; -itis names inflammation: the abdominal lining becomes inflamed.

pronunciation.note: 本卡选用英式读音；先听完整单词，再留意重读音节。

forms: 比较级 weenier；最高级 weeniest。不要把 weenies 当作本课形容词的比较形式。

morphology.text: wee（小）+ -ny（小称词尾）→ weeny（极小的）；这个词尾的形式受到 tiny 一类词的影响。
morphology.source: 作者教学分析，结合本批事实表及 https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/weeny

etymology.text: 18世纪由 wee 加上像 tiny 词尾那样的小称成分形成。可以用看东西时捏起两根手指表示“一丁点”的动作助记。

usage_note: 口语，常带亲昵或强调语气，如 a weeny bit；正式测量宜用具体数值。

etymology_story.zh: Weeny 是 wee（小的）的强化或小称形式，一般认为形成于18世纪末。它的词形可能受到 tiny 等表示微小的词影响，后来尤其常见于 teeny-weeny 这样的押韵组合。
etymology_story.en: Weeny developed as an emphatic or diminutive form of wee, generally dated to the late eighteenth century. Its form may have been influenced by words such as tiny, and it became especially familiar in rhyming combinations such as teeny-weeny.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代宜分析为 wee（小）经表现性扩展形成 weeny，不宜把 -ny 当作可以自由构词的常规后缀。屈折形式：weenier（更小的）、weeniest（最小的）；相关形式：wee、teeny-weeny、teeny-weenie（极小的，异体拼写）。CEFR-C2 为编辑估级，并非官方逐词定级。
morphology_enriched.en: Synchronically, weeny is best treated as an expressive extension of wee rather than as a transparent formation with a productive suffix -ny. Inflected forms are weenier and weeniest; related forms include wee, teeny-weeny, and the spelling variant teeny-weenie. CEFR-C2 is an editorial estimate, not an official word-level classification.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tiny（极小的）最中性、适用范围最广；teeny（小小的）同样口语化、带俏皮语气；minute（微小的）较正式，常强调小到难以察觉。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tiny is the most neutral and widely applicable. Teeny is similarly informal and playful. Minute is more formal and often suggests something so small that it is difficult to notice.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 wee 的“小”想到 weeny 的“小小一点儿”，再用两指捏出一丁点距离。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with wee, meaning small, and imagine pinching your fingers together to show a weeny amount.

etymology_story.zh: 表示婆罗门阶层成员的 Brahman 来自梵语 brāhmaṇa；哲学义“梵”对应梵语 brahman，二者历史相关，但所指不同。牛种名称取自其印度血统，而美国社会精英义则借用了婆罗门在传统社会中的高阶层地位这一联想。
etymology_story.en: Brahman meaning a member of the priestly class comes from Sanskrit brāhmaṇa; the philosophical term represents Sanskrit brahman, a historically related but distinct word. The cattle name reflects Indian ancestry, while the American elite sense draws on the association with high social rank.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 Brahman 是整体借入词，不宜拆成 brah + man；指人时复数为 Brahmans。主要派生词：Brahmanism（婆罗门教或相关宗教传统）、Brahmanic／Brahmanical（婆罗门的）；Brahmin 是指阶层成员及社会精英时的相关异体，另有 Brahminism、Brahminical；哲学义通常大写且不可数。CEFR-C2 为编辑估级，并非官方逐词定级。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Brahman is a borrowed lexical base, not brah + man; its personal plural is Brahmans. Principal derivatives include Brahmanism, Brahmanic, and Brahmanical. Brahmin is a related variant for the caste member and social-elite senses, with Brahminism and Brahminical as related forms; philosophical Brahman is normally capitalized and uncountable. CEFR-C2 is an editorial estimate, not an official word-level classification.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Brahmin（婆罗门；社会精英）在阶层成员义和美国精英义上可与 Brahman 互换，但通常不用于“梵”或牛种；the Absolute（绝对者、绝对实在）可解释哲学义，但宗教适用范围更广；zebu（瘤牛）范围更广，Brahman 是具有瘤牛血统的特定牛种。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Brahmin is interchangeable in the caste-member and American elite senses, but generally not for the philosophical reality or cattle breed. The Absolute is an explanatory equivalent for philosophical Brahman but has wider religious application. Zebu is broader: Brahman names a particular breed with zebu ancestry.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Separate the person from the principle: a Brahman belongs to a social class; Brahman names ultimate reality. The cattle and Boston elite senses are later naming extensions.

etymology_story.zh: Chirrup 在16世纪作为 chirp 的表现性变体出现，属于模仿鸟鸣的拟声词。增加的音节使它听起来更像一串轻快细碎的叫声，后来也用来描写人欢快尖细的说话声。
etymology_story.en: Chirrup appeared in the sixteenth century as an expressive variant of chirp, an imitation of a bird's call. Its extra syllable suggests a lively sequence of small sounds, and its use later extended to cheerful human speech.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代把 chirrup 作为整体拟声词根；名词与动词同形，不宜把 -up 分析成独立后缀。屈折形式：chirrups、chirruped、chirruping；较少见的施事名词为 chirruper（发出啁啾声者）；chirp、chirping、chirpy 是相关拟声词族，并非都直接由 chirrup 派生。CEFR-C2 为编辑估级，并非官方逐词定级。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat chirrup as a whole imitative base; its noun and verb share the same form, and -up is not a separate suffix here. Inflected forms are chirrups, chirruped, and chirruping; chirruper is an uncommon agent noun. Chirp, chirping, and chirpy belong to the related sound-symbolic family rather than all being direct derivatives of chirrup. CEFR-C2 is an editorial estimate, not an official word-level classification.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chirp usually emphasizes a short, clear call. Tweet often suggests a light, high bird note. Twitter emphasizes a rapid series of small sounds. Chirrup commonly adds an impression of liveliness or cheerfulness.

etymology_story.zh: Cumulate 来自拉丁语 cumulāre（堆起）的分词词干 cumulāt-，其基础名词 cumulus 意为“堆”。英语保留了“逐渐堆积”的核心意义，地质学又用它指晶体聚集形成的岩石及相关结构。
etymology_story.en: Cumulate comes from Latin cumulāt-, the participial stem of cumulāre, meaning to heap up, from cumulus, a heap. English retained the idea of gradual accumulation, while geology developed specialized uses for rocks and textures formed by collected crystals.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：cumul-（堆、聚集）+ -ate（动词或形容词构形成分）；名词为同形专业用法。动词词尾读 /eɪt/，形容词和名词通常读 /ət/。主要词族：cumulation（累积）、cumulative（累积的）、cumulatively（累积地）、accumulate（积累）、accumulation（积累）、accumulator（蓄积器；累加器）、cumulus（积云；原义为堆）。CEFR-C2 为编辑估级，并非官方逐词定级。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: cumul- (heap or accumulation) + -ate, a verbal or adjectival formative; the noun is a specialized use of the same form. The verb ends in /eɪt/, while the adjective and noun normally end in /ət/. Principal family members include cumulation, cumulative, cumulatively, accumulate, accumulation, accumulator, and cumulus. CEFR-C2 is an editorial estimate, not an official word-level classification.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: accumulate（积累）是通用英语中最自然、最常见的近义词；amass（大量积聚）强调形成很大的数量，常涉及财富或收藏；aggregate（汇集）强调把分散的项目合为总体，技术和统计语境较常见。这些词主要对应 cumulate 的动词义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Accumulate is the usual general-English equivalent. Amass emphasizes gathering a large quantity, often of wealth or possessions. Aggregate emphasizes combining separate items into a whole and is common in technical or statistical contexts. These equivalents primarily concern the verb.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cumul- 就是“堆”：东西越积越成堆；地质学中，晶体聚成堆就形成堆晶岩。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cumul- means heap: quantities build into a heap, and accumulated crystals form a geological cumulate.

etymology_story.zh: dishy 由 dish 加形容词后缀 -y 构成；其“迷人的”义来自二十世纪俚语中用 dish 称呼有吸引力的人的用法。“八卦丰富的”义则与 dish 表示“八卦消息”以及 dish the dirt 表示“传播八卦”的用法相关。
etymology_story.en: Dishy was formed from dish and the adjective suffix -y; its attractiveness sense developed from the twentieth-century slang use of dish for an attractive person. Its gossip sense is related to dish meaning gossip and expressions such as dish the dirt.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：dish（俚语：迷人的人；八卦消息）+ -y（具有……特点的）→ dishy。直接词族包括 dishier（更迷人的；更富八卦的）、dishiest（最迷人的；最富八卦的）和 dishiness（迷人；八卦丰富的特质）；相关基础词 dish 兼作名词和动词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: dish, in its slang senses of an attractive person or gossip, + -y, meaning having the qualities of, → dishy. The direct family includes dishier, dishiest, and dishiness; the related base dish functions as both a noun and a verb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: attractive（有吸引力的）语气中性、适用范围广；sexy（性感的）更直接强调性吸引力；gossipy（爱谈八卦的；充满八卦的）对应 dishy 的八卦义，但不一定带有 dishy 所暗示的趣味性或内幕感。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Attractive is neutral and broadly applicable; sexy emphasizes sexual appeal more directly. Gossipy matches the gossip sense of dishy but does not necessarily suggest the same entertaining or revealing quality.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: dish 可以比喻“养眼的人”，也可以指“八卦料”；加 -y，就是“很养眼的”或“很有料的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A dish can be an attractive person or a serving of gossip: dishy means appealing to look at or full of juicy details.

senses.collocation_en: Egyptian faience; faience beads

etymology_story.zh: 英语 faience 借自法语 faïence，该名称来自以制作锡釉陶器闻名的意大利城市 Faenza。后来，人们也将这个名称用于古埃及外观相似的施釉石英材料，尽管其胎体与陶土不同。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed faience from French faïence, a name derived from Faenza, an Italian city renowned for tin-glazed pottery. The term was later applied to visually similar ancient Egyptian glazed quartz objects, although their bodies differ from clay pottery.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为不可再作常用词缀拆分的借词；faïence 是保留法语分音符的拼写变体。没有常用的派生词系列；faience ware（费昂斯制品）和 faience-like（类似费昂斯的）属于透明的组合表达。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, faience is a borrowed base without a productive internal root-and-affix breakdown; faïence is a spelling variant retaining the French diaeresis. It has no common series of derivatives; faience ware and faience-like are transparent combinations.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tin-glazed earthenware（锡釉陶器）是陶瓷义最明确的释义性近义表达；maiolica（意大利锡釉彩陶）通常特指意大利传统；delftware（代尔夫特式锡釉陶器）通常指荷兰及相关英国传统的制品。这些名称不能直接替代 Egyptian faience。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tin-glazed earthenware is the clearest descriptive equivalent for the pottery sense. Maiolica usually identifies the Italian tradition, while delftware usually identifies Dutch and related British traditions; these terms are not direct substitutes for Egyptian faience.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Faenza 城留下 faience 这个名字：先记锡釉彩陶，再单独记古埃及的施釉石英材料。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Faenza gives faience its name: remember tin-glazed pottery first, then the separate Egyptian glazed-quartz sense.

etymology_story.zh: fluvial 来自拉丁语 fluvialis，意为“河流的”，其基础词 fluvius 意为“河流”，与 fluere“流动”相关。英语保留了这一核心含义，并在地理学和地质学中用它描述河流环境及河流塑造地表的作用。
etymology_story.en: Fluvial comes from Latin fluvialis, meaning of a river, from fluvius, river, which is related to fluere, to flow. English retains this core meaning, especially in geography and geology for river environments and the processes that shape landscapes.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学术构词分析：fluvi-（河流）+ -al（……的）→ fluvial。相关形式包括 fluvially（通过河流作用地，专业用语）、fluviatile（河流的，较少见），以及共享河流词根的 fluvioglacial／glaciofluvial（冰川融水河流作用的）和 fluviolacustrine（河湖的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern learned analysis: fluvi-, river, + -al, relating to, → fluvial. Related forms include the technical adverb fluvially, the less common adjective fluviatile, and compounds sharing the river stem, including fluvioglacial/glaciofluvial and fluviolacustrine.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: riverine（河流及其周边的）常侧重河流环境或生态；alluvial（冲积的）专指流水沉积形成的物质或地貌；riparian（河岸的）侧重河岸地带。fluvial 的范围较广，还包括侵蚀和搬运过程。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Riverine often emphasizes river settings or ecosystems; alluvial specifically concerns material or landforms produced by deposition from flowing water; riparian concerns riverbanks. Fluvial is broader and also covers erosion and transport.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fluvi- 表示河流：河水流到哪里，fluvial 就描述哪里的河流环境或作用。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect fluvi- with a flowing river: fluvial describes the river setting and what river water does.

senses.collocation_zh: 践行多神信仰的人；古代多神信仰者
senses.sentence_en: Many ancient Greeks were polytheists who worshipped several gods.
senses.sentence_zh: 许多古希腊人是崇拜多个神的多神信仰者。

senses.meaning_zh: 多神论的；信奉多个神的，通常更常用 polytheistic
senses.meaning_en: Believing in or involving more than one god; polytheistic is more usual.
senses.english_definition: A polytheist religion or society recognizes more than one god.
senses.collocation_en: a polytheist religion; a polytheist society
senses.collocation_zh: 一种多神教；一个信奉多神的社会
senses.sentence_en: The exhibition explores religious life in a polytheist society.
senses.sentence_zh: 这场展览探讨了一个多神信仰社会中的宗教生活。

etymology_story.zh: polytheist 属于以希腊语 polys“多”和 theos“神”为基础形成的宗教词汇，与 polytheism“多神论”同族。英语用 -ist 表示持有某种信仰的人，也可用相同形式作形容词。
etymology_story.en: Polytheist belongs to a religious vocabulary built from Greek polys, many, and theos, god, and is related to polytheism. English uses -ist to identify an adherent of a belief, and the same form can also function as an adjective.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：poly-（多）+ the-（神）+ -ist（信奉者）→ polytheist；也可与 polytheism 对照，理解为 -ism（信仰体系）与 -ist（信奉者）的对应。核心词族包括 polytheists（复数）、polytheism（多神论）、polytheistic（多神论的）和 polytheistically（以多神论方式）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: poly-, many, + the-, god, + -ist, adherent, → polytheist; comparison with polytheism also shows the contrast between -ism for a belief system and -ist for an adherent. The core family includes polytheists, polytheism, polytheistic, and polytheistically.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: polytheistic believer（多神信仰者）是明确的释义性近义表达；pagan（异教徒；现代自然宗教信奉者）范围随语境变化，不一定信奉多个神；heathen（异教徒）常带历史性或贬义色彩，不宜作为中性的直接替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Polytheistic believer is a clear descriptive equivalent. Pagan varies by context and does not necessarily imply belief in several gods; heathen often carries historical or derogatory associations and is not a neutral direct substitute.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: poly- 多 + the- 神 + -ist 信奉者：相信“神不止一个”的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Poly- means many, the- means god, and -ist means believer: a believer in many gods.

meaning: 电位计；三端可调电阻器

morphology.text: potenti-（potential 电势的词干形式）+ -o-（连接元音）+ -meter（仪器）→ potentiometer（电位计）。

etymology.text: 19世纪末在英语中由 potential 的词干加 -meter 形成；potential 经拉丁语承接“能力、势”的概念，-meter 来自希腊语“测量”。名字原来强调电势测量，后来也用于三端可调电阻元件。

usage_note: 本课教电路中三端可调电阻元件这一用法；也能指传统的电势差测量仪器，具体看电路或仪器语境。

senses.meaning_zh: 电位差计；通过与已知电势差比较来测量电势差或电动势的仪器
senses.meaning_en: An instrument that measures potential difference or electromotive force by comparison with a known voltage.
senses.english_definition: A potentiometer is an instrument that measures an unknown voltage by balancing it against a known voltage.
senses.collocation_en: a DC potentiometer; a precision potentiometer
senses.collocation_zh: 直流电位差计；精密电位差计
senses.sentence_en: The laboratory used a potentiometer to compare the electromotive forces of two cells.
senses.sentence_zh: 实验室用电位差计比较了两个电池的电动势。

senses.meaning_zh: 电位器；带有可动触点、通常用作可调分压器的三端电阻元件
senses.meaning_en: A three-terminal resistor with a movable contact, typically used as an adjustable voltage divider.
senses.english_definition: A potentiometer is an electrical component whose movable contact lets you adjust the voltage taken from a resistive element.
senses.collocation_en: a rotary potentiometer; a linear potentiometer
senses.collocation_zh: 旋转式电位器；线性电位器
senses.sentence_en: A rotary potentiometer controls the volume of the amplifier.
senses.sentence_zh: 一个旋转式电位器控制着放大器的音量。

etymology_story.zh: potentiometer 是十九世纪形成的科技词，由 potential 的词干与表示“测量仪器”的 -meter 组合而成；potential 最终与拉丁语中表示“能力、力量”的词有关，-meter 则源自希腊语表示“尺度、测量”的词。名称最初强调电势测量，后来也用于电路中调节电压的三端电阻元件。
etymology_story.en: Potentiometer is a nineteenth-century technical formation combining a stem of potential with -meter, meaning a measuring instrument; potential ultimately derives from Latin vocabulary for power or ability, while -meter comes from Greek vocabulary for measure. The name originally emphasized voltage measurement and later also came to denote the three-terminal resistive component used to adjust voltage.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：potenti-（来自 potential，电势）+ -o-（连接元音）+ -meter（测量仪器）→ potentiometer。核心词族包括 potentiometers（复数）、potentiometry（电位测定法）、potentiometric（电位测定的）和 potentiometrically（用电位测定法）；pot 是电位器义的非正式简称。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: potenti-, from potential in its electrical sense, + linking -o- + -meter, measuring instrument, → potentiometer. The core family includes potentiometers, potentiometry, potentiometric, and potentiometrically; pot is an informal shortening for the component.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: variable resistor（可变电阻器）是较宽泛的类别名称；rheostat（变阻器）通常按两个端子接线，用来改变电阻并调节电流，而电位器通常按三个端子接线进行分压；voltmeter（电压表）与仪器义功能相关，但通常直接显示电压读数，不专指采用平衡比较法的电位差计。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Variable resistor is a broader category. A rheostat normally uses two terminals to vary resistance and control current, whereas a potentiometer normally uses three terminals as a voltage divider. A voltmeter is related to the instrument sense but normally displays voltage directly and does not specifically denote a balancing instrument.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: potential 电势 + meter 测量仪：先记“测电势”，再联想到用滑动触点“调电压”的电位器。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Potential plus meter gives measuring voltage; extend the idea to the movable contact that adjusts voltage in a circuit.

meaning: 闲职；领薪却几乎不用做事的职位
aliases: 闲职；领薪却几乎不用做事的职位
领薪却几乎不用做事的职位

pronunciation.note: 本卡选用英式读音；先听完整单词，再留意重读音节。

forms: 可数名词；复数 sinecures。
family: sinecurist 占据闲职的人；sinecures 是职位的复数。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；sinecure + -ist → sinecurist（占据闲职的人），去掉末尾 e 后接 -ist。
morphology.source: 作者教学分析，结合本批事实表及 https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/sinecure

etymology.text: 17世纪来自中古拉丁语短语 beneficium sine cura，指无须承担牧灵职责的教会俸禄；sine 是“没有”，cura 是“照管”。后来泛指拿薪水却没多少职责的职位。

usage_note: 通常带批评或讽刺意味，重点是职位有收入而职责很轻，不只是工作让人满意。

senses.meaning_zh: 闲职；工作或责任很少的有薪职位
senses.meaning_en: a paid position involving little work or responsibility
senses.english_definition: A sinecure is a paid position in which you have very little work to do or responsibility to take.
senses.collocation_en: a well-paid sinecure; a political sinecure
senses.collocation_zh: 薪酬优厚的闲职；政治性闲职
senses.sentence_en: He treated his appointment as a sinecure and rarely came to the office.
senses.sentence_zh: 他把这次任命当成一份闲差，很少来办公室。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 sine cura，意为“无须照管”，最初用于指不必承担牧灵职责的教会俸禄职位。英语在17世纪借入后，将其推广为工作或责任很少却能领取薪酬的职位。
etymology_story.en: It comes from Latin sine cura, meaning 'without care,' originally referring to an ecclesiastical benefice without responsibility for parishioners' spiritual care. Borrowed into English in the seventeenth century, it broadened to mean a paid position with few duties.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 sinecure 作为整体词基，不宜把历史上的拉丁语成分当作现代英语词缀。词族包括 sinecures（复数）和 sinecurist（占据闲职者，由 sinecure 去掉末尾 e 后加 -ist 构成）；另有罕见名词 sinecurism（闲职制度或占据闲职的做法）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, sinecure functions as a whole base rather than a productive combination of English affixes. Its family includes the plural sinecures and sinecurist, formed by dropping final e and adding -ist; the rare noun sinecurism refers to the system or practice of holding sinecures.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cushy job 指轻松舒适的工作，未必几乎没有职责；easy job 只强调工作容易；no-show job 指领薪却不必实际到岗的职位，比 sinecure 更明确地涉及不到岗。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A cushy job is comfortable and undemanding but may still involve real duties; an easy job simply requires little effort or skill; a no-show job specifically allows someone to collect pay without reporting for work.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史逻辑：sine（没有）＋cura（照管）→ 无须操心照管，却照样领薪。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Historical hook: sine 'without' + cura 'care' → pay without much to take care of.

meaning: 烧结（加热粉末使其结合而不完全熔化）
aliases: 烧结（加热粉末使其结合而不完全熔化）

pronunciation.note: 采用英式或英语借词常用读法；重音符号标在重读音节前。

morphology.text: sinter + -ing → sintering（烧结工艺）；sinter 作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 借自德语 Sinter，原指矿物沉积物或熔渣，进入英语后也用于粉末加热结合的工艺。

usage_note: 材料加工用语。sinter 强调颗粒结合，不等于把材料完全熔成液体。

senses.meaning_zh: 烧结；通过加热使粉末或颗粒结合，而不使整体完全熔化
senses.meaning_en: to bond powder or particles by heating without completely melting the material
senses.english_definition: If you sinter a powdered material, or if it sinters, its particles join together when heated without the whole material becoming liquid.
senses.collocation_en: sinter metal powders; sintered ceramics
senses.collocation_zh: 烧结金属粉末；烧结陶瓷
senses.sentence_en: The pressed powder is sintered in a furnace to produce a strong component.
senses.sentence_zh: 将压制成形的粉末放入炉中烧结，制成坚固的零件。

senses.meaning_zh: 烧结料；烧结块
senses.meaning_en: material formed by bonding particles through sintering
senses.english_definition: Sinter is a solid material made by heating small particles until they bond together without completely melting.
senses.collocation_en: iron ore sinter; sinter production
senses.collocation_zh: 铁矿石烧结矿；烧结料生产
senses.sentence_en: The plant produces iron ore sinter for use in blast furnaces.

senses.meaning_zh: 泉华；由泉水沉积形成的矿物沉积物
senses.meaning_en: a mineral deposit formed from spring water
senses.english_definition: Sinter is a mineral deposit that forms when substances dissolved in spring water come out of solution and build up on a surface.
senses.collocation_en: siliceous sinter; calcareous sinter
senses.collocation_zh: 硅华；钙华
senses.sentence_en: A pale crust of siliceous sinter surrounds the hot spring.
senses.sentence_zh: 温泉周围覆盖着一层浅色的硅华硬壳。

etymology_story.zh: 借自德语 Sinter，该词历史上指矿渣及某些矿物沉积物。英语先将其用于矿物材料，后来又发展出表示粉末颗粒受热结合的工业动词用法。
etymology_story.en: It was borrowed from German Sinter, historically used for slag and certain mineral deposits. In English, the mineral noun was later joined by an industrial verb describing the bonding of heated particles.

morphology_enriched.zh: sinter 是独立词基，名词和动词同形。常见词族包括 sinters（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、sintered（过去式、过去分词，也可作形容词，意为“烧结的”）、sintering（现在分词及工艺名词“烧结”）；相关构词包括 sinterability（可烧结性）、sinterable（可烧结的）和 sintering furnace（烧结炉）。
morphology_enriched.en: Sinter is an independent base used as both noun and verb. Common family forms include sinters, sintered, and sintering, which also names the process; related formations include sinterability, sinterable, and the compound sintering furnace.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 动词 agglomerate 强调颗粒聚成较大的团块，不限定加热；fuse 强调熔合，常涉及熔化；consolidate 强调使材料致密、牢固。sinter 特指通过加热使颗粒结合而不使整体完全熔化。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Agglomerate means to gather particles into larger masses without specifying heat; fuse emphasizes joining and often involves melting; consolidate emphasizes making material compact and firm. Sinter specifically involves heat-induced bonding without complete melting.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住工业义：颗粒受热“抱成团”；地质义另记为泉水留下的矿物壳。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For the industrial sense, picture heated grains bonding into a lump; for the geological sense, picture a mineral crust left by spring water.

senses.meaning_zh: 单线的；沿单一路径或单一发展序列推进的
senses.meaning_en: following a single line, path, or sequence of development

senses.sentence_en: The theory assumes a unilinear progression from simple societies to complex ones.

etymology_story.zh: 由表示“一、单一”的 uni- 与 linear（线性的）构成，两部分均有拉丁语来源，其中 linear 可追溯至 linea（线）。其“一条线”的字面概念被用于描述单一路径，尤其是社会或文化发展的单一序列。
etymology_story.en: It combines uni-, meaning 'one,' with linear, ultimately from Latin linea, 'line.' The literal idea of one line was extended to a single developmental path, particularly in accounts of social or cultural change.

morphology_enriched.zh: uni-（单一）＋linear（线性的）→ unilinear。linear 所属词族包括 line（线）、linearity（线性）和 linearly（线性地）；unilinear 的直接派生词包括 unilinearly（沿单一路径地）和 unilinearity（单线性）。相关对比词有 multilinear（多线的）和 nonlinear（非线性的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Uni- 'one' + linear gives unilinear. The underlying family includes line, linearity, and linearly; direct derivatives include unilinearly and unilinearity. Related contrasting formations include multilinear and nonlinear.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: linear 强调线状关系或顺序发展，未必突出只有一条路径；single-track 强调只沿一条轨道或思路推进，有时带批评意味；unidirectional 强调方向单一，未必表示遵循同一条发展序列。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Linear emphasizes a line-like relationship or sequential progression without necessarily stressing one exclusive path; single-track emphasizes one track or line of thought and can sound critical; unidirectional specifies one direction rather than one developmental sequence.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: uni-＝一，linear＝线性的：所有变化都沿“一条线”推进。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Uni- means 'one': imagine development moving along one single line.

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 bonne，原是 bon（好的）的阴性形式，后来名词化，用来称呼女佣。英语借入后主要用于育儿女佣，尤其是法国家庭女佣或法国籍保姆，如今带有明显的历史色彩。
etymology_story.en: It was borrowed from French bonne, the feminine form of bon, 'good,' which developed a noun use meaning a female domestic servant. English used it especially for a nursemaid, often a French one, and the word now has a distinctly historical flavor.

morphology_enriched.zh: 英语中的 bonne 作为整体借词使用，不拆作 bon＋英语后缀 -ne；复数为 bonnes。法语短语 bonne d’enfants 意为“育儿女佣”，其中 d’enfants 表示“照料孩子的”；该短语不是英语的派生构词，英语中也没有常用的进一步派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In English, bonne is a whole borrowed base, not bon plus an English suffix -ne; its plural is bonnes. The French phrase bonne d’enfants means 'children's nursemaid'; it is a borrowed phrase rather than an English derivative, and bonne has no common further English derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nanny 是现代英语中照料儿童的常用职业名称；nursemaid 也指育儿女佣，但更有旧式家仆色彩；maid 泛指女佣，不一定承担育儿工作。bonne 尤其带有法语背景和历史语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nanny is the usual modern occupational term for someone employed to care for children; nursemaid has a more historical domestic-service flavor; maid is broader and does not necessarily involve childcare. Bonne particularly suggests a French connection and an older setting.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把它放回旧式法国家庭：bonne 是照料孩子的女佣；其历史词源与法语“好的”有关。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a nursemaid in an old French household; historically, her title comes from the French word for 'good.'

etymology_story.zh: cel 是 celluloid（赛璐珞）的截短形式，名称来自早期动画所用的透明片材。后来即使片材改用其他塑料，这个名称仍保留下来，用来指传统动画中的透明绘图片。
etymology_story.en: Cel is a shortening of celluloid, named after the transparent material used in early animation. The name remained in use for animation sheets even when other plastics replaced celluloid.

morphology_enriched.zh: celluloid 截短并调整拼写为 cel；现代英语中 cel 是独立词基，复数为 cels。常见相关构词包括 cel animation（赛璐珞动画、透明片动画）、cel shading（卡通渲染）和 cel-shaded（采用卡通渲染的）；后两者指模仿传统动画色块与明暗效果的视觉风格。
morphology_enriched.en: Celluloid was clipped and respelled as cel, which now functions as an independent base; its plural is cels. Related formations include cel animation, cel shading, and cel-shaded; the latter two describe a visual style that imitates the flat colors and shading of traditional animation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: animation cel 是明确说明用途的同义表达；animation sheet 是较宽泛的描述，可能还包括其他动画用片材或纸张。相关词 frame 指影片中的一帧完整画面，一帧可以由多张 cel 叠合而成。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Animation cel is an explicit equivalent; animation sheet is a broader description that may include other sheets used in animation. The related word frame means a complete film image, which may combine several cels.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: celluloid 缩成 cel：记住那张叠在背景上的透明动画片。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Shorten celluloid to cel, and picture a transparent drawing laid over a background.

etymology_story.zh: charnel 经古法语进入中古英语，其源头是中世纪拉丁语 carnale，指存放尸骨的地方，与拉丁语 carnalis（肉身的）和 caro（肉）有关。它由与肉身有关的词发展为藏骨场所的名称，并产生了与尸体、死亡有关的形容词用法。
etymology_story.en: Charnel entered Middle English through Old French and ultimately derives from Medieval Latin carnale, a place for human remains, related to Latin carnalis, meaning 'of the flesh,' and caro, meaning 'flesh.' It became a name for a repository of bones and also developed an adjective use associated with bodies and death.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 charnel 作为不可再作能产拆分的完整借词，不拆为 char + -nel。主要相关形式：名词复数 charnels；复合词 charnel house 或 charnel-house（藏骨堂），复数 charnel houses；无常用的独立派生动词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, charnel is normally treated as a whole borrowed base, not as char + -nel. Principal related forms are the noun plural charnels and the compound charnel house or charnel-house, plural charnel houses; there is no commonly used derived verb or adverb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ossuary（藏骨所）更明确指集中存放遗骨的容器或场所；mortuary（停尸房）通常暂存尚待安葬或检验的尸体；sepulchral（坟墓般阴森的）主要描述墓葬般的气氛、声音或外观。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: An ossuary specifically holds collected bones; a mortuary usually keeps bodies temporarily before burial or examination; sepulchral describes a tomb-like atmosphere, sound, or appearance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 同源线索：carn- 表示“肉身”——肉身消逝，遗骨留在 charnel。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the historical carn- connection with flesh: the flesh disappears, but the bones remain in a charnel.

senses.meaning_zh: 易怒的；暴躁的；动辄发火的
senses.meaning_en: Easily angered and inclined to express anger.
senses.english_definition: Someone who is choleric becomes angry easily and often shows their anger.
senses.collocation_en: a choleric temperament; a choleric outburst
senses.collocation_zh: 暴躁的性情；一次怒气冲冲的发作

senses.sentence_zh: 他暴躁的性情使得即使是小小的分歧也难以化解。

etymology_story.zh: choleric 经法语和拉丁语追溯至希腊语，与 cholē（胆汁）有关。古代体液学说认为黄胆汁过多会使人易怒，因此表示胆汁性质的词逐渐获得了“暴躁的”这一性格含义。
etymology_story.en: Choleric traces through French and Latin to Greek and is related to cholē, meaning 'bile.' Ancient humoral theory associated excess yellow bile with an angry temperament, giving the word its enduring sense of being easily angered.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词可分析为 choler（怒气；旧指胆汁）+ -ic（具有……性质的）→ choleric。主要词族：choler、choleric、cholerically（暴躁地）；choler 本身在现代英语中较古旧。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern formation can be understood as choler, meaning 'anger' or historically 'bile,' + -ic, meaning 'characterized by,' producing choleric. The principal family consists of choler, choleric, and cholerically; choler itself is now old-fashioned.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: irascible（易怒的）同样强调容易被激怒，语体较正式；irritable（烦躁易怒的）也可指疲劳、压力造成的暂时状态；hot-tempered（脾气火暴的）较日常，突出发火迅速。choleric 较具文学色彩，常描写一贯暴躁的性情。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Irascible is similarly formal and emphasizes readiness to become angry; irritable can describe a temporary state caused by fatigue or stress; hot-tempered is more everyday and emphasizes quick anger. Choleric is relatively literary and often describes a habitually angry disposition.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 古人的逻辑：“胆汁多，火气大”——choler + -ic → 易怒的。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the old belief: more bile, more anger—choler + -ic gives choleric.

etymology_story.zh: distaff 源自古英语 distæf，由表示一束待纺纤维的 dis 和 stæf（杆）组成。由于纺纱在传统社会中常由女性承担，纺纱杆后来成为女性的象征，并引申出“女系的、母系的”等用法。
etymology_story.en: Distaff comes from Old English distæf, combining dis, a bunch of fibers ready for spinning, with stæf, meaning 'staff' or 'rod.' Because spinning was traditionally associated with women, the implement became a symbol of women and acquired uses referring to female descent.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常将 distaff 作为完整词干；历史结构是 dis（纤维束，已不再能产）+ staff（杆），其中 dis 不是现代否定或逆转前缀 dis-。主要相关形式：distaffs（复数）、distaff side（母系一方）、distaff line（女系血统）；形容词由名词转类而来。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats distaff as a whole base; historically it consists of dis, a now-unproductive element meaning a bunch of fibers, + staff. This dis is not the modern negative or reversative prefix dis-. Principal related forms are distaffs, distaff side, and distaff line; the adjective developed by conversion from the noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: spindle（纺锤）是捻线和卷线的工具，distaff 则承托尚未纺成线的纤维，两者并非同一器具；maternal（母系的）明确涉及母亲一方；female（女性的）范围更广，不必涉及血统。distaff 用于女性或女系时带有传统、古旧色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A spindle twists or winds thread, whereas a distaff holds the unspun fibers, so the tools are not interchangeable. Maternal specifically concerns the mother's side; female is broader and need not concern ancestry. Distaff carries a traditional or dated tone when applied to women or female descent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先记 staff“杆”：纤维绕杆待纺；再由传统纺纱者联想到女系。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with staff: fibers wait on a rod; the traditional association with women leads to the female line.

senses.meaning_en: To cause suspended particles to gather into loose clumps, or to gather into such clumps.
senses.english_definition: When particles flocculate, or something flocculates them, they gather together into loose clumps that can often be separated from a liquid.
senses.collocation_en: flocculate suspended particles; flocculate and settle

etymology_story.zh: flocculate 是以拉丁语 flocculus（小绒团）为基础形成的科学用词，而 flocculus 是 floccus（绒毛束）的指小形式。悬浮颗粒聚成松软、絮状团块的外观，使这一词源形象成为其现代技术含义。
etymology_story.en: Flocculate is a scientific formation based on Latin flocculus, meaning 'a small tuft,' a diminutive of floccus, meaning 'a tuft of wool.' Its technical meaning reflects the soft, tuft-like appearance of the clumps formed when suspended particles gather together.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：floccul-（絮团）+ -ate（动词后缀）→ flocculate。主要词族：floc、floccule（絮团），flocculent（絮状的），flocculated、flocculating，flocculation（絮凝），flocculant（絮凝剂），flocculator（絮凝设备）；加 de- 构成 deflocculate（使解絮）、deflocculation（解絮）、deflocculant（解絮剂）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: floccul-, meaning 'floc or small tuft,' + the verbal suffix -ate → flocculate. Principal family members include floc and floccule, flocculent, flocculated, flocculating, flocculation, flocculant, and flocculator; de- forms include deflocculate, deflocculation, and deflocculant.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: aggregate（聚集）泛指颗粒或单位聚成整体；coagulate（凝结）常强调胶体失稳或液体凝固，在水处理中可指促进随后絮凝的前一步；precipitate（沉淀析出）强调溶解物形成不溶固体。flocculate 专指形成较松散的絮团，不必产生新的化学物质。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Aggregate broadly means to gather into a larger whole; coagulate often concerns colloidal destabilization or the setting of a liquid and can precede flocculation in water treatment; precipitate concerns dissolved material forming an insoluble solid. Flocculate specifically emphasizes relatively loose flocs and need not involve forming a new chemical substance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: floccul-＝小绒团；颗粒抱成“小棉絮”，就是絮凝。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Floccul- suggests a little tuft: particles gather into tiny wool-like clumps.

etymology_story.zh: gie 是苏格兰语中与标准英语 give 对应的传统形式，承接北部中古英语中不带 v 音的形式。它属于日耳曼语“给予”这一词族，与古英语 giefan 和古诺尔斯语 gefa 有历史联系，并非随意省写的现代拼法。
etymology_story.en: Gie is a traditional Scots counterpart of standard English give, continuing northern Middle English forms without the v sound. It belongs to the Germanic 'give' family, historically connected with Old English giefan and Old Norse gefa, rather than being an arbitrary modern abbreviation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代苏格兰语中 gie 是简单动词词干，不作前后缀拆分。常见相关形式包括 gies（第三人称单数）、gied（过去式的一种形式）、gien（过去分词的一种形式）、giein 或 gieing（现在分词）；屈折和拼写随方言而异。相关词 forgie（原谅）在结构上对应标准英语 forgive。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern Scots, gie is a simple verb base without a productive prefix–suffix division. Related forms include gies, gied as a past-tense form, gien as a past participle, and giein or gieing as present participles; inflection and spelling vary by dialect. The related verb forgie corresponds structurally to standard English forgive.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: give（给）是最直接的标准英语对应词；hand（递给）强调用手把东西交过去；bestow（授予、赐予）语体正式，常用于荣誉或恩惠。gie 的基本意义与 give 相同，主要区别在语言变体和地域身份。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Give is the direct standard English equivalent; hand emphasizes physically passing something to someone; bestow is formal and often concerns honors or favors. Gie generally differs from give in language variety and regional identity rather than basic meaning.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 对照 give：听见没有 /v/ 的 /ɡiː/，就想到苏格兰语里的“给”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with give: /ɡiː/ without the /v/ points to the Scots word for 'give.'

etymology_story.zh: 该词与法语 humoral 和中世纪拉丁语 humoralis 有关，最终源于拉丁语 humor，意为“液体、湿气”。它先用于传统体液学说，后来也用于现代生理学和免疫学，表示与体液或其中的物质有关。
etymology_story.en: The word is connected with French humoral and Medieval Latin humoralis, ultimately from Latin humor, meaning liquid or moisture. Originally associated with traditional theories of bodily humours, it later acquired modern physiological and immunological uses.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 humor（体液，历史医学义）+ -al（与……有关的）→ humoral。相关词族包括 humor／humour（体液）、humoral（体液的）、humorally（通过体液地）、humoralism（体液学说）和 humoralist（体液学说支持者）；这里的 humor 不取“幽默”义。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: humor, in its historical medical sense of bodily fluid, + -al, meaning relating to, → humoral. The relevant family includes humor/humour, humoral, humorally, humoralism, and humoralist; humor here does not mean amusement.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: body-fluid-related（与体液有关的）是通俗释义；fluid-mediated（由液体介导的）强调作用途径，但不限定为人体体液；antibody-mediated（抗体介导的）适合免疫学语境，范围比 humoral 的一般生理学含义更窄。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Body-fluid-related is a plain-language equivalent; fluid-mediated emphasizes the mechanism but need not concern bodily fluids; antibody-mediated is a close equivalent in immunology but is narrower than the general physiological meaning of humoral.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: humor 在这里是“体液”：把抗体想成随体液流动的防御力量。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Read humor as bodily fluid: picture antibodies providing protection through the body's fluids.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古英语延续自古英语 nihtscada，其组成成分分别对应“夜”和“阴影”。这个古老植物名称的具体命名缘由并不完全明确，不能仅凭字面推断植物的生长习性或毒性。
etymology_story.en: The word continues Old English nihtscada through Middle English, with elements corresponding to night and shade. The precise reason for the original name is uncertain, so its literal components do not reliably indicate a plant's habitat or toxicity.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词为 night（夜）+ shade（阴影）→ nightshade，是复合名词；复数为 nightshades。常见复合名称有 deadly nightshade（颠茄）、black nightshade（龙葵）和 woody nightshade（欧白英）；没有常用的加词缀派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: night + shade → nightshade, a compound noun; the plural is nightshades. Established compound names include deadly nightshade, black nightshade, and woody nightshade; there is no common family of affix-derived forms.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: solanaceous plant（茄科植物）是广义语境中的近义表达；Solanum（茄属）范围较窄，不包括所有被称为 nightshade 的植物；belladonna（颠茄）仅指特定植物，不能替代泛称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Solanaceous plant is a close equivalent in the broad family-level sense; Solanum names a narrower genus and excludes some plants called nightshades; belladonna identifies one particular plant rather than the whole group.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: night + shade：“夜色阴影”帮助记住茄类植物这个名称，不代表都有毒。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Night + shade gives a memorable shadowy image for the plant name, without implying that every nightshade is poisonous.

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代生物学术语，其希腊语来源的成分包括 pro-（在……之前）和 karyon（坚果、核）。名称体现了早期对细胞结构层次的理解，但现代定义的关键是没有膜包细胞核，并非没有遗传物质。
etymology_story.en: This modern biological term uses Greek-derived elements including pro-, meaning before, and karyon, meaning nut or kernel. Its name reflects an early view of cellular organization, while its defining modern feature is the absence of a membrane-bound nucleus, not the absence of genetic material.

morphology_enriched.zh: 学习性拆分为 pro-（在前）+ kary(o)-（核）+ -ote（该组生物名称中的结尾）；不宜把 -ote 当作可自由套用的普通英语后缀。词族包括 prokaryote（原核生物）、prokaryotes（复数）、prokaryotic（原核的）以及较少见拼写 procaryote、procaryotic；对应的对照词为 eukaryote（真核生物）和 eukaryotic（真核的）。
morphology_enriched.en: A useful learned breakdown is pro- meaning before + kary(o)- meaning nucleus + the ending -ote used in this group of organism names; -ote is not a freely productive everyday English suffix. The family includes prokaryote, plural prokaryotes, prokaryotic, and the less common spellings procaryote and procaryotic; the contrasting terms are eukaryote and eukaryotic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: prokaryotic organism（原核生物）是直接同义表达；bacterium（细菌）仅指其中一类；archaeon（古菌）指另一类，后两者都不能单独覆盖 prokaryote 的全部范围。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Prokaryotic organism is a direct equivalent; bacterium identifies one major group of prokaryotes, while archaeon identifies the other. Neither bacterium nor archaeon alone covers the full meaning of prokaryote.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pro- 在前，kary- 核：记成“尚无膜包核”，别记成“没有 DNA”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pro- means before and kary- points to the nucleus: remember no membrane-bound nucleus, while DNA is still present.

etymology_story.zh: 该币名经波斯语和阿拉伯语中的相关形式传播，最终源自西班牙语 real，原意为“王室的”，也用作旧币名称。这个源于王室钱币的名称后来被不同国家用于各自的货币。
etymology_story.en: The currency name spread through related Persian and Arabic forms and ultimately comes from Spanish real, meaning royal and also naming a historical coin. A name associated with royal coinage was subsequently adopted for distinct national currencies.

morphology_enriched.zh: rial 在现代英语中作为不可进一步拆分的借入词处理，复数为 rials；没有常用的加词缀派生词。相关复合表达包括 rial-denominated（以里亚尔计价的）；riyal 是相关币名拼写，具体采用哪种拼写取决于所指货币的惯例。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, rial is an unanalyzed loanword, with the plural rials and no common affix-derived forms. A related compound is rial-denominated; riyal is a related currency-name spelling whose use depends on the naming convention for the particular currency.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 该词没有适用于所有语境的通用同义词：riyal 是用于某些相关货币名称的拼写，不能随意替换；currency unit（货币单位）是上位概念；real（雷亚尔或历史上的里亚尔币）虽与其同源，却可指不同货币。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no universal substitute: riyal is used for certain related currency names and is not freely interchangeable; currency unit is a broader category; real is historically related but can name a different currency.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 real 的“王室钱币”联想到 rial：旧币名跨语言流传。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect rial with the old Spanish real: a royal coin name that travelled across languages.

etymology.text: 由意大利语短语 sotto voce 缩短而来，字面与“在声音之下”有关，英语用它表示压低声音。

etymology_story.zh: 英语 sotto 是意大利语短语 sotto voce 的省略形式，其中 sotto 意为“在……下面”，voce 意为“声音”。该短语经音乐用语进入英语，用来表示压低声音或以轻柔含蓄的方式表达。
etymology_story.en: English sotto is a shortening of Italian sotto voce, in which sotto means under and voce means voice. The expression entered English through musical usage and denotes a lowered or subdued voice or delivery.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中应把 sotto 视为借入短语 sotto voce 的截短形式，不拆成英语词根和词缀。相关完整形式为 sotto voce；无常用的英语屈折或加词缀派生词族，单独使用 sotto 的范围比完整短语更窄。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, sotto is a clipping of the borrowed expression sotto voce, rather than an English root-plus-affix formation. Its related full form is sotto voce; it has no common English inflections or affix-derived family, and its standalone use is more restricted than that of the full phrase.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sotto voce（低声地；低声的）是更完整、使用范围更广的对应表达；softly（轻声地；轻柔地）只强调声音柔和或音量低；in an undertone（压低声音地）通常用于说话，常带不愿让旁人听清的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sotto voce is the fuller and more widely usable equivalent; softly simply emphasizes low volume or gentleness; in an undertone usually describes speech and often suggests keeping it from being clearly heard by others.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sotto 是“在下面”：把声音往下压，便是低声轻说。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sotto means under: picture lowering the voice beneath its usual level.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古英语传自古英语 swōgan，原有“呼啸、作响、带着声响移动”等义；名词由动词发展而来，后来主要用于文学作品中的风声描写。[词源资料](https://www.etymonline.com/word/sough)
etymology_story.en: The word descends through Middle English from Old English swōgan, meaning to roar, rustle, or move noisily; the noun developed from the verb, and the word later became chiefly literary. [Etymological source](https://www.etymonline.com/word/sough)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 sough 是不可进一步拆分的词基，可兼作动词和名词。屈折形式：soughs（第三人称单数或名词复数）、soughed（过去式及过去分词）、soughing（现在分词，也可作动名词）；没有常用的独立派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, sough is an unanalyzed base used as both a verb and a noun. Its inflected forms are soughs, soughed, and soughing; soughing can also function as a verbal noun, and there is no substantial commonly used derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: rustle（沙沙作响）偏指树叶、纸张等轻微摩擦的声音；murmur（低声作响）强调轻柔而连续；sigh（叹息般作响）强调气流声。sough 特别适合描写风穿过树木时低沉、绵延的声响，文学色彩较强。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rustle suggests light friction, murmur emphasizes a quiet continuous sound, and sigh suggests an airy exhalation. Sough is especially evocative of low, sustained wind noise among trees and has a distinctly literary tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 风穿树梢，低声长叹：动作是 sough，声音也是 sough。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hear the wind give the trees a long, low sigh: sough names both the action and its sound.

senses.meaning_zh: 使拮据；使资源不足而陷入困境〔正式用语，常见于过去分词形式〕
senses.meaning_en: To cause hardship by restricting someone's money or resources; formal, especially in participial forms.
senses.english_definition: If circumstances straiten someone, they leave that person with too little money or too few resources to live or act comfortably.
senses.collocation_en: in straitened circumstances; financially straitened
senses.collocation_zh: 处于经济拮据的境况；经济上捉襟见肘

senses.sentence_zh: 生意失败后，这家人在经济上陷入了困境。

etymology_story.zh: 该词由旧形容词 strait（狭窄的、受限制的）加使动后缀 -en 构成；strait 经古法语追溯至拉丁语 strictus，意为“被拉紧的”。“使变窄”后来引申为压缩生活余地、使人经济拮据。[词源资料](https://www.etymonline.com/word/straiten)
etymology_story.en: Straiten combines the older adjective strait, meaning narrow or restricted, with causative -en; strait comes through Old French from Latin strictus, meaning drawn tight. Physical narrowing developed figuratively into pressure from financial hardship. [Etymological source](https://www.etymonline.com/word/straiten)

morphology_enriched.zh: strait（狭窄的、受限制的）+ -en（使成为）→ straiten。屈折形式：straitens、straitened、straitening；straitened 还可作形容词，意为“拮据的”。相关词族包括 strait（海峡；复数 straits 也指困境）、straitness（狭窄或困窘，少用）、straitly（严格地，旧用）、straitjacket（约束衣；束缚）及 strait-laced（拘谨守旧的）；straighten（弄直）属于另一个词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Strait + causative -en → straiten. Inflections are straitens, straitened, and straitening; straitened also functions as an adjective meaning financially constrained. Related formations include strait, straits, the uncommon straitness, the dated straitly, straitjacket, and strait-laced. Straighten, meaning make straight, belongs to a different family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: impoverish（使贫困）强调财富或资源明显减少；constrain（限制）适用范围更广；cramp（束缚）强调限制行动或发展空间。straiten 尤其强调因财力或资源不足而捉襟见肘。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Impoverish emphasizes loss of wealth or resources; constrain broadly means limit; cramp suggests restricting freedom or room for action. Straiten particularly evokes hardship caused by insufficient means.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: strait 是“窄”，-en 是“使”：把生活余地挤窄，就会拮据。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Strait means narrow; -en means make: narrow someone's financial room, and you straiten them.

etymology_story.zh: 动画及漫画义是 cartoon 的截短形式，后来也用于卡通人物，并在游戏用语中扩展为玩家角色。植物义则独立借自印地语、乌尔都语 tūn，最终来自梵语 tunna，与 cartoon 无关。[词源资料](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/toon)
etymology_story.en: The cartoon sense is a clipping of cartoon, subsequently applied to animated characters and, in gaming slang, player characters. The unrelated tree name comes from Hindi and Urdu tūn, ultimately from Sanskrit tunna. [Etymological source](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/toon)

morphology_enriched.zh: cartoon → toon，属于截短构词；复数为 toons。toon + -y → toony（卡通风格的，非正式）；相关构词有 webtoon（网络条漫）。原词 cartoon 的词族包括 cartoons（漫画；动画片）、cartoonist（漫画家）、cartooning（漫画创作）、cartoonish（卡通般的）和 cartoonishly（以卡通般的方式）；植物义 toon 是独立借词。
morphology_enriched.en: Cartoon → toon is clipping; the plural is toons. Toon + -y produces informal toony, meaning cartoonlike; webtoon is a related formation. The source-word family includes cartoons, cartoonist, cartooning, cartoonish, and cartoonishly. Botanical toon is a separate borrowed base.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cartoon（漫画；动画片）是较中性的完整形式；animated character（动画角色）明确指角色本身；avatar（虚拟化身）强调用户在数字环境中的代表形象。toon 更口语化，在游戏中通常直接指玩家角色；这些近义表达均不适用于植物义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cartoon is the fuller, more neutral term; animated character explicitly names the character; avatar emphasizes a user's digital representation. Toon is more informal and commonly means a player's character in gaming; these alternatives do not cover the tree sense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 cartoon 前半截剪掉，留下 toon：动画、卡通人物，再到游戏角色；树名另作独立词记。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Clip cartoon to toon: cartoon, cartoon character, then game character. Learn the unrelated tree name separately.

morphology.text: zona 是拉丁语借词，作为独立词素记忆，指带状或环状结构；同源词 zone 的派生式：zone + -al → zonal（区域的、带状的）。

etymology.text: 直接借自拉丁语 zona（腰带、带），与希腊语 zone（腰带）相关；用一圈腰带记住包围着组织的带状结构。

usage_note: 解剖学中的拉丁语借词，常同限定词连用，如 zona pellucida；本卡不教疾病义。

senses.meaning_zh: 带状区域；环带状结构〔解剖学用语〕
senses.meaning_en: A beltlike region or encircling structure in the body; anatomical.
senses.english_definition: A zona is a region or structure in the body that forms a band or surrounds something.
senses.collocation_en: zona pellucida; zona fasciculata
senses.collocation_zh: 透明带；（肾上腺皮质的）束状带

senses.sentence_zh: 透明带在哺乳动物卵细胞周围形成一层保护结构。

etymology_story.zh: zona 借自拉丁语 zona（腰带、带），最终来自希腊语 zōnē（腰带）。解剖学沿用“带”的空间形象，指身体中的带状区域或环绕结构；这一专门义见于 [Collins 词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/zona)。
etymology_story.en: Zona is borrowed from Latin zona, meaning belt or girdle, ultimately from Greek zōnē. Anatomy preserves the belt image in a bandlike region or encircling structure, as described in [Collins Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/zona).

morphology_enriched.zh: zona 是整体借入的词，不宜按现代英语拆成 zon + -a；学术复数为 zonae。相关同源词族包括 zone（区域）、zonal（区域的；带状的）、zonally（按区域地）、zonation（分带；带状分布）和 zonate（具环带的）；zonule／zonula（小带）及 zonular（小带的）也来自同一词源，其中 zone 的派生词并非直接由 zona 构成。
morphology_enriched.en: Zona is borrowed as a whole and should not be analyzed as modern English zon + -a; its learned plural is zonae. Related forms include zone, zonal, zonally, zonation, and zonate, as well as zonule or zonula and zonular. Derivatives of zone share the historical base but are not direct derivatives of zona.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: zone（区域、带）适用范围最广；band（带状部分）强调狭长形态；layer（层）强调组织的层次。zona 是解剖学命名用词，不能在固定术语中随意用这些普通词替换。[释义参考](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/zona)
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Zone broadly denotes a region, band emphasizes a striplike shape, and layer emphasizes tissue arranged in a sheet or level. Zona is an anatomical naming term, so these ordinary alternatives cannot freely replace it in established names. [Definition reference](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/zona)

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一条腰带圈住组织：zona 就是身体里的“带”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a belt around tissue: a zona is an anatomical band.
